body.translated_text: <s>Bhaiṣajyavastu</s> (Chapter on Medicine)

children.translated_text: In the <s>Bhaiṣajyavastu</s>:
Summary verse (<s>piṇḍoddāna</s>):
Medicine, <s>Mahāsena</s>, <s>Rājagṛha</s>, the <s>Veṇuvana</s> grove,
<s>Icchānaṅgalā</s> and <s>Kampilla</s>, the first kingdom, <s>Kumāravardhana</s>,

children.text: glānakāś ca kaineyo vargo bhavati samudyataḥ //
children.translated_text: the sick ones and <s>Kaineya</s> — this section is set forth. //

body.translated_text: Synopsis (<s>uddāna</s>):

children.text: bhaiṣajyam anujñātaṃ vasā kacchuś ca añjanam* /
children.translated_text: Medicine permitted, fat, skin-disease, and eye-ointment,

children.text: unmattakaḥ pilindaś ca revataḥ sauvīrakeṇa ca //
children.translated_text: <s>Unmattaka</s>, <s>Pilinda</s>, <s>Revata</s>, and with <s>Sauvīraka</s> [vinegar]. //

body.text: buddho bhagavān śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍadasyārāme / tena khalu samayena bhikṣavaḥ śāradakena rogeṇa bādhyante / te śāradakena rogeṇa bādhyamānā utpāṇḍūtpāṇḍukā bhavanti kṛṣālukā durbalakā mlānā aprāptakāyāḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s> in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. At that time, the monks were afflicted by autumnal illness. Being afflicted by the autumnal illness, they became very pale, emaciated, weak, withered, and their bodies did not flourish.

children.translated_text: Knowing, they ask; not knowing, they do not ask.

children.text: } yāvat pṛcchati buddho bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam* / kasmād ānanda etarhi bhikṣavaḥ utpāṇḍūtpāṇḍukāḥ kṛṣālukā durbalakā mlānā aprāptakāyā iti / (
children.translated_text: } The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, asked the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Why, <s>Ānanda</s>, are the monks now very pale, emaciated, weak, withered, and their bodies not flourishing?'
(MSV I ii)

children.text: ) āyuṣmān ānandaḥ kathayati / etarhi bhadanta bhikṣavaḥ śāradakena rogeṇa bādhyante / etarhi śāradakena rogeṇa bādhyamānā utpāṇḍūtpāṇḍukā bhavanti kṛṣālukā durbalakā mlānā aprāptakāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: The Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'At present, Venerable Sir, the monks are afflicted by autumnal illness. Being afflicted by the autumnal illness, they have become very pale, emaciated, weak, withered, and their bodies do not flourish.'
The Blessed One said:

children.text: / tasmād ānanda anujānāmi bhikṣubhir bhaiṣajyaṃ sevitavyam iti /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, I permit monks to use medicine.'

body.translated_text: The <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, are knowers and askers. {Manuscript adds:

children.text: uktaṃ bhagavatā bhikṣubhir bhaiṣajyaṃ pratisevitavyam iti
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said that monks should use medicine.

children.text: / bhikṣavaḥ kāle sevanti kālātikrāntaṃ na sevanti / te bhavanti utpāṇḍūtpāṇḍukāḥ kṛṣālukā durbalakā mlānā aprāptakāyāḥ / jānakāḥ pṛcchakā buddhā bhagavantaḥ / pṛcchati buddho bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam* / uktaṃ mayā bhikṣubhir bhaiṣajyaṃ sevitavyam iti / atha ca punar bhikṣavaḥ utpāṇḍūtpāṇḍukāḥ kṛṣālukā durbalakā mlānā aprāptakāyāḥ / uktaṃ bhadanta bhagavatā bhikṣubhir bhaiṣajyaṃ pratisevitavyam iti / ta ete kālabhojino vayam iti kāle sevante kālātikrāntaṃ na sevante / tenotpāṇḍūtpāṇḍukāḥ kṛṣālukā durbalakā mlānā aprāptakāyāḥ / tasmāt tarhy ānanda anujānāmi bhikṣubhiś caturvidhāni bhaiṣajyāni pratisevitavyāni / kālikāni yāmikāni sāptāhikāni yāvajjīvikāni / tatra kālikāni maṇḍaḥ odanaṃ kulmāṣo māṃsam apūpāś ca / yāmikam aṣṭau pānāni / cocapānaṃ mocapānaṃ kolapānam (
children.translated_text: The monks used it during the [permitted] time but did not use it past the time. They remained very pale, emaciated, weak, withered, and their bodies did not flourish. The <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, are knowers and askers. The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, asked the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'I said that monks should use medicine. Yet the monks are still very pale, emaciated, weak, withered, and their bodies do not flourish.' 'Venerable Sir, the Blessed One said that monks should use medicine. But these, thinking "We are those who eat only at the proper time," use it during the time and do not use it past the time. Therefore they are very pale, emaciated, weak, withered, and their bodies do not flourish.' 'Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, I permit monks to use medicines of four kinds: timely (<s>kālika</s>), watch-period (<s>yāmika</s>), seven-day (<s>sāptāhika</s>), and lifelong (<s>yāvajjīvika</s>). Among these, the timely medicines are: gruel, cooked rice, barley-meal, meat, and cakes. The watch-period medicine consists of eight drinks: banana drink, plantain drink, jujube drink,
<s>aśvattha</s> (fig) drink, <s>udumbara</s> drink, <s>pāruṣika</s> (rough-skinned fruit) drink,
{Manuscript: parūṣaka-}
grape drink, and date drink.

children.translated_text: Banana, plantain, and jujube, and with <s>aśvattha</s> and <s>udumbara</s>,

children.translated_text: <s>pāruṣika</s> and grape, and date is considered the eighth. //

children.translated_text: flower-medicines, fruit-medicines, five resins, five alkalis, five salts, and five astringents.

body.translated_text: The seven-day medicines are: ghee, oil, molasses, honey, and sugar. The lifelong medicines are: root-medicines, stem-medicines,

flower-

The fruit-medicines are: <s>harītakī</s> (chebulic myrobalan), <s>āmalaka</s> (Indian gooseberry), <s>vibhītaka</s> (beleric myrobalan), <s>marica</s> (black pepper), and <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper). And whatever else also serves the purpose of fruit-medicine but not for the purpose of food. The five resins are: <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), <s>sarjarasa</s> (sal resin), <s>taka</s> (lac),

(MSV I iv)

children.translated_text: <s>Sarjarasa</s> is the exudation of the <s>sāla</s> tree. <s>Taka</s> is lac. <s>Takakarṇī</s> is beeswax. <s>Tadāgata</s> (the rest) is the exudation of other trees. What are the five alkalis? Barley alkali, barley-husk alkali, <s>sarjikā</s> (natron) alkali, sesame alkali, and <s>vāsaka</s> (adhatoda) alkali. What are the five salts? Rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>), black salt (<s>viḍa</s>), <s>sauvarcala</s> salt, <s>romaka</s> salt, and sea salt (<s>sāmudraka</s>). What are the five astringents? Mango astringent, neem astringent, rose-apple (<s>jambū</s>) astringent,
<s>śirīṣa</s> (silk tree) astringent,
and <s>kośamba</s> astringent.

body.translated_text: Among these, the root-medicines are: <s>mustā</s> (nut-grass), <s>vacā</s> (calamus), <s>haridrā</s> (turmeric), fresh ginger (<s>ārdraka</s>), and <s>ativiṣā</s> (monkshood). And whatever else also serves the purpose of root-medicine but not for the purpose of food. The stem-medicines are: sandalwood (<s>candana</s>), <s>cavikā</s> (long pepper), <s>padmaka</s> (wild cherry), <s>devadāru</s> (deodar cedar), <s>guḍūcī</s> (giloy), and <s>dāruharidrā</s> (barberry). And whatever else also serves the purpose of stem-medicine but not for the purpose of food. The leaf-medicines are: <s>paṭola</s> (snake gourd) leaf, <s>vāśika</s> (adhatoda) leaf, <s>nimba</s> (neem) leaf, <s>kośātakī</s> (luffa) leaf, and <s>saptaparṇa</s> (devil tree) leaf. And whatever else also serves the purpose of leaf-medicine but not for the purpose of food. The flower-medicines are five flowers: <s>vāśika</s> flower, <s>nimba</s> (neem) flower, <s>dhātukī</s> (woodfordia) flower, <s>śaṭī</s> (zedoary) flower,

children.text: ) samanvāharāyuṣman* / aham evaṃnāmā idaṃ bhaiṣajyaṃ yāvajjīvikam adhiti
children.translated_text: 'May the Venerable attend to this: I, named so-and-so, formally designate this medicine
as lifelong. For the benefit of those

children.text: ya sabrahmacāriṇāṃ ca evaṃ dvir api trir api / yathā yāvajjīvikam adhiṣṭhitam evaṃ yāmikaṃ sāptāhikaṃ vādhiṣṭheyam* /
children.translated_text: and of my co-practitioners in the holy life.' Thus twice, thrice also. As the lifelong medicine is formally designated, so should the watch-period and seven-day medicines be designated.

body.translated_text: Among these: if a timely medicine, a watch-period medicine, a seven-day medicine, or a lifelong medicine is mixed with a timely medicine, it should be consumed during the [permitted] time and not consumed past the time. If a watch-period medicine, a seven-day medicine, or a lifelong medicine is mixed with a watch-period medicine, it should be consumed within the watch-period and not consumed past the watch-period. If a seven-day medicine or a lifelong medicine is mixed with a seven-day medicine, it should be consumed within seven days and not consumed past seven days. A lifelong medicine should be formally designated and then consumed. And it should be formally designated thus: having washed the hands, having it received, standing before the monks, one should say:

body.text: śrāvastyāṃ nidānam* / athānyatamasya bhikṣor vāyvābādhikaṃ glānyam utpannam* / sa vaidyasakāśam upasaṃkrāntaḥ /

children.translated_text: Having approached, he said: 'An illness caused by wind

children.text: ) glānyam utpannaṃ bhaiṣajyaṃ vyapadiśeti / sa kathayati / ārya vasāṃ sevasva svāsthyaṃ te bhaviṣyatīti / bhikṣur āha / bhadramukha kim ahaṃ puruṣādaḥ / sa kathayati / bhikṣo / idaṃ te bhaiṣajyaṃ na śakyam anyathā svasthena bhavitum iti / etat prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣavo bhagavata ārocayanti / bhagavān āha / yadi vaidyaḥ kathayati / idaṃ te bhikṣor bhaiṣajyaṃ na śakyam anyathā svasthena bhavitum iti sevitavyā vaseti / bhikṣavo na jānate / tair vaidyaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ / sa kathayati / ārya yuṣmākam eva śāstā sarvajñas tam eva gatvā pṛccheti / etat prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣavo bhagavata ārocayanti / bhagavān āha / pañca vasāḥ prasevitavyāḥ / katamāḥ pañca / matsyavasā śuśukāvasā śuśumāravasā rikṣavasā sūkaravasā ca / itīmāḥ pañca vasāḥ / akāle pakvā akāle parisrutā akāle pratigrāhitā akāle 'dhiṣṭhitā na paribhoktavyāḥ / kāle pakvā akāle parisrutā akāle pratigrāhitā akāle 'dhiṣṭhitā na paribhoktavyāḥ / kāle pakvāḥ kāle parisrutā akāle pratigrāhitā akāle 'dhiṣṭhitā na paribhoktavyāḥ / kāle pakvāḥ kāle parisrutāḥ kāle pratigrāhitāḥ kāle 'dhiṣṭhitās tailaparibhogena saptāhaṃ paribhoktavyā iti / tatas tena bhikṣuṇā vasā paribhuktā / svasthaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ / (
children.translated_text: ) has arisen. Prescribe a medicine.' The physician said: 'Venerable one, use animal fat; you will become well.' The monk said: 'Good sir, am I a man-eater?' The physician said: 'Monk, this is your medicine; you cannot become well otherwise.' The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said: 'If a physician says, "This is the medicine for this monk; he cannot become well otherwise," then fat should be used.' The monks did not know [which fats]. They asked the physician. He said: 'Venerable ones, your own Teacher is omniscient; go and ask Him.' The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said: 'Five fats should be used. Which five? Fish fat, porpoise fat, crocodile fat, bear fat, and pig fat. These are the five fats. If cooked at the wrong time, strained at the wrong time, received at the wrong time, or designated at the wrong time, they should not be consumed. If cooked at the right time but strained at the wrong time, received at the wrong time, or designated at the wrong time, they should not be consumed. If cooked at the right time and strained at the right time but received at the wrong time or designated at the wrong time, they should not be consumed. If cooked at the right time, strained at the right time, received at the right time, and designated at the right time, they should be consumed within seven days as an oil-type preparation.' Then that monk consumed the fat and became well.
(MSV I vi)

bhikṣuṇopayuktaśeṣā vasā yācitāny asya bhikṣor dātavyā / noced glānakalpikaśālāyāṃ sthāpayitavyā / yo 'rthī bhaviṣyati sa grahīṣyatīti / vasādhārako bhikṣur yathāprajñaptān āsamudācārikān dharmān na samādāya vartate sātisāro bhavati /
children.translated_text: Having become well, he discarded the remaining fat, thinking 'I am healthy.' Then another monk developed the same kind of illness. He too went to the physician and said: 'Good sir, I have developed this kind of illness; prescribe a medicine.' The physician prescribed fat for him too. He went to that [first] monk and said: 'Venerable one, you used fat, and fat has been prescribed for me too by the physician. Is there any left over?' He said: 'There was, but I discarded it. That was not a good thing to do.' The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said: 'Indeed, a monk should not discard the remaining fat that has been used. I shall prescribe the customary rules for the monk who is the fat-keeper. The fat-keeper monk should give the remaining used fat to whichever monk requests it. If not, he should store it in the sick-room. Whoever needs it will take it.' A fat-keeper monk who does not observe the prescribed customary rules commits a transgression (<s>sātisāra</s>).

body.translated_text: At <s>Śrāvastī</s> was the setting. Now a certain monk developed an illness caused by wind [disorder]. He approached a physician.

children.translated_text: <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, on the second five hundred sages, and on the third five hundred monkeys. It was the habit of the monkey troop-leader to kill each newborn monkey infant. Thereupon those female monkeys, overcome with grief for their young, began to confer among themselves: "Listen, lady monkeys! This troop-leader of ours kills every infant as it is born. We must devise a stratagem. Whichever female monkey among us becomes pregnant should not report it to the troop-leader." In time, a certain female monkey became pregnant. She was hidden by the others in a concealed place and sustained with roots and fruits. A baby monkey was born. He too was placed by them in a concealed place, nourished, and raised. When he had grown large, he drove that troop-leader from his own troop. He began roaming here and there on Mount <s>Urumuṇḍa</s>.

children.translated_text: restlessness, finding no comfort, he listened attentively, longing for the sound of human voices. Then he heard the sound of the voices of those sages. Like a traveler who has lost his way, he hastened swiftly into their presence. Those sages were performing harsh austerities: some stood with arms raised upward, some on one foot, some practicing the five-fire penance. When that monkey had become accustomed to dwelling with them, he would bring those sages roots, leaves, flowers, fruits, and tooth-sticks as an offering. They too would give him the remainder of their alms-food. He then disrupted their deportment and demonstrated the deportment of the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. For those standing with arms raised, he pulled their arms down, made a clicking sound, and sat cross-legged before them. For those practicing the five-fire penance, he extinguished their fires, made a clicking sound, and sat cross-legged before them. Then those sages reported to their preceptor: "Preceptor, this tree-dwelling animal is disrupting our austerities." They reported to him in detail. He said: "Good sirs, these tree-dwelling animals are indeed possessed of memory. Surely this one must have seen some

You should show him disrespect; revile him with verbal abuse.' <s>Nīlabhūti</s> replied: 'Good sirs, this tongue of mine is truth-abiding. If he deserves abuse, I will abuse him. But if he deserves praise, I will praise him.' Then the Brahmin <s>Nīlabhūti</s>, accompanied by the most senior Brahmin residents of <s>Mathurā</s>, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The Brahmin <s>Nīlabhūti</s> saw the <s>Bhagavān</s> from afar, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty secondary characteristics, ornamented with an aura like the sky, his radiance surpassing that of a thousand suns,
(MSV I 9)

children.text:
) jaṃgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam anyataraṃ vṛkṣamūlaṃ niśritya śāntena īryāpathena niṣaṇṇam* / dṛṣṭvā ca vismayotphulladṛṣṭiḥ stotum
ārabdhaḥ /
children.translated_text: like a moving mountain of jewels, auspicious in every way, seated at the foot of a tree in a serene deportment. Having seen him, with eyes wide open in amazement, he began to praise him:

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, wandering through the <s>Śūrasena</s> country, arrived at <s>Mathurā</s>. The Brahmin inhabitants of <s>Mathurā</s> heard: 'The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> has arrived at <s>Mathurā</s>. He greatly advocates, illuminates, proclaims, promotes, opens up, reveals, makes clear, and teaches the purity of the four <s>varṇas</s> (social classes). If he enters <s>Mathurā</s>, there will be an obstruction to our gains. And he is heard to be averse to disrespect. If someone were to show him disrespect, he would not enter <s>Mathurā</s>. But if a lowly person were to disrespect him,

children.translated_text: O repository of virtues, O great ocean of virtues, I shall declare but a portion of your qualities. // 1
You are the supreme among debaters, faultless, with senses perfectly composed,
a knower of the ultimate truth, unshakable by all rival debaters however earnest. // 2

children.text: caraṇaṃ susamāptam eva te susamāptavrata sādhitavrataḥ /
children.translated_text: Your conduct is perfectly accomplished, O you of perfectly fulfilled vows, one whose vows are realized,

children.text: balavāṃś ca samādhir avyayas tava nārāyaṇaśailarājavat* // 3
children.translated_text: and your <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) is mighty and imperishable, like that of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and the king of mountains. // 3

children.text: puruṣarṣabha nāsti te vyathā na viṣādo na bhayaṃ na ca klamaḥ /
children.translated_text: O bull among men, you have no distress, no sorrow, no fear, and no fatigue,

children.text: na ca te vyasanaṃ kutaḥ kalir na ca bhūteṣu kadācid akṣamā // 4
children.translated_text: nor have you any misfortune—whence then strife?—nor ever any intolerance toward beings. // 4

children.text: na ca dhāvasi nātilīyase na ca santapyasi nāpi hṛṣyase /
children.translated_text: You neither rush about nor withdraw excessively, you neither burn with anguish nor become elated,

children.text: satataṃ śubham eva te manaḥ satataṃ merur ivācalādhipaḥ // 5
children.translated_text: your mind is always auspicious, like <s>Meru</s>, the lord of immovable mountains, always steadfast. // 5

children.text: munipuṅgava sarvadhātubhir vipulaṃ jñānam apāvṛtaṃ tava /
children.translated_text: O foremost among sages, through all the elements, your vast knowledge is unveiled,
unobstructed, imperishable and inexhaustible—you operate in the manifold sense-fields. // 6

children.text: na ca te 'sti mune kathaṃkathā vimatir nāsti na saṃśayaḥ kvacit* /
children.translated_text: Nor is there in you, O sage, any uncertainty, no wrong view, no doubt anywhere,

children.text: svayam eva na te parāparaṃ viditaṃ sarvam avedi vidyayā // 7
children.translated_text: not on your own account—the higher and the lower, all is known to you through your wisdom. // 7
Pleasing to behold, virtuous to behold, dear to the good, beloved of the wise,

children.text: samam eva hi te priyāpriyaṃ satataṃ prītikaras tatheryase // 8
children.translated_text: for pleasant and unpleasant are equal to you—always bringing delight, so you conduct yourself. // 8'
You are of sweet eloquence, of smiling speech, possessed of mindfulness, and confident;

children.text: vividānumataṃ prabhāṣase triṣu lokeṣu ca te stṛtaṃ yaśaḥ / 9
children.translated_text: you speak what is approved by the learned, and your fame is spread across the three worlds. (9)
Humans, gods, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>, many who are wise in this world,

children.text: upagamya mune punaḥ punaḥ paripṛcchanti na cābhiṣūyase // 10
children.translated_text: approaching you, O sage, again and again, ask questions, and you are never displeased. (10)
Satisfied by your own words, kings of men, gods, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: pratiyānti vinītasaṃśayāś caraṇau vandya ca te mahāmune // 11
children.translated_text: depart with their doubts removed, having bowed at your feet, O great sage. (11)

children.text: sthitam āsitam āgataṃ gataṃ śayitaṃ maunam athābhyudīritam* /
children.translated_text: Whether standing, sitting, coming, going, lying down, in silence, or in speaking,

children.text: atha cīvarapātradhāraṇaṃ ruciraṃ gautama sarvam eva te // 12
children.translated_text: and in the wearing of robe and bowl — everything is graceful in you, O <s>Gautama</s>. (12)
Neither too slow nor too fast, even, endowed with the qualities of sweetness of voice,

children.text: vacanaṃ punar uktavarjitaṃ samaye vyāharase narottama // 13
children.translated_text: words free from repetition — you speak at the proper time, O best of men. (13)

children.text: balavān asi lokaviśrutaḥ puruṣajñaḥ puruṣarṣabhaḥ prabhuḥ /
children.translated_text: You are powerful, renowned in the world, a knower of persons, a bull among men, a master;

children.text: na ca manyasi nāvamanyase sakalaṃ lokam imaṃ sadaivatam* // 14
children.translated_text: yet you neither pride yourself nor look down upon this entire world together with its gods. (14)

children.text:
na ca vismayase kadācana prakṛtistheṣu calācaleṣu ca /
suhṛdeṣu
children.translated_text: And you are never astonished by things remaining in their natural state, whether moving or unmoving, whether among friends
or
among foes, whether in adverse or favorable circumstances. (15)
The lamentation with its un-dejected sound, its cry accompanied by flowing saliva,
combined with burning and scorching, emaciated by fear, disease, fever, and grief — (16)

children.text: prasamīkṣya jagat samākulaṃ vividhair duḥkhaśatair upadrutam* /
children.translated_text: observing the world in turmoil, afflicted by hundreds of various sufferings,
long without protector, anxious, spread with the craving for existence, enveloped in darkness — (17)

children.text: avatārya muner mahākṛpāṃ vividhāṃ cātmagatāṃ prabhāvatām* /
children.translated_text: bringing down the great compassion of the sage and the manifold splendor belonging to yourself,

children.text: svayam eva hi śākyapuṅgava vyathitān mocayituṃ tvam udyataḥ // 18
children.translated_text: you yourself, O bull of the <s>Śākyas</s>, have arisen to liberate the afflicted. (18)

children.text: bhavaduḥkham idaṃ sahetukaṃ bhavaduḥkhasya ca yaḥ parikṣayaḥ /
children.translated_text: This suffering of existence together with its cause, and the destruction of that suffering of existence,
and the path leading to the cessation of existential suffering — incomparably, this is taught by you. (19)
O supreme hero, best of the great guides, foremost among those who teach,

children.text: na ca te sadṛśaḥ kuto 'dhikas triṣu lokeṣv api naiva vidyate // 20
children.translated_text: none equal to you exists, let alone one superior, in all three worlds. (20)
Feelings of hostility and attachment (

children.text: ) na santi te na ca te santi mune parisravāḥ /
children.translated_text: ) do not exist in you, nor, O sage, do <s>āsravas</s> (mental outflows) exist in you;

children.text: anurodhavirodhavigrahāḥ satataṃ suvrata naiva naiva te // 21
children.translated_text: affection, aversion, and conflict — never, never are these in you, O keeper of excellent vows. (21)
Having abandoned, O sage, the pleasant and unpleasant, happiness and suffering, the un-
even and the even likewise,

children.text: aratiṃ ca ratiṃ viparyayann upaśāntaś carasīha saṃyataḥ // 22
children.translated_text: and displeasure and pleasure exchanging — you walk here pacified and self-controlled. (22)

children.text: vyasane na ca nāma nirmanā na ca nāmonnamase praśaṃsayā /
children.translated_text: In misfortune you are not dejected, nor are you elated by praise;

children.text: ayaśaś ca yaśaś ca te samaṃ samam ākruṣṭam athāpi vanditam* // 23
children.translated_text: ill-repute and fame are the same to you, equal are abuse and veneration. (23)

children.text: ativākyam atho titikṣase puruṣaṃ pāpajanair udīritam* /
children.translated_text: You endure harsh words uttered by wicked people,

children.text: samarāgragato viṣāṇavān bhṛśamuktān iva kuñjaraḥ śarān* // 24
children.translated_text: like an elephant at the forefront of battle endures arrows fiercely shot. (24)

children.text: suvacas tvam ṛṣe vacaḥkṣamaḥ sudurukteṣv api nābhiṣūyase /
children.translated_text: You are of pleasant speech, O seer, patient with words, and even at harsh abuse you are not angered;

children.text: samam eva ca vartase mune paribhāṣāsu śubhāsu vākṣu ca // 25
children.translated_text: you remain the same, O sage, whether in insults or in auspicious words. (25)
Constantly, O worthy one, you are worshipped by kings of men, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: ṛṣibhiś ca sadā mahātmabhir na ca te vikriyate sthiraṃ manaḥ // 26
children.translated_text: and always by great-souled seers — yet your mind is not altered; it remains firm. (26)

children.text: pravaro 'ham ito na manyase 'tyavaro 'ham ito na manyase /
children.translated_text: 'I am superior to these' — thus you do not think; 'I am inferior to these' — thus you do not think;

children.text: sadṛśo 'ham ito na manyase trividhā mānavidhā na santi te // 27
children.translated_text: 'I am equal to these' — thus you do not think; the three kinds of conceit do not exist in you. (27)
Steadfast, regarding a lump of earth and gold as equal, a sapphire and gravel as the same,

children.text: tṛṇakāṣṭhasamaṃ mahāmune carasīdaṃ hi sadevakaṃ jagat* // 28
children.translated_text: regarding grass and wood as equal, O great sage, you move through this world with its gods. (28)
Enduring wind that is cold and hot from the contact of snow and sun's rays,

children.text: adhivāsayase nagendravan na ca te pravyathate sthiraṃ manaḥ // 29
children.translated_text: you bear it like a mountain-lord, and your firm mind is not disturbed. (29)
Bedding, seat, drink, food, and various robes — upper and lower garments —

children.text: idam arthikato nideśase pratisaṃkhyāya mune nirāsravam* // 30
children.translated_text: these you indicate only upon being asked, having reflected, O sage, free from outflows. (30)

children.text: na ca śocasi nātha nāsti me na ca te santi mune parigrahāḥ /
children.translated_text: You do not grieve saying 'I have not, O Lord,' nor do you have possessions, O sage;
you are seated, of pleasant speech, free from possessiveness, released from various calamities. (31)

children.text: na ca lābham avāpya hṛṣyase tadalābhāc ca layaṃ na gacchasi /
children.translated_text: Nor upon obtaining gain do you rejoice, and from its non-obtainment you do not collapse;

children.text: avamānam atho titikṣase na ca saṃmānam ihābhinandasi // 32
children.translated_text: you endure disrespect, and you do not delight in honor here. (32)
Supreme sandalwood paste, fragrant, born from <s>Mandāra</s> essence of the divine realm,

children.text: asayo niśitāḥ śarāś ca te na vikurvanti manaḥ kadācana // 33
children.translated_text: and sharp, whetted arrows — neither ever disturbs your mind. (33)

children.text:
na kathāṃ kathayasy anarthikāṃ na ca yā durjanasevitā kathā /
na
children.translated_text: You do not tell a story that is purposeless, nor a story that is frequented by the wicked, nor
a story about gain, nor

children.text: sāmiṣā na ca yā nānumatā mahātmabhiḥ // 34
children.translated_text: one that is tainted, nor one that is not approved by the great-souled. (34)

children.text: pravivekakathāḥ sukhāvahāḥ praśamaṃ yāḥ pravadanti kevalam* /
children.translated_text: Stories of solitude, bringing happiness, that speak only of tranquility —

children.text: kathayasy atidevatāḥ kathāḥ kathitā yā vinayanti kilviṣam* // 35
children.translated_text: you tell stories surpassing those of the gods, stories that, when told, remove sin. (35)

children.text: madhurāṇi ca saṅgatāni ca svabhinītāni ca sāravanti ca /
children.translated_text: Sweet, coherent, well-composed, and substantial —

children.text: vacanāni mune prabhāṣase jagadarthāya viniścitāni ca // 36
children.translated_text: such words you speak, O sage, for the benefit of the world, and with firm resolve. (36)
The foolish, those of perverted views, the fickle, the reckless, those attached to pleasures,

children.text: piśunāḥ paruṣāḥ śaṭhāś ca ye bhagavaṃs taiḥ saha saṅgataṃ na te // 37
children.translated_text: the slanderous, the harsh, and the deceitful — with these, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, you have no association. (37)

children.text: aśaṭhā ṛjavaś ca ye narāḥ śucayaḥ satyaratā jitendriyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those men who are without deceit, upright, pure, devoted to truth, with senses controlled,

children.text: satataṃ ca samīkṣyakāriṇo bhagavaṃs taiḥ saha saṅgataṃ tava // 38
children.translated_text: and always acting with deliberation — with these, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is your association. (38)

children.text: dharmajña nayajña pudgalajña tvāṃ vande ṣaḍabhijña sarvadaiva /
children.translated_text: O knower of <s>Dharma</s>, knower of guidance, knower of persons — I bow to you, O possessor of the six <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), at all times;

children.text: kṣetrajña mune parāparajña tvāṃ vande śirasā nayānayajña // 39
children.translated_text: O knower of the field, O sage, knower of the higher and the lower — I bow to you with my head, O knower of propriety and impropriety. (39)
Even this extensive quality
of yours
is but a single portion of your qualities, described by me;

children.text: na tava guṇamahārṇavasya pāraṃ jagati pumān adhigantum ārya śaktaḥ // 40
children.translated_text: no person in the world, O noble one, is capable of reaching the far shore of the great ocean of your virtues. (40)

body.translated_text: 'Having directed the mind together with the senses, and the speech and body in due order,

body.text: ity evamādibhiḥ pañcabhiḥ stotraśatair bhagavān abhiṣṭutaḥ {MS

children.translated_text: was pleased

children.text: } / tathābhiprasannasya ca bhagavatā nīlabhūter dharmo deśitaḥ / yathā yathā tasminn evāsane niṣaṇṇena satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam* / atha nīlabhūtir brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ stutvā prakrāntaḥ / so 'dhvapratipanno māthuryair brāhmaṇaiḥ saṃcamparīkṛtaḥ / upādhyāya tvam asmābhir abhihitaḥ / śramaṇasya gautamasyāsatkāraṃ kuruṣveti / sa tvam etarhi stutvā āgataḥ / bhavanto na tv ahaṃ pūrvam avocam* / mama jihvā satyābhidhāyinī / yady ākrośārho bhaviṣyati / ākrośe / stavārho bhaviṣyati / stoṣya iti / stavārhaḥ śramaṇo gautamo mayā stutaḥ /
children.translated_text: } And to the thus-devoted <s>Nīlabhūti</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> taught the <s>Dharma</s>. While seated on that very seat, he attained the vision of truth. Then the brahmin <s>Nīlabhūti</s>, having praised the <s>Bhagavān</s>, departed. While on his journey, he was accosted by the brahmins of <s>Mathurā</s>: 'Teacher, we told you to show disrespect to the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>, yet you have now come back having praised him.' He replied: 'Good sirs, did I not say before? My tongue speaks truth. If he were deserving of abuse, I would abuse him. If he were deserving of praise, I would praise him. The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> is deserving of praise; therefore I praised him.'

body.translated_text: With five hundred verses of praise such as these and more, the <s>Bhagavān</s> was extolled. {MS:

body.text: atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya mathurāṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat* / tena khalu samayena mathurāyāṃ nakṣatrarātraḥ pratyupasthitaḥ / atha yā devatā mathurāyām adhyuṣitā tasyā etad abhavat* / yadi śramaṇo gautamo mathurāṃ pravekṣyati / mama nakṣatrarātrer antarāyaṃ kariṣyatīti viditvā bhagavataḥ purastād vinagno 'sthāt* / bhagavān āha / apraticchannas tāvad devate mātṛgrāmo na śobhate prāg eva vinagna iti / atha sā devatā jihrīya nagnarūpā ekānte 'pakrāntā / tato bhagavān mārgād apakramya purastād bhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ / niṣadya bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma / pañceme bhikṣava ādīnavā mathurāyām* / katame pañca / utkūlanikūlāḥ sthāṇukaṇṭakapradhānā (

children.translated_text: MSV I 15
), has many stones, gravel, and pebbles, its food offerings are poor, and it has an abundance of women.'

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robes, entered <s>Mathurā</s> for alms. At that time, a <s>nakṣatra</s>-festival (star-festival) had arrived in <s>Mathurā</s>. Then a goddess who dwelt in <s>Mathurā</s> had this thought: 'If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> enters <s>Mathurā</s>, he will create an obstacle to my <s>nakṣatra</s>-festival.' Having ascertained this, she stood naked before the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'O goddess, even when not concealed a woman is not becoming, how much less when naked.' Then that goddess, feeling ashamed in her naked form, withdrew to one side. Thereupon the <s>Bhagavān</s>, turning aside from the road, sat down on a seat prepared before the assembly of monks. Having sat down, the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'There are, O monks, five disadvantages of <s>Mathurā</s>. What five? It has uneven terrain, is strewn with stumps and thorns (

body.text: atha bahagavān na praviśann eva mathurāṃ yena gardabhasya yakṣasya bhavanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / upasaṃkramya gardabhasya yakṣasya bhavanam abhyavagāhyānyatarad vṛkṣamūlaṃ niśritya niṣaṇṇo divāvihārāya / aśrauṣur māthurā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo bhagavān piṇḍāya prāviśat* devatayā viheṭhitaḥ / apraviśann eva mathurāṃ gardabhasya yakṣasya bhavanaṃ gata iti śrutvā ca punaḥ śucinaḥ praṇītasya khādanīyabhojanīyasya pratyekaṃ pratyekaṃ sthālīpākaṃ samudānīya śakaṭe āropya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ / ekāntaniṣaṇṇān* śrāddhān māthurān brāhmaṇagṛhapatīn bhagavān dharmyayā kathayā pūrvavad yāvat saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm* / atha śrāddhā brāhmaṇagṛhapataya utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantam idam avocat* / ihāsmābhir bhadanta bhagavantam uddiśya śucinaḥ praṇītasya khādanīyabhojanīyasya śakaṭaṃ pūrṇam ānītam* / tad bhagavān pratigṛhṇātu anukampām upādāya iti / tatra bhagavān ānandam āyuṣmantam āmantrayate / gacchānanda yāvanto bhikṣavo gardabhasya yakṣasya bhavanam (

children.translated_text: MSV I 16

'Yes, venerable sir,' the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, assembled all the monks dwelling in the vicinity of the dwelling of the <s>Yakṣa</s> <s>Gardabhaka</s> in the assembly hall, and approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached and bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> feet, he stood to one side. Standing to one side, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> spoke thus to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Venerable sir, however many monks were dwelling in the vicinity of the dwelling of the <s>Yakṣa</s> <s>Gardabhaka</s>, they are all seated and assembled in the assembly hall. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> now do as he sees fit.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> approached the assembly hall. Having approached, he sat on a seat prepared before the assembly of monks. Then the faithful brahmins and householders of <s>Mathurā</s>, having ascertained that the <s>Saṃgha</s> (monastic community) headed by the <s>Buddha</s> was comfortably seated, as before, up to the point where, with hands washed and bowls put away, they stood before the <s>Bhagavān</s> making a request and said: 'Venerable sir, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has tamed various fierce <s>Nāgas</s> and fierce <s>Yakṣas</s>. Venerable sir, this <s>Yakṣa</s> <s>Gardabhaka</s> has been our long-standing enemy though we bear no enmity, our rival though we have no rivalry, our harmer though we have done no harm. Generation after generation, he carries off our children. Would that the <s>Bhagavān</s> might tame the <s>Yakṣa</s> <s>Gardabhaka</s>, out of compassion.' At that time, the <s>Yakṣa</s> <s>Gardabhaka</s> was seated in that very assembly, having arrived. Thereupon the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the <s>Yakṣa</s> <s>Gardabhaka</s>: 'Have you heard, <s>Gardabhaka</s>?' 'I have heard, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' 'Have you heard, <s>Gardabhaka</s>?' (

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, without entering <s>Mathurā</s>, went to the dwelling of the <s>Yakṣa</s> <s>Gardabhaka</s>. Having entered the dwelling of the <s>Yakṣa</s> <s>Gardabhaka</s>, he sat down at the foot of a certain tree for his midday rest. The brahmins and householders of <s>Mathurā</s> heard that the <s>Bhagavān</s> had entered for alms but was obstructed by the goddess, and that without entering <s>Mathurā</s> he had gone to the dwelling of the <s>Yakṣa</s> <s>Gardabhaka</s>. Having heard this, they gathered individually prepared offerings of pure, choice hard and soft foods in pots, loaded them onto carts, and approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached and bowed their heads at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> feet, they sat down to one side. To the faithful householders and brahmins of <s>Mathurā</s> seated to one side, the <s>Bhagavān</s> gladdened them with a discourse on <s>Dharma</s>, as before, up to falling silent. Then the faithful brahmins and householders, rising from their seats, arranging their upper robes over one shoulder, joining their palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, spoke thus to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Venerable sir, we have brought here for the <s>Bhagavān</s> a cart full of pure, choice hard and soft foods. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> accept it out of compassion.' Thereupon the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, and however many monks are dwelling in the vicinity of the dwelling of the <s>Yakṣa</s> <s>Gardabhaka</s> (

The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'They performed such <s>karmas</s>, monks,' and so forth in detail.

body.text: ete kāśyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya śāsane pravrajitāḥ / ebhis tatra kausīdyenābhināmitam* / tasya karmaṇo vipākena kārṣikāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ / ebhiś ca balīvardais tatraiva pravrajitaiḥ kṣudrānukṣudraiḥ śikṣāpadair anādaraṃ kṛtam* / tasya karmaṇo vipākena tiryakṣūpapannāḥ / yat te kāśyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya śāsane pravrajitās tasya karmaṇo vipākena mamāntikāt satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam iti hi bhikṣavaḥ ekāntakṛṣṇānām iti vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: They had gone forth in the dispensation of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One. There they succumbed to laziness. By the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, they became farmers. And these oxen, having gone forth in the same dispensation, showed disrespect toward the minor and subsidiary training rules. By the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, they were reborn in the animal realm. Because they had gone forth in the dispensation of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, by the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, they attained the vision of truth in my presence. Thus, monks, those of exclusively dark deeds... and so forth in detail.

body.translated_text: Then the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Otalāyana</s> thought: 'What harm will this cause us?' He had previously heard: 'The ascetic <s>Gautama</s>, having fed the <s>Saṃgha</s> together with his disciples, makes a dedication. Whatever he contemplates, whatever he desires, all of that he obtains.' Then the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Otalāyana</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, extending his joined palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: 'May the venerable <s>Gautama</s> consent to accept a meal tomorrow in my house together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks.' As before, up to the point where, knowing he had finished eating and had washed his hands and the bowl had been removed, having taken a lower seat before the <s>Bhagavān</s>, he began to form a wrong aspiration: 'May all these <s>śramaṇas</s>, sons of the <s>Śākya</s>, whom I have fed, become my oxen!' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing with his mind the thought in <s>Otalāyana</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s mind, addressed the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Otalāyana</s> thus: 'You have generated an unseemly thought, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. It will not succeed. For all these monks have exhausted future births. Generate another thought.' Having said this, the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave instruction on the dedication of merit and departed. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> went to the monastery and sat upon a seat arranged before the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks. Having sat down, the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'Monks, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Otalāyana</s> generated an evil thought arising from a wrong aspiration (

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, after the passing of that very night, entered <s>Otalā</s> for alms, with the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> as his attendant walking behind. At that time in <s>Otalā</s> there was an old woman named <s>Kacaṃgalā</s>. She, seeking water, had gone to the riverbank. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, perceiving the time for her spiritual training, addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, and tell this old woman: "The <s>Bhagavān</s> is thirsty; please offer water."' 'Yes, venerable sir,' the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> replied to the <s>Bhagavān</s> and approached the old woman <s>Kacaṃgalā</s>. Having approached, he addressed the old woman <s>Kacaṃgalā</s> thus: '<s>Kacaṃgalā</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> is thirsty; please offer water.' She said: 'Venerable one, I myself will bring it.' Then <s>Kacaṃgalā</s>, having filled a water pot, quickly and hastily approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. <s>Kacaṃgalā</s> beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, adorned with a halo of light, his radiance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, auspicious on all sides. At the very sight, a motherly love for him arose in <s>Kacaṃgalā</s>. She, with arms raised, began to embrace the <s>Bhagavān</s>, crying 'Son! Son!' The monks tried to restrain her. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Do not restrain this old woman, monks. And for what reason?'

body.translated_text: Having said this, she paid homage at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet with her head and departed from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence. Then <s>Kacaṃgalā</s>, at another time, having obtained permission from her master, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached and paid homage at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet with her head, she sat to one side. Seated to one side, <s>Kacaṃgalā</s> addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: 'May I, venerable sir, obtain the going forth, the full ordination, the status of a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> (nun) in the well-taught <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>; may I practice the holy life in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s (

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo bodhisatvacaryāyāṃ vartamānasya eṣā mama mātā babhūva / yadāhaṃ pravrajitum icchāmi tadā mām eva vārayati / tasya karmaṇo vipākena vṛddhā pravrajitā / dānaṃ dadato me 'nayā dānāntarāyaḥ kṛtaḥ / tena daridrā saṃvṛttā / na cānayā puṇyamaheśākhyasaṃvartanīyāni karmāṇi kṛtāni yathā mahāmāyayā yenāham anayā paścime garbhavāsena dhāritaḥ / kāśyape ca samyaksaṃbuddhe pravrajitā yāḥ śaikṣāśaikṣā bhikṣuṇyo dāsīvādena samudācaritāḥ / tena dāsī saṃvṛttā / yat tatrānayā paṭhitaṃ svādhyāyitaṃ skandhakauśalaṃ dhātukauśalam āyatanakauśalaṃ pratītyasamutpādakauśalaṃ sthānāsthānakauśalaṃ ca kṛtaṃ tena mama śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* / yasyāś copādhyāyikāyāḥ sakāśe pravrajitā sā bhagavatā kāśyapena samyaksaṃbuddhena sūtrāntavibhāgakartrīṇām agrā nirdiṣṭā / tatrānayā maraṇakālasamaye praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ yan mayā bhagavati kāśyape samyaksaṃbuddhe anuttare dakṣiṇīye yāvad āyur brahmacaryaṃ caritaṃ na ca kaścid guṇagaṇo 'dhigataḥ / anena kuśalamūlena yo 'sau bhagavatā kāśyapenottaro nāma māṇavo vyākṛto bhaviṣyati / tvaṃ māṇava varṣaśatāyuṣi prajāyāṃ śākyamunir nāma tathāgato 'rhat samyaksaṃbuddha iti / tasyāhaṃ śāsane pravrajeyam* / (

Thus, monks, for actions that are entirely black, the ripening is entirely black. As before, up to: effort should be made. 'Thus, monks, you should train yourselves.' This he spoke.

body.translated_text: Monks, in a former time, when I was engaged in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice, this one was my mother. Whenever I wished to go forth into homelessness, she would restrain me. As the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, she went forth only in old age. When I was giving gifts, she created an obstruction to my giving. Through that she became poor. Nor had she performed <s>karma</s> leading to the designation 'Great Lord of Merit,' as <s>Mahāmāyā</s> had, by whom I was borne in the womb in my last birth. And under the perfectly awakened <s>Kāśyapa</s>, she went forth but addressed the trainee and non-trainee <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> with the epithet 'slave.' Through that she became a slave. But whatever she recited and studied there—skill in the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), skill in the <s>dhātus</s> (elements), skill in the <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), skill in <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), and skill in <s>sthānāsthāna</s> (possible and impossible)—through that, having gone forth in my dispensation, she realized <s>arhatva</s> (the state of an arhat) by the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). And the preceptress under whom she went forth was declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the perfectly awakened one, as foremost among those who analyze the <s>sūtras</s>. There, at the time of death, she made this aspiration: 'Under the <s>Bhagavān Kāśyapa</s>, the perfectly awakened one, the supreme field of merit, I have practiced the holy life for a full lifespan, yet I have not attained any collection of virtues. By this root of merit, may I go forth in the dispensation of the one whom the <s>Bhagavān Kāśyapa</s> prophesied—the young man named <s>Uttara</s>: You, young man, in a generation whose lifespan is a hundred years, will be the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly awakened one named <s>Śākyamuni</s>.' body.translated_text: There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Come, <s>Ānanda</s>, let us go to <s>Vairaṃbhya</s>.' 'Yes, Venerable Sir,' the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> set out and reached a certain garden. A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> was drawing water from a well and had begun to irrigate the garden. That <s>brāhmaṇa</s> saw the <s>Bhagavān</s> from afar. Having seen him, he thought: 'If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> enters the garden, he will defile the garden's well.' So he hid the rope and bucket and stood there. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> entered the garden by his supernatural power, and <s>Pāṃcika</s>, the great <s>Yakṣa</s> general, caused that well to overflow. The entire garden was flooded with water. Then that <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having understood that 'this ascetic <s>Gautama</s> is of great supernatural power and great might,' spoke with great faith: (

The venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having risen early in the morning, approached the residence of <s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king. There he saw that the servants of <s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king were standing about with little enthusiasm. Seeing this, he said: 'Good people, why do you stand about with so little enthusiasm?' They replied: 'Venerable Sir, what can we do? Has not <s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king invited the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> for the three months with all requisites? Yet you stand about with little enthusiasm, neither preparing food nor arranging seats. Will the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> suffer a break in meals?' They replied: 'Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, the king gave orders: "Prepare food for five hundred—choice and abundant." But he did not say "for such and such a purpose."' 'Good people, go and inform him.' 'Venerable Sir, the king has had a bell proclamation made: "No one shall come to see me. Whoever approaches shall receive the death penalty." Why should we risk our heads? We shall not inform him.' Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s> in detail. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, take the <s>saṃghāṭī</s> (monastic robe) and a wandering ascetic, and announce in the streets, lanes, crossroads, and intersections of <s>Vairaṃbhya</s>: "Whoever among you, good people, is able to feed the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> for the three months, let him do so."' 'Yes, Venerable Sir,' the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, took the <s>saṃghāṭī</s> and a wandering ascetic, and announced in the streets, lanes, crossroads, and intersections: 'Whoever among you, good people, is able to feed the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> for the three months, let him do so.' body.translated_text: Then <s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, joined his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May the <s>Bhagavān Gautama</s>, together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks, accept from me for the three months' rains-retreat robes, almsfood, bedding and seats, and medicines and provisions for the sick.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> accepted <s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king's invitation through silence. Then <s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king, having understood the <s>Bhagavān's</s> acceptance through silence, rejoiced and approved of the <s>Bhagavān's</s> words, and departed from the <s>Bhagavān's</s> presence. Having gone to his residence, he gave orders to his ministers: 'Prepare daily eighteen kinds of food and abundant meals accompanied by various soups and flavorful condiments.' And he had a bell proclamation made in <s>Vairaṃbhya</s>: 'No one else shall feed the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> during the three months. Whoever feeds him shall receive the death penalty.' body.translated_text: When the <s>Bhagavān</s> began to eat the barley, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, distressed, began to shed tears, thinking: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s>, in those cycles of birth, having given gifts of hands, feet, head, and so forth, having attained omniscience through three incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), now eats hollow barley grains!' Thereupon the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Why are you distressed, <s>Ānanda</s>, shedding tears?' 'Venerable sir, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, born in the lineage of <s>Cakravartins</s>, having renounced kingship and gone forth, having given gifts of hands, feet, head, and so forth, having attained omniscience through three incalculable <s>kalpas</s>, now eats hollow barley grains!' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Do you wish, <s>Ānanda</s>, to eat barley grains that have passed between the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teeth?' 'I do, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> one of the barley grains (

body.text: taiḥ sāmantakaiḥ śabdo vistṛtaḥ / agnidatto brāhmaṇarājo buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃgham upanimaṃtryādarśanapathe sthito bhagavān vairaṃbhye yavān paribhuṃkte iti / sāmantarājair api śrutaṃ tair agnidattasya brāhmaṇarājasya dūtasaṃpreṣaṇaṃ kṛtam* / te praveśaṃ na labhante dvāri sthitāḥ / anāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā śrutaṃ tena paṃcamātrāṇi śakaṭaśatāni parṇopagūṭhasya śāleḥ preṣitāni / atha mārasya pāpīyasa etad abhavat* / bahuśo mayā śramaṇo gautamo viheṭhito na kadācid avatāro labdhaḥ / atrāpi tāvad asya praharāmi iti viditvā āyuṣmantam ānandam ātmānaṃ vinirmāya teṣāṃ paṃcānāṃ śakaṭaśatānāṃ purataḥ sthitvā kathayati / bhavantaḥ kutra gamyate / te kathayanti /

children.translated_text: 'Venerable

children.text: ānanda agnidatto brāhmaṇarājo bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃgham upanimaṃtryādarśanapathe sthito bhagavān vairaṃbhye yavān paribhuṃkte iti / anāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā śrutvaitāni parṇopagūṭhasya śāler bhagavato 'rthāya paṃca śakaṭaśatāni preṣitāni iti / sa kathayati / bhavanto devo abhiprasannā nāgā yakṣāḥ / yadi bhagavān ākāśe pātraṃ prasārayati tad api devās trayastriṃśā divyāyāḥ sudhāyāḥ pūrayanti / kimarthaṃ bhagavān yavān paribhuṃkte / nivartayatha (
children.translated_text: <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king, having invited the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples, has gone out of sight, and the <s>Bhagavān</s> is eating barley in <s>Vairaṃbhya</s>. The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, having heard this, has sent these five hundred cartloads of rice wrapped in leaves for the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' He said: 'Good people, the gods are well-disposed, the <s>nāgas</s> and <s>yakṣas</s> too. If the <s>Bhagavān</s> extends his bowl into the sky, even the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-three) gods would fill it with divine ambrosia. Why would the <s>Bhagavān</s> eat barley? Turn back (
MSV I 40

children.text: ) iti / te kathayanti / āryānanda saṃprasthitā vayaṃ kim idānīṃ nivartāmaḥ / gacchāma iti / māraḥ saṃlakṣayati / na śakyam ete nivartayitum* / upāyasaṃvidhānaṃ kartavyam iti / sa uparivihāyasam abhyudgamya akṣamātrābhir vāridhārābhir varṣitum ārabdhaḥ / tena tāvad dṛṣṭaṃ yāvat tāni śakaṭāni nābhiṃ yāvan nimagnāni / tatas te śākaṭikā balīvardān muktvā prakrāntā iti / tatra bhagavatā vairaṃbhye yavāḥ paribhuktāḥ sārdhaṃ dvayonaiḥ paṃcabhir bhikṣuśataiḥ / āyuṣmadbhyāṃ śāriputramaudgalyāyanābhyāṃ triśaṃkuke parvate varṣopagatābhyāṃ divyā sudhā paribhuktā /
children.translated_text: )!' They replied: 'Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, we have already set out; why should we turn back now? We shall go.' <s>Māra</s> reflected: 'These cannot be turned back. A stratagem must be devised.' He rose up into the sky and began to rain down hailstones the size of dice. And so much fell that those carts sank up to their hubs. Then those carters, having released the oxen, departed. There in <s>Vairaṃbhya</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> ate barley together with the five hundred monks minus two. The venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, who had entered the rains-retreat on <s>Triśaṃku</s> mountain, ate divine ambrosia.

body.translated_text: The report spread throughout the vicinity: '<s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king, having invited the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>, has gone out of sight while the <s>Bhagavān</s> eats barley in <s>Vairaṃbhya</s>.' The neighboring kings also heard this and sent messengers to <s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king. But they could not gain entry and stood at the gate. The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> heard this and sent five hundred cartloads of rice wrapped in leaves. Then <s>Māra</s> the evil one thought: 'Many times I have harassed the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> and have never found an opportunity. Let me strike at him here too.' Knowing this, having created a likeness of the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, he stood before those five hundred carts and said: 'Good people, where are you going?' They replied:

body.text: tatas tena sārthavāhena traimāsasyātyayād bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃgho bhaktenopanimaṃtritaḥ / adhivāsitaṃ ca bhagavatā tūṣṇīṃbhāvena / sa sārthavāhas tām eva rātriṃ śuciṃ praṇītaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ samudānīya pūrvavad yāvad bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastam apanītapātraṃ bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ / anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena rājā bhaveyaṃ cakravartī aśvājāneyaḥ putro yuvarājas tāny api paṃcāśvaśatāni paṃca putraśatāni / (

children.text: ) yā sā dārikā bhagavatā strīratnaṃ yāni paṃca dārikāśatāni tasyāḥ paricārikā iti / tato bhagavāṃs tasya sārthavāhasya cetasā cittam ājñāya taṃ sārthavāham idam avocat* / bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ sārthavāha rājā cakravartī aśvājāneyas te putro yuvarājas tāny api paṃcāśvaśatāni paṃca putraśatāni / sā dārikā (

Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing with his mind the thought in that caravan-leader's mind, said this to that caravan-leader: 'You, caravan-leader, will become a <s>Cakravartin</s> king; the thoroughbred horse will be your son, the crown prince; those five hundred horses will be five hundred sons; that girl will be the (

children.text: ) strīratnam* / tāny api dvyūnāni paṃca dārikāśatāni tasyāḥ paricārikā iti /

body.translated_text: Then, after the three months had passed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks was invited to a meal by that caravan-leader. The <s>Bhagavān</s> accepted through silence. That caravan-leader, on that very night, having prepared pure and excellent hard and soft foods, as before up to, knowing the <s>Bhagavān</s> had finished eating and had washed his hands and the bowl had been removed, fell at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and began to make an aspiration: 'By this root of merit, may I become a <s>Cakravartin</s> king; may the thoroughbred horse be my son, the crown prince; may those five hundred horses be five hundred sons; (

body.text: atha bhagavān traimāsasyātyayāt kṛtacīvaro niṣṭhitacīvaraḥ āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate / gacchānanda agnidattaṃ brāhmaṇarājam ārocaya / evaṃ ca vada / uṣitāḥ smo mahārāja tava vijite / avalokito bhava / gacchāma iti / evaṃ bhadanta iti / āyuṣmān ānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya yenāgnidattasya brāhmaṇarājasya niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / tena khalu samayenāgnidatto brāhmaṇarājaḥ puṇyāham āgamayaṃs tiṣṭhati / athāyuṣmān ānando dauvārikaṃ puruṣam āmantrayate / ehi tvaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa yenāgnidatto brāhmaṇarājas tenopasaṃkrama / upasaṃkramyāgnidattaṃ brāhmaṇarājam evaṃ vada / ānando bhikṣur dvāre tiṣṭhati devaṃ draṣṭukāma iti / evam ārya iti dauvārikapuruṣaḥ āyuṣmata ānandasya pratiśrutya yenāgnidatto brāhmaṇarājas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / upasaṃkramyāgnidattaṃ brāhmaṇarājam idam avocat* / devāryānando bhikṣur dvāre tiṣṭhati devaṃ draṣṭukāmaḥ / sa kathayati / ahaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa puṇyāham āgamayaṃs tiṣṭhāmi / ānando bhikṣuḥ puṇyamaheśākhyaḥ / sa eva puṇyāho bhavatu /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, at the end of the three months, having finished making his robes, addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, and inform <s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king. Speak thus: "We have dwelt, O great king, in your domain. Consider yourself noticed. We shall depart."' 'Yes, Venerable Sir,' the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s> and approached the residence of <s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king. At that time, <s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king was observing an auspicious day. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> addressed the doorkeeper: 'Come, good man, approach <s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king and say this: "The monk <s>Ānanda</s> stands at the gate, wishing to see His Majesty."' 'Yes, noble sir,' the doorkeeper assented to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> and approached <s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king. Having approached, he spoke thus to <s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king: 'Your Majesty, the noble monk <s>Ānanda</s> stands at the gate, wishing to see Your Majesty.' He replied: 'Good man, I am observing an auspicious day. The monk <s>Ānanda</s> is called the Great Lord of Merit. Let him himself be the auspicious day.

body.text: paṃcakalyāṇaś cāyam* / nāmakalyāṇo rūpakalyāṇo varṇakalyāṇaḥ pratibhānakalyāṇaḥ pratipattikalyāṇaś ca /
body.translated_text: Moreover, he possesses the five excellences: excellence of name, excellence of form, excellence of complexion, excellence of eloquence, and excellence of conduct.

body.text: praviśatu / ko bhavantam ānandaṃ vārayatīti / dauvārikeṇāyuṣmata ānandāyaivam ārocitam* āyuṣmān ānandaḥ praviṣṭaḥ / te 'pi sāmantarājānāṃ dūtās tenaiva sārdhaṃ praviṣṭāḥ /
body.translated_text: Let him enter. Who would turn away the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>?' The doorkeeper informed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> accordingly. The venerable <s>Ānanda</s> entered. The envoys of the neighboring kings also entered along with him.

body.text: athāyuṣmān ānando 'gnidattaṃ brāhamaṇarājam ārogyayitvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ / ekāntaniṣaṇṇaḥ āyuṣmān ānando 'gnidattaṃ brāhmaṇarājam idam avocat* / bhagavāṃs te mahārāja ārogyayati kathayati ca / uṣitāḥ smo mahārāja tava vijite traimāsīm* / avalokito bhava / gacchāma iti / vande āryānanda buddhaṃ bhagavantam* / kaccid āryānanda bhagavān vairaṃbhyeṣu janapadeṣu sukhaṃ varṣoṣitaḥ / na ca piṇḍakena klānta iti / taiḥ sāmantarājadūtair uktaḥ / devo 'pratyakṣitarājyas tvaṃ yo bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ traimāsīm upanimaṃtryādarśanapathe vyavasthitaḥ / traimāsīṃ koṭarayavāḥ paribhuktā iti / sa kathayati / satyam āryānanda bhagavatā traimāsīṃ yavāḥ paribhuktāḥ / satyaṃ mahārāja / sa saṃmūrchitaḥ (

children.text: ) pṛthivyāṃ nipatito mahatā jalapariṣekeṇa pratyāgataprāṇaḥ amātyān āhūya pṛcchati / bhavanto na mayā yuṣmākam ājñā dattā / pratidivasaṃ paṃcānāṃ śatānām āhāraṃ sajjīkuru / praṇītaṃ prabhūtaṃ ceti / te kathayanti / asti devenaivam ājñaptam* / na tv ājñā dattā amukasya dātavyam iti / api tu adyāpy āhāraḥ sajjīkṛta eva / athāgnidatto brāhmaṇarājo yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ / ekāntaniṣaṇṇam agnidattaṃ brāhmaṇarājaṃ bhagavān dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati pūrvavad yāvat saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm* / athāgnidatto brāhmaṇarājo bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya bhagavantam idam avocat* / (
children.translated_text: ) and fell to the ground. Having been revived by a great sprinkling of water, he summoned his ministers and asked: 'Good sirs, did I not give you the order: "Prepare daily food for five hundred, choice and abundant"?' They replied: 'Your Majesty did indeed give such an order, but no order was given as to whom it should be given.' 'Moreover, the food has been prepared even to this day.' Then <s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached and bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> feet, he sat down to one side. To <s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king seated to one side, the <s>Bhagavān</s> instructed him with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, as before up to gladdening him, then fell silent. Then <s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king, falling at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> feet, spoke thus to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: (
MSV I 43

children.text:
) atyayo bhagavann atyayaḥ sugata yathā bālo yathā mūḍho yathāvyakto yathākuśalo yo 'haṃ bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ traimāsīm upanimaṃtryādarśanapathe vyavasthitaḥ / tasya mama bhagavann atyayaṃ jānato 'tyayaṃ paśyataḥ atyayam atyayataḥ pratigṛhṇīṣvānukampām upādāya / tathyaṃ te mahārāja atyayam atyayata āgamā yathā bālo yathā mūḍho yathāvyakto yathākuśalo yas tvaṃ tathāgataṃ traimāsīm upanimaṃtryādarśanapathe vyavasthitaḥ / yatas tvaṃ mahārāja atyayaṃ jānāsy atyayaṃ paśyasi taṃ ca dṛṣṭvādeśayasi vṛddhir eva te pratikāṃkṣitavyā
kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ na hāniḥ /
children.translated_text: ) 'A transgression, <s>Bhagavān</s>! A transgression, <s>Sugata</s>! Like a fool, like one deluded, like one ignorant, like one unskillful — that I, having invited the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples for the three months, remained out of sight. May the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing my transgression as a transgression, seeing the transgression, accept the transgression as a transgression, out of compassion.' 'Truly, O great king, a transgression came upon you as a transgression — that like a fool, like one deluded, like one ignorant, like one unskillful, you invited the <s>Tathāgata</s> for the three months and then remained out of sight. But since you, O great king, know the transgression as a transgression and see the transgression, and having seen it you confess it — growth is to be expected for you in wholesome qualities, not decline.'

body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having greeted <s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king with wishes for his health, sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> spoke thus to <s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> sends you greetings of health, O great king, and says: "We have dwelt, O great king, in your domain for the three months. Consider yourself noticed. We shall depart."' 'Noble <s>Ānanda</s>, I pay homage to the <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s>. Is the <s>Bhagavān</s>, noble <s>Ānanda</s>, comfortable after having spent the rains in the <s>Vairaṃbhya</s> region? Was he not wearied by alms-begging?' The envoys of the neighboring kings spoke to him: 'Your Majesty, you are one who has neglected his kingdom, for having invited the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples for the three months, you remained out of sight. For the three months, husked barley was consumed.' He replied: 'Is it true, noble <s>Ānanda</s>, that the <s>Bhagavān</s> consumed barley for the three months?' 'It is true, O great king.' He fainted (

children.text: ) śoṇitaṃ chardayitvā kālaṃ kariṣyatīti viditvā adhivāsitaṃ bhagavatā tūṣṇīṃbhāvena / athāgnidatto brāhmaṇarājo bhagavatas tūṣṇīṃbhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrānto yena svaṃ niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / upasaṃkramyāmātyān āmaṃtrayate bhavantaḥ ko 'sau upāyaḥ syād yena sarvo 'yam āhāro buddhapramukhena bhikṣusaṃghena paribhukto bhaved iti / te kathayanti / deva sarvo 'yaṃ pṛthivyām āhāras tīryatām* / bhikṣavaḥ padbhyām ākramiṣyanti / evaṃ paribhukto bhaviṣyatīti / tena (
children.translated_text: ) blood and die.' Having known this, the <s>Bhagavān</s> accepted through silence. Then <s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king, having understood the <s>Bhagavān's</s> acceptance through silence, departed from the <s>Bhagavān's</s> presence and approached his own residence. Having approached, he addressed his ministers: 'Good sirs, what means could there be by which all this food would be consumed by the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>?' They replied: 'Your Majesty, let all this food be spread upon the ground. The monks will walk upon it with their feet. Thus it will be consumed.' Thereupon (

children.text: ) pauruṣeyāṇām ājñā dattā / bhavanto yāvān ayam āhāraḥ sarvam etat samantāt pṛthivyām ākirata iti / taiḥ sarvaṃ samantād ākīrṇam* / athāgnidatto brāhmaṇarājas tām eva rātriṃ śuci praṇītaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ samudānīya pūrvavad yāvad bhagavān purastād bhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ / yāvad anyatamena mahallena saṃjātāmarṣeṇāsmābhis traimāsīṃ koṭarayavāḥ paribhuktāḥ / idānīm ayaṃ kalirājo vibhavaṃ darśayatīti viditvā khādanīyabhojanīyasya pṛthivyām ākīrṇasyopari pārṣṇiprahāro dattaḥ / brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo 'vadhyāyanti kṣipanti vivācayanti / ārya khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ mukhābhyavahāryaṃ pādena spṛśanti / etat prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣavo bhagavata ārocayanti / bhagavān saṃlakṣa
children.translated_text: ) he gave orders to his servants: 'Good sirs, however much food there is, spread all of it evenly upon the ground.' They spread everything evenly. Then <s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king, that very night, having gathered pure, choice hard and soft foods, as before up to the <s>Bhagavān</s> being seated on a seat prepared before the assembly of monks. Then a certain senior monk, having become indignant — 'We have consumed husked barley for the three months; now this wicked king is displaying his wealth' — having known this, stamped his heel upon the hard and soft foods spread upon the ground. The <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders censured, criticized, and reproached him: 'Noble sir, they are treading with their feet upon food that is meant for the mouth.' The monks reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> reflect-
ed

ti / yaḥ kaścid ādīnavo
bhikṣavaḥ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ (

children.text: ) mukhābhyavahāryaṃ pādena spṛśantīti viditvā bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma / amukena bhikṣavo mahallabhikṣuṇā saṃjātāmarṣeṇa khādanīyabhojanīyasya mukhābhyavahāryasya pṛthivyām ākīrṇasyopari pārṣṇiprahāro datta iti / brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo 'vadhyāyanti kṣipanti

Having reflected, he addressed the monks: 'Such and such a senior monk, O monks, being indignant, stamped his heel upon the hard and soft foods that are meant for the mouth, spread upon the ground.' The <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders censure, criticize, and

body.translated_text: Then <s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king spoke thus to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> accept from me for life robes, almsfood, bedding and seats, and medicines and provisions for the sick, together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s>, O great king, was born in an age of short lifespan, and there is much to be done and accomplished, and the time of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> approaches.' He did not accept. 'If so, may the <s>Bhagavān</s> accept for seven years, seven months, seven days.' Even so, the <s>Bhagavān</s> did not accept. <s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king spoke thus to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> accept from me a meal tomorrow in my residence, together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> reflected: 'If I do not accept even a single meal from him, there is the possibility that <s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king will vomit hot (

Having in many ways instructed, inspired, encouraged, and gladdened him with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, he rose from his seat and departed. Then a number of monks, at the end of the three months of the rains-retreat, having finished making their robes, took up their bowls and robes and approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached and bowed their heads at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> feet, they stood to one
side.

body.translated_text: Then <s>Agnidatta</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-king, having ascertained that the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> was comfortably seated, served them with his own hands pure, choice hard and soft foods. As before, up to: with hands washed and bowls put away, having taken a lower seat, he sat before the <s>Bhagavān</s> to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. children.translated_text: arrived at the capital. Then, having filled their bowls with food accompanied by various soups and condiments, they went out. That <s>brāhmaṇa</s> saw them and asked: 'Good monks, let me see—what kind of alms-food have you obtained?' They showed it to him directly. Then, being envious by nature, with indignation aroused, he addressed the students: 'These shaven-headed little ascetics do not deserve to eat fine rice with various soups, condiments, and flavorings. They deserve to eat <s>koṭara</s>-barley (coarse barley husks).' They too approved: 'Indeed so, preceptor, indeed so. These shaven-headed little ascetics do not deserve to eat fine rice with various soups, condiments, and flavorings. They deserve to eat <s>koṭara</s>-barley.' But among them, two students were faithful, virtuous, and of good disposition. They said: 'Preceptor, do not speak thus! These are great beings who deserve to eat even celestial <s>sudhā</s> (ambrosia), not <s>koṭara</s>-barley.'

body.translated_text: In a former time, O monks, when the lifespan of people was eighty thousand years, a perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Vipaśyī</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He, attended by eighty thousand monks, was dwelling near the royal capital <s>Bandhumatī</s>. At that time, in the royal capital <s>Bandhumatī</s>, a certain <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who was a guild-teacher was teaching <s>Vedic</s> mantras to a group of five hundred <s>brāhmaṇa</s> students. He was exceedingly honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped, and regarded as worthy by all people. But from the moment the perfectly awakened <s>Vipaśyī</s> arrived at the royal capital <s>Bandhumatī</s>, no one honored him, revered him, esteemed him, or worshipped him. He saw this. He became exceedingly jealous of the <s>Tathāgata</s> and his <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples. Then a number of trainee and non-trainee monks, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken their bowls and robes, entered <s>Bandhumatī</s> (

And those two students who were faithful, virtuous, and of good disposition are none other than the monks <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>. Because I, in the presence of the trained and non-trained disciples of the perfectly awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, generated a defiled mind and uttered harsh speech, and because it was approved by the five hundred students less two, but not approved by those two—as the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> now ate <s>koṭara</s>-barley at <s>Vairaṃbhya</s>,

children.translated_text: for that purpose for which sons of good family, having shaved off their hair and beard and put on saffron robes, go forth from home to homelessness with perfect faith—that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life, I would in this very life realize by my own direct knowledge, attain, and declare: "Birth is exhausted, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done, I know there is nothing beyond this state of being."' When this was said, the <s>Bhagavān</s> looked toward the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> saw a great log of wood being carried by the current of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>. Having seen it, he addressed that monk: 'Do you see, monk, this great log of wood being carried by the current of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>?'
(MSV I 49)

children.text: ) / evaṃ bhadanta saced eṣa na pārime tīre saṃsrakṣyati / nāpārime tīre saṃsrakṣyati / na madhye saṃsrakṣyati / na sthale utpatsyati / na manuṣyagrāhyo bhaviṣyati / nāmanuṣyagrāhyaḥ / nāvartagrāhyaḥ / nāntaḥpūtībhāvaṃ gamiṣyati / evam eṣa bhikṣo dāruskandho 'nupūrveṇa samudranimno bhaviṣyati samudrapravaṇaḥ samudraprāgbhāraḥ / evam eva sacet tvaṃ bhikṣo na pārime tīre saṃsrakṣyasi / pūrvavad yāvat* / nāntaḥpūtībhāvaṃ gamiṣyasi / evaṃ hi tvaṃ bhikṣo anupūrveṇa nirvāṇanimno bhaviṣyasi nirvāṇapravaṇo nirvāṇaprāgbhāraḥ / nāhaṃ bhadanta jāne kim apārimaṃ tīraṃ kiṃ pārimaṃ tīram* / kiṃ madhye
children.translated_text: 'Yes, <s>Bhadanta</s>. If this log does not get caught on the far bank, nor on the near bank, nor run aground in the middle, nor be cast up on high ground, nor be seized by humans, nor seized by non-humans, nor caught in a whirlpool, nor rot internally—then, monk, this log will in due course tend toward the ocean, slope toward the ocean, incline toward the ocean. Even so, monk, if you do not get caught on the far bank, as before up to, nor rot internally—then you, monk, will in due course tend toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>, slope toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>, incline toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>.' 'I do not understand, <s>Bhadanta</s>, what is the far bank, what is the near bank, what is running aground in the middle,
what

body.translated_text: {Mark Allon 2003: Parallel see SN IV 179-181} There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Come, <s>Ānanda</s>, let us go to <s>Ayodhyā</s>.' 'Yes, <s>Bhadanta</s>,' the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, wandering on a journey through the Southern <s>Pāñcāla</s> country, arrived at <s>Ayodhyā</s> and dwelt in <s>Ayodhyā</s> on the bank of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>. Then a certain monk approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he paid homage at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet with his head and stood to one side. Standing to one side, that monk said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> teach me the <s>Dharma</s> in brief, so that I, having heard the <s>Dharma</s> in brief from the <s>Bhagavān</s>, may dwell alone, withdrawn, heedful, ardent, and resolute. Dwelling alone, withdrawn, heedful, ardent, and resolute,

Being seized by non-humans means, for example, someone here who lives the holy life with this aspiration: "By this morality, or by this vow,
or by this austerity,
or by this practice of the holy life, may I become
a <s>deva</s> (god)

children.text: devānyatamo veti / āvartagrāha iti yathāpīhaikaḥ śikṣāṃ pratyākhyāya hānāyāvartate / antaḥpūtībhāva iti yathāpīhaiko duḥśīlo bhavati pāpadharmā antaḥpūtir avasrutaḥ kaṣaṃvakajātaḥ śaṃkhasvarasamācāraḥ / aśramaṇaḥ śramaṇapratijño 'brahmacārī brahmacāripratijñaḥ / evaṃ hi sacet tvaṃ bhikṣo nāpārime tīre saṃsrakṣyasi pūrvavad yāvan nirvāṇaprāgbhāraḥ /
children.translated_text: or one among the <s>devas</s>." Being caught in a whirlpool means, for example, someone who, having renounced the training, turns back to decline. Rotting internally means, for example, someone here who is immoral, of evil character, internally rotten, oozing with corruption, of a nature that conceals, whose conduct resembles the sound of a conch—a non-ascetic claiming to be an ascetic, a non-celibate claiming to be celibate. Thus, monk, if you do not get caught on the far bank, as before up to: incline toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>.'

body.translated_text: 'The far bank, monk, is a designation for the six internal sense-bases. The near bank is a designation for the six external sense-bases. Running aground in the middle is a designation for <s>nandīrāga</s> (delight and passion). Being cast up on high ground is a designation for the conceit "I am" (<s>asmimāna</s>). Being seized by humans means, for example, someone here who dwells

body.text: atha sa bhikṣur bhagavato bhāṣitam abhinandyānumodya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ / atha sa bhikṣur bhagavatā anena dāruskandhopamenāvavādenāvavāditaḥ / eko vyapakṛṣṭo 'pramattaḥ ātāpī prahitātmā viharan yad arthaṃ kulaputrāḥ keśaśmaśrūṇy avatārya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇy ācchadya samyag eva śraddhayā agārād anagārikāṃ pravrajanti tad anuttaraṃ brahmacaryaparyavasānaṃ dṛṣṭa eva dharme svayam abhijñāya sākṣātkṛtvopasaṃpadya pravedayate kṣīṇā me jātir uṣitaṃ brahmacaryaṃ kṛtaṃ karaṇīyaṃ nāparam asmād bhavaṃ prajānāmīty ājñātavān* / sa āyuṣmān arhan babhūva suvimuktacittaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then that monk, having rejoiced in and approved of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words, paid homage at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet with his head and departed from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence. Then that monk, having been admonished by the <s>Bhagavān</s> with this admonition using the simile of the log, dwelling alone, withdrawn, heedful, ardent, and resolute—for that purpose for which sons of good family, having shaved off their hair and beard and put on saffron robes, go forth from home to homelessness with perfect faith—that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life, he in this very life realized by his own direct knowledge, attained, and declared: 'Birth is exhausted, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done, I know there is nothing beyond this state of being.' He was one who had attained full knowledge. That venerable one became an <s>arhat</s>, with mind fully liberated.

body.text: tena khalu samayena nando gopālako bhagavato nātidūre sthito 'bhūt* / daṇḍam avaṣṭabhya gāś cārayati / tena daṇḍenāvaṣṭabdho maṇḍūkaḥ saṃchidyamāneṣu carmasu mucyamāneṣu sandhiṣu cittam utpādayati yady ahaṃ kāyaṃ vā cālayeyaṃ vācaṃ vā niścārayeyaṃ syād atonidānaṃ nandasya gopālasya kathāvyākṣepam iti viditvā bhagavato 'ntike cittam abhiprasādya kālagataś cāturmahārājikeṣu deveṣūpapannaḥ /
body.translated_text: At that time, <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd was standing not far from the <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was tending cattle, leaning on his staff. A frog, crushed beneath that staff, with its skin being torn and its joints being separated, generated this thought: 'If I were to move my body or utter a sound, that would, on account of that, cause an interruption in the conversation of <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd.' Knowing this, having generated faith in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence, it died and was reborn among the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods.

body.text: atha nando gopālako daṇḍam ekānte upanikṣipya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / upsasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte 'sthāt* / ekāntasthito nando gopālako bhagavantam idam avocat* / ahaṃ bhadanta nāpārime tīre saṃsrakṣyāmi / na pārime tīre saṃsrakṣyāmi /
