'Even though, <s>Nanda</s>, the cows are young and have young calves and will know their own herds and will go to their own homesteads, nevertheless this is a duty of a cowherd—as is proper when one has accepted food and clothing from a master.'

body.translated_text: Then <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd set aside his staff, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>, paid homage at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet with his head, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'I, <s>Bhadanta</s>, will not get caught on the far bank, I will not get caught on the near bank,

body.text: atha nando gopālako bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ / tato bhayaṃ bhayam ity uccaiḥ śabdaṃ kurvāṇaḥ pradhāvitum ārabdhaḥ / antarmārge ātmīyaiḥ paṃcabhir gopālakaśatair dṛṣṭaḥ / te kathayanti / kasya bhayam iti / jātibhayaṃ jarābhayaṃ vyādhibhayaṃ maraṇabhayam iti / te 'pi tasya pṛṣṭhataḥ pradhāvitum ārabdhāḥ / tān dṛṣṭvā anye 'pi gopālakā aśvapālakās tṛṇahārakāḥ kāṣṭḥahārakāḥ pathājīvā utpathājīvāś ca manuṣyāḥ pradhāvitum ārabdhāḥ / ānupathikair dṛṣṭās tathā vikrośantaḥ pṛṣṭāḥ / kim etad bhavantaḥ / te kathayanti / bhayam* / kasya bhayam* / jātibhayaṃ jarābhayaṃ vyādhibhayaṃ maraṇabhayam* / śrutvā te 'pi nivṛttāḥ / yāvat karvaṭakasamīpaṃ saṃprāptāḥ / tataś cāsau karvaṭakanivāsī janakāyas taṃ mahāntaṃ janakāyaṃ dṛṣṭvā itaś cāmutaś ca santrastāḥ / kecin niṣpalāyitāḥ / kecid bhāṇḍaṃ gopāyanti / kecit sannahyāvasthitāḥ / apare vīrapuruṣās taiḥ pratyudgamya pṛṣṭāḥ / bhavantaḥ kim etad iti / te kathayanti / bhayam* / kasya bhayam* / jātibhayaṃ jarābhayaṃ vyādhibhayaṃ maraṇabhayam iti / tato 'sau karvaṭakanivāsī janakāyaḥ samāśvastaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd paid homage at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet with his head and departed from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence. Then crying out loudly 'Danger! Danger!' he began to run. On the way he was seen by his own five hundred cowherds. They asked: 'What is the danger?' 'The danger of birth, the danger of old age, the danger of sickness, the danger of death!' They too began to run after him. Seeing them, other cowherds, horse-keepers, grass-gatherers, wood-gatherers, those who live on the roads, and those who live off the roads also began to run. Fellow travelers seeing them crying out thus asked: 'What is this, good sirs?' They replied: 'Danger!' 'What danger?' 'The danger of birth, the danger of old age, the danger of sickness, the danger of death.' Having heard, they too turned back. They arrived near a market town. The townspeople, seeing that great multitude, became frightened in all directions. Some fled. Some guarded their goods. Some armed themselves and stood ready. Other brave men went out to meet them and asked: 'Good sirs, what is this?' They replied: 'Danger!' 'What danger?' 'The danger of birth, the danger of old age, the danger of sickness, the danger of death.' Thereupon the townspeople were reassured.

body.text: tena khalu samayenāyuṣmān śāriputras tasyām eva parṣadi sanniṣaṇṇo 'bhūt sannipatitaḥ / athāyuṣmān śāriputraś ciraprakrāntaṃ nandaṃ gopālakaṃ viditvā bhagavantam idam avocat* / kasmād bhadanta bhagavatā nando gopālakaḥ svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajitukāmaḥ punar apy agārāyodyojitaḥ / asthānam etac chāriputrānavakāśo yan nando gopālakaḥ punar api gṛhī agāram adhyāvatsyati sannidhikāraparibhoge (

children.translated_text: This is not possible. Now <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd, having returned the cows to their owners, will come back. That goal for the sake of which sons of good family, having shaved off hair and beard and donned saffron robes, go forth from the household life to homelessness with right faith — that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life — he will, in this very life, having directly known and realized it for himself, attain and declare: "Birth is exhausted for me, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, I know of no further existence beyond this."'

body.translated_text: At that time, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> was seated in that very assembly, having come together. Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, knowing that <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd had departed long ago, said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Why, Venerable Sir, did the <s>Bhagavān</s> send <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd, who wished to go forth in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, back to the householder's life?' 'It is impossible, <s>Śāriputra</s>, there is no occasion that <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd will again live as a householder in a home, enjoying sensual pleasures through the use of stored provisions.

body.text: athāpareṇa samayena nando gopālakaḥ svāmināṃ gā arpayitvā paṃcaśataparivāro yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / upsaṃkramya bhagavantam idam avocat* / arpitā me bhadanta svāmināṃ gāvaḥ / labheyāhaṃ bhadanta svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyām upasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvaṃ careyam (

Thus ordained, the venerable one, as before up to: became one whose mind was well-liberated.

body.translated_text: Then, at a later time, <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd, having returned the cows to their owners, came with a retinue of five hundred to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'I have returned the cows to their owners, Venerable Sir. May I, Venerable Sir, receive ordination, full ordination, and the status of a monk in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>? May I

body.text: dharmatā aciropapannasya devaputrasya devakanyāyā vā trīṇi cittāny utpadyante / kutaś cyutaḥ / kutropapannaḥ / kena karmaṇeti / maṇḍūkapūrvī devaputraḥ paśyati / tiryagbhyaś cyutaś cāturmahārājikeṣu deveṣūpapanno bhagavato 'ntike cittam abhiprasādyeti / tasyaitad abhavat* / na mama pratirūpaṃ syād yad ahaṃ paryuṣitaparivāso bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrameyam* / yanv aham aparyuṣitaparivāsa eva bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrameyam iti / atha maṇḍūkapūrvī devaputraś calavimalakuṇḍaladharaḥ pūrvavad yāvat sarvaṃ gaṃgātīram udāreṇāvabhāsenāvabhāsya bhagavantaṃ puṣpair (

children.translated_text: MSV I 54

children.text: ) avakīrya bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya / atha bhagavān maṇḍūkapūrviṇo devaputrasyāśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśīṃ caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavān* / yāṃ śrutvā pūrvavad yāvad anādikālopacitaṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* / abhikrānto 'haṃ bhadantābhikrāntaḥ / eṣo 'haṃ bhagavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi dharmaṃ ca bhikṣusaṃghaṃ ca / upāsakaṃ ca māṃ dhārayādyāgreṇa yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇopetaṃ śaraṇagatam abhiprasannam* / atha maṇḍūkapūrvī devaputro vaṇig iva labdhalābhaḥ śasyasampanna iva kārṣakaḥ śūra iva vijitasaṃgrāmaḥ sarvarogaparimukta ivāturo yayā vibhūtyā bhagavatsakāśam āgatas tayaiva vibhūtyā svabhavanaṃ gataḥ /
children.translated_text: and sat before the <s>Bhagavān</s> to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing the disposition, latent tendencies, nature, and temperament of the <s>devaputra</s> who had formerly been a frog, gave such a teaching on the <s>Dharma</s> as leads to the penetration of the Four Noble Truths. Having heard it, as before up to: having shattered with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the perishable aggregate (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) accumulated since beginningless time, he realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>). 'Excellent, Venerable Sir, excellent! I go to the <s>Bhagavān</s> for refuge, to the <s>Dharma</s>, and to the <s>Bhikṣusaṃgha</s>. May he accept me as a lay follower (<s>upāsaka</s>), from this day forth for as long as I live, one who has taken refuge and is filled with faith.' Then the <s>devaputra</s> who had formerly been a frog, like a merchant who has obtained profit, like a farmer whose crops are abundant, like a hero who has won a battle, like a sick person freed from all disease, returned to his own abode with the same splendor with which he had come to the <s>Bhagavān's</s> presence.

body.translated_text: It is the nature of things that when a <s>devaputra</s> (son of the gods) or <s>devakanyā</s> (daughter of the gods) is newly reborn, three thoughts arise: 'From where have I passed away? Where have I been reborn? By what <s>karma</s>?' The <s>devaputra</s> who had formerly been a frog saw: 'I passed away from the animal realm and have been reborn among the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods, having generated faith in the <s>Bhagavān's</s> presence.' He thought: 'It would not be proper for me to approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> after my retreat period has elapsed. Let me approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> for an audience while my retreat period has not yet elapsed.' Then the <s>devaputra</s> who had formerly been a frog, wearing trembling, bright earrings, as before up to: illuminating the entire bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> with a magnificent radiance, showered the <s>Bhagavān</s> with flowers

body.text: bhikṣavaḥ pūrvāpararātraṃ jāgarikāyogam anuyuktā viharanti / tair dṛṣṭo bhagavato 'ntike udāro 'vabhāsaḥ / yaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃdigdhā bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ / kiṃ bhagavann imāṃ rātriṃ bhagavantaṃ darśanāya brahmā sahāṃpatiḥ śakro devendraś catvāro lokapālā upasaṃkrāntāḥ / na bhikṣavo brahmā sahāṃpatir na śakro devendro na catvāro lokapālā māṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāntāḥ / api tu nandena gopālena daṇḍena vāvaṣṭabdho maṇḍūkaḥ sa cchidyamāneṣu carmasu mucyamāneṣu sandhiṣu mā nandasya gopālakasya dharmavikṣepo bhaviṣyatīti niścalas tūṣṇīm avasthito mamāntike cittam abhiprasādya kālagataś cāturmahārājikeṣu deveṣūpapannaḥ / sa imāṃ rātriṃ matsakāśam upasaṃkrāntaḥ / tasya mayā dharmo deśitaḥ / dṛṣṭasatyaś ca svabhavanaṃ gata iti /
body.translated_text: The monks, devoted to the practice of wakefulness in the first and last watches of the night, saw a magnificent radiance in the <s>Bhagavān's</s> presence. Having seen it, they were filled with doubt and asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Did <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, <s>Śakra</s> lord of the gods, or the four world-guardians come to see the <s>Bhagavān</s> this night?' 'No, monks, neither <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, nor <s>Śakra</s> lord of the gods, nor the four world-guardians came to see me. Rather, a frog, pressed down by <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd's staff, while its skin was being torn and its joints dislocated — thinking "Let there be no disturbance of the <s>Dharma</s> for <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd" — remained motionless and silent, generated faith in my presence, died, and was reborn among the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods. He came to my presence this night. I taught him the <s>Dharma</s>. He saw the truths and returned to his own abode.'

body.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ / kiṃ bhadanta nandena gopālena paṃcaśataparivāreṇa karma kṛtaṃ yena gopālakeṣūpapanno bhagavataś ca śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ (

children.text: ) sākṣātkṛtam* / maṇḍūkapūrviṇā devaputreṇa kiṃ karma kṛtaṃ yena maṇḍūkeṣūpapannaḥ satyadarśanaṃ ca kṛtam iti / bhagavān āha / tenaiva bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pūrvavad yāvat phalanti khalu dehinām* /
children.translated_text: And what <s>karma</s> did the <s>devaputra</s> who had formerly been a frog perform, that he was reborn among frogs and then attained the seeing of the truths?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Those very <s>karmas</s>, O monks, were performed and accumulated by them, their requisites gathered — as before up to: indeed, they bear fruit for embodied beings.'

body.translated_text: The monks, having doubts, asked the <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s>, who resolves all doubts: 'What <s>karma</s>, Venerable Sir, did <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd with his retinue of five hundred perform, that he was reborn among cowherds, and having gone forth in the <s>Bhagavān's</s> teaching, through the abandonment of all afflictions, realized <s>arhatva</s> (arhatship)?

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavaḥ asminn eva bhadrake kalpe viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loke udapādi / pūrvavad yāvat sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upanisṛtya viharati ṛṣivadane mṛgadāve / tasya pravacane nando gopālakaḥ pravrajitaḥ / tripiṭo dhārmakathiko yuktamuktapratibhānaḥ paṃcaśataparivāraḥ adhikaraṇakuśalaḥ / sa utpannotpannāni saṃghasyādhikaraṇāni vyupaśamayati / tatra dvau bhikṣū stabdhau māninau / na kadācit tasya sakāśam upasaṃkrāmataḥ / tayor apareṇa samayena parasparam adhikaraṇam utpannam* / tāv arthārthinau tasya sakāśam upasaṃkrāntau pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā kathayataḥ / idaṃ cedaṃ cāvayor adhikaraṇam utpannaṃ vyupaśamayeti / sa saṃlakṣayati / yady aham anayor adyaivādhikaraṇaṃ vyupaśamayiṣyāmi arthārthināv etau na bhūya upasaṃkramiṣyataḥ / tena sarvasaṃghaṃ saṃnipātya tad adhikaraṇaṃ saṃghamadhye upanikṣipya na ekāntīkṛtam* / ataḥ parasminn api divase tasya karvaṭake karaṇīyam utpannam* / sa (

children.translated_text: MSV I 56

children.text: ) tatra gataḥ / tatas tābhyāṃ cirayatīti saṃghaṃ saṃnipātya tad adhikaraṇam upanikṣiptam* / tataḥ saṃghena vyupaśamitam* / yāvad asau tripiṭo bhikṣus tasmāt karvaṭakād āgataḥ / mārgaśrame prativinodite sārdhaṃvihāryantevāsikān pṛcchati / na tāv arthapratyarthikāv āgacchata iti / te kathayanti / upādhyāya vyupaśāntaṃ tayos tad adhikaraṇam* / kena vyupaśamitam* / saṃghena / yathākathaṃ tair vistareṇa samākhyātam* / tena kharaṃ vākkarma niścāritam* / jñāyate āyuṣmanto gopālakair yathā tad adhikaraṇaṃ vyupaśamitam iti / tair apy anusaṃvarṇitam eva me tad upādhyāya gopālakair yathā tad adhikaraṇaṃ vyupaśamitam iti /
children.translated_text: He went there. Then those two, thinking he was delayed, convened the <s>Saṃgha</s> and placed the dispute before it. The <s>Saṃgha</s> then settled it. When that <s>tripiṭaka</s> monk returned from that village, after recovering from the fatigue of travel, he asked his co-residents and pupils: 'Did those two disputants not come?' They replied: 'Teacher, that dispute of theirs has been settled.' 'By whom was it settled?' 'By the <s>Saṃgha</s>.' 'How so?' They recounted it to him in detail. Then he uttered harsh speech: 'Do the venerable ones know how cowherds settle that dispute?' They too praised it in exactly the same way: 'It was settled by the cowherds in just the way our teacher described.'

body.translated_text: In a former time, O monks, in this very auspicious <s>kalpa</s> (aeon), when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, a perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — as before up to: he dwelt near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at the Deer Park in <s>Ṛṣivadana</s>. In his dispensation, <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd had gone forth. He was a master of the three baskets (<s>tripiṭaka</s>), a <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, of ready and apt eloquence, with a retinue of five hundred, skilled in disputes. He would settle disputes of the <s>Saṃgha</s> as they arose. There were two monks who were stiff-necked and proud. They would never approach him. At a later time, a dispute arose between those two. Being desirous of settling it, they approached him, paid homage at his feet, and said: 'Such and such a dispute has arisen between us; please settle it.' He reflected: 'If I settle their dispute today, being desirous of settlement, they will never approach me again.' So he convened the entire <s>Saṃgha</s>, placed that dispute before the assembly, but did not settle it conclusively. On the following day as well, an obligation arose for him in a village.

body.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tripiṭo bhikṣur eṣa evāsau nando gopālakas tena kālena tena samayena / yāny asya tāni paṃca sārdhaṃvihāryantevāsikānāṃ śatāni etāny eva paṃca gopālakaśatāni / yad anena kāśyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya śrāvakasaṃgho gopālakavādena samudācaritaḥ sārdhaṃvihāryantevāsikaiś cānusaṃvarṇitaṃ tasya karmaṇo vipākena paṃca janmaśatāni paṃcaśataparivāro gopālakeṣūpapannaḥ / yāvad etarhy api paṃcaśataparivāro gopālakeṣv evopapannaḥ / yad anena paṭhitaṃ svādhyāyitaṃ skandhakauśalaṃ dhātukauśalam āyatanakauśalaṃ sthānāsthānakauśalaṃ ca kṛtaṃ tenaitarhi paṃcaśataparivāreṇa mama śāsane pravrajya (

children.translated_text: through the abandonment of all afflictions, he has realized <s>arhatva</s> (arhatship).

body.translated_text: What do you think, O monks? That <s>tripiṭaka</s> monk was none other than this <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd at that time and on that occasion. And his five hundred co-residents and pupils were these very five hundred cowherds. Because he addressed the <s>Śrāvaka-saṃgha</s> of the perfectly awakened <s>Kāśyapa</s> with the epithet 'cowherds,' and because his co-residents and pupils concurred, as the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, for five hundred births he was reborn among cowherds with a retinue of five hundred. Even now he has been reborn among cowherds with a retinue of five hundred. But because he studied, recited, acquired skill in the aggregates, skill in the elements, skill in the sense-bases, and skill in what is possible and impossible, therefore now, with his retinue of five hundred, having gone forth in my teaching,

body.text: maṇḍūkapūrvy api devaputraḥ kāśyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya pravacane bhikṣur āsīt* / prāhāṇikaḥ sa janapadacārikāṃ caran anyatamasmin karvaṭake vihāram anuprāptaḥ / sa rātryāḥ prathame yāme paryaṅkaṃ baddhvā (

children.translated_text: he began to direct his attention. Meanwhile, monks who were reciters were reciting their texts. Meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>) are vulnerable to the thorn of sound. Due to the noise, he could not attain one-pointedness of mind. He reflected: 'These are reciting now. I shall sit in meditation during the middle watch.' He rose during the middle watch and sat down, but other monks were reciting. He reflected: 'I shall sit during the last watch.' He rose during the last watch and sat down, but still others were reciting. Since he was not free from passion, an intense affliction arose in him. He said: 'These <s>Kāśyapa</s> ascetics croak like frogs the entire night!'

body.translated_text: The <s>devaputra</s> who had formerly been a frog was also a monk in the dispensation of the perfectly awakened <s>Kāśyapa</s>. He was devoted to the practice of striving. Wandering on a tour through the countryside, he arrived at a <s>vihāra</s> in a certain town. During the first watch of the night, having sat cross-legged,

body.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau prāhāṇiko bhikṣur eṣa evāsau maṇḍūkapūrvī devaputraḥ / yad anena kāśyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya śrāvakā maṇḍūkavādena samudācaritāḥ / tasya karmaṇo vipākena paṃca janmaśatāni maṇḍūkeṣūpapanno yāvad etarhy api maṇḍūkeṣv evopapannaḥ / yan mamāntike cittaṃ prasāditaṃ tena cāturmahārājikeṣu deveṣūpapannaḥ / yat kāśyape samyaksaṃbuddhe brahmacaryaṃ caritaṃ tenedānīṃ satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam* / iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ pūrvavad yāvad ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam idam avocat* /
body.translated_text: What do you think, O monks? That monk devoted to striving was none other than this <s>devaputra</s> who had formerly been a frog. Because he addressed the disciples of the perfectly awakened <s>Kāśyapa</s> with the epithet 'frogs,' as the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, for five hundred births he was reborn among frogs, and even now he has been reborn among frogs. But because he generated faith in my presence, he was reborn among the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods. And because he practiced the holy life under the perfectly awakened <s>Kāśyapa</s>, he has now attained the seeing of the truths. Therefore, O monks, the ripening of exclusively dark <s>karmas</s> is exclusively dark — as before up to: effort must be made. Thus should you train, O monks.' This he said.

body.text: atha bhagavān nadīṃ gaṃgām avatīrṇas tatra paṃcabhir haṃsamatsyakūrmaśataiḥ parivṛtaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtaś ca / teṣāṃ bhagavatā tribhiḥ padair dharmaḥ (

children.translated_text: MSV I 58

children.text: ) deśitaḥ / iti hi bhadramukhāḥ sarvasaṃskārā anityāḥ / sarvadharmā anātmānaḥ / śāntaṃ nirvāṇam* / mamāntike cittam abhiprasādayata / apy evaṃ tiryagyoniṃ virāgayiṣyatheti / teṣām etad abhavat* / nāsmākaṃ pratirūpaṃ syād yad vayaṃ bhagavato 'ntikāt tribhiḥ padair dharmaṃ śrutvā āhāram āharema iti / te nāharaṇāṃ pratipannāḥ / tīkṣṇas tiryayonigatānām agniś cyutaḥ / kālagatāś cāturmahārājikeṣu deveṣūpapannāḥ / dharmatā khalv aciropapannasya devaputrasya vā devakanyāyā vā trīṇi cittāny utpadyante / kutaś cyutaḥ / kutropapannaḥ / kena karmaṇā iti / te paśyanti / tiryagbhyaś cyutāḥ / cāturmahārājikeṣu deveṣūpapannāḥ / pūrvavad yāvan mandārakāṇāṃ puṣpāṇām utsaṃgaṃ pūrayitvā bhagavatsāmantakena nadīṃ gaṃgām avabhāsya bhagavantaṃ puṣpair ākīrya bhagavatsāmantakenānuparivāryāvasthitāḥ / bhagavatā teṣām āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā pūrvavad (
children.translated_text: ) was taught. 'Thus, O noble ones, all conditioned things are impermanent. All phenomena are without self. <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is peace. Generate faith in my presence; thus you will become free from passion toward rebirth in the animal realm.' They thought: 'It would not be proper for us, having heard the <s>Dharma</s> in three verses from the <s>Bhagavān</s>, to consume food.' They undertook the practice of non-eating. The fire of those born in the animal realm is fierce; they died and were reborn among the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> (Four Great Kings') gods. For it is the natural law that when a god-son or god-daughter is newly reborn, three thoughts arise: 'From where have I died? Where have I been reborn? By what <s>karma</s>?' They saw: 'We died from the animal realm and have been reborn among the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods.' As before, up to: having filled their laps with <s>mandāraka</s> flowers, illuminating the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> in the <s>Bhagavān's</s> vicinity, showering the <s>Bhagavān</s> with flowers, and standing nearby attending on the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing their disposition, latent tendencies, temperament, and nature, gave such a teaching leading to the penetration of the Four Noble Truths, as before (

children.text: ) yāvad anādikālopacitaṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* / te dṛṣṭasatyāḥ kathayanti / abhikrāntā vayaṃ bhadantābhikrāntāḥ / ete vayaṃ buddhaṃ śaraṇam gacchāmo dharmaṃ ca bhikṣusaṃghaṃ ca / upāsakāṃś cāsmān dhāraya / adyāgreṇa yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇopetaṃ śaraṇagatān abhiprasannān* / atha te (
children.translated_text: ) up to: having shattered with the vajra of knowledge the mountain of the view of the personal self accumulated since beginningless time, they directly realized the fruit of stream-entry. Having seen the truths, they said: 'We are blessed, Venerable Sir, blessed! We go for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks. Accept us as lay followers from this day forth, for as long as we live, endowed with life, who have gone for refuge and have faith.' Then those (

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> descended into the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>. There he was surrounded and circumambulated by five hundred geese, fish, and turtles each. The <s>Bhagavān</s> taught them the <s>Dharma</s> in three verses.

body.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ / kiṃ bhadanta ebhir haṃsakacchapamatsyaiḥ karma kṛtaṃ yena haṃsakacchapamatsyeṣūpapannāḥ satyadarśanaṃ ca kṛtam iti / bhagavān āha / ebhir eva bhikṣavo haṃsamatsyakacchapaiḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni pūrvavad yāvat phalanti khalu dehinām* /
body.translated_text: The monks, having doubts, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, who resolves all doubts: 'Venerable Sir, what <s>karma</s> did these geese, turtles, and fish perform that they were reborn as geese, turtles, and fish, and yet attained the seeing of the truths?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'These very geese, fish, and turtles, O monks, performed and accumulated <s>karmas</s>, their requisites gathered, their conditions ripened—as before up to: indeed they bear fruit for embodied beings.'

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavaḥ asminn eva bhadrake kalpe viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kaśyapo nāma śāstā loke udapādi pūrvavad yāvat sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśṛtya viharati ṛṣivadane mṛgadāve / tasyaite śāsane pravrajitā abhūvan* / tatraitebhir bhikṣubhiḥ kṣudrānukṣudrāṇi śikṣāpadāni khaṇḍitāni / tasya karmaṇo vipākena haṃsamatsyakūrmeṣūpapannāḥ / yan mamāntike cittam abhiprasāditaṃ tena deveṣūpapannāḥ / yat kāśyape samyaksaṃbuddhe brahmacaryaṃ caritaṃ tena satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam* / iti hi bhikṣavaḥ ekāṇtakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ pūrvavad yāvad ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam idam avocat* /
body.translated_text: In a former time, O monks, in this very auspicious <s>kalpa</s> (aeon), when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, a teacher named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world—as before up to: he dwelt near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> at <s>Ṛṣivadana</s> in the Deer Park. These had gone forth in his dispensation. These monks violated the minor and subsidiary training rules. As the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, they were reborn among geese, fish, and turtles. Because they generated faith in my presence, they were reborn among the gods. Because they practiced the holy life under the perfectly awakened <s>Kāśyapa</s>, they attained the seeing of the truths. Thus, O monks, for actions that are entirely black, the ripening is entirely black—as before up to: effort should be made. 'Thus, O monks, you should train yourselves.' This he spoke.

body.text: atha bhagavān nadīṃ gaṃgām uttīrṇaḥ paṃcamātraiḥ pretaśataiḥ parivṛto dagdhasthūṇākṛtibhir asthiyantravaducchritaiḥ svakeśasaṃchannaiḥ parvatopamakukṣibhiḥ sūcīcchidropamamukhair ādīptaiḥ pradīptaiḥ saṃprajvalitaiḥ (

The <s>Bhagavān</s> pointed out the <s>Gaṅgā</s> to them:

We see it filled with blood and filth; and guards with axes and clubs in hand protect it.'

body.translated_text: 'For us this <s>Bhāgīrathī</s> flows with dried-up water,

nāhaṃ bhayān na puruṣād api vā janasya

'It is not out of fear, nor because of any person,

body.text: tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanam āmaṃtrayate / saṃtarpaya maudgalyāyana pretān iti / evaṃ bhadanta iti āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya pretān santarpayitum ārabdhaḥ / tatra pretāḥ sūcīmukhatvān na śaknuvanti mukhaṃ vivartayitum* / tato bhagavatā teṣām ṛddhyā mukhaṃ vivṛtam* / āyuṣmatā mahāmaudgalyāyanena pānīyaṃ dattam* / tais tṛṣāturaiḥ prabhūtaṃ pītam* / udarāṇi sphuṭitāni / tato bhagavato 'ntike cittam abhiprasādya kālagatāḥ / pūrvavad dṛṣṭasatyāḥ svabhavanaṃ gatāḥ /
body.translated_text: There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'Satisfy the <s>pretas</s>, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>.' 'Yes, Venerable Sir,' the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s> and began to satisfy the <s>pretas</s>. But the <s>pretas</s>, because of their needle-like mouths, could not open their mouths. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> opened their mouths by supernatural power. The venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> gave them water. Being tormented by thirst, they drank abundantly. Their bellies burst. Then, having generated faith in the <s>Bhagavān's</s> presence, they died. As before, having seen the truths, they went to their own abodes.

body.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ / kiṃ bhadanta ebhiḥ pretaiḥ karma kṛtaṃ yena preteṣūpapannāḥ / kiṃ karma kṛtaṃ yena deveṣūpapannāḥ / satyadarśanaṃ ca kṛtam iti / bhagavān āha / ebhir eva bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pūrvavad yāvat phalanti dehināṃ* /
body.translated_text: The monks, having doubts, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, who resolves all doubts: 'Venerable Sir, what <s>karma</s> did these <s>pretas</s> perform that they were reborn as <s>pretas</s>? What <s>karma</s> did they perform that they were reborn among the gods? And they attained the seeing of the truths?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'These very beings, O monks, performed and accumulated <s>karmas</s>, their requisites gathered—as before up to: indeed they bear fruit for embodied beings.'

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavaḥ asminn eva bhadrake kalpe viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kaśyapo nāma śāstā loke udapādi pūrvavad yāvat sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśṛtya viharati ṛṣivadane mṛgadāve / tasya śrāvakāc chandakabhikṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā buddhadharmasaṃgheṣu kārān kurvanti / yadā bhagavataḥ kāśyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya śāsanaṃ na vaistārikaṃ (

children.translated_text: ) there were few soliciting monks. But when it became widespread, then many soliciting monks arose. Eventually, in a certain assembly hall, five hundred lay followers had gathered and assembled for some purpose. Many soliciting monks approached them, wishing to inspire them. Those lay followers, overcome by intense irritation, uttered harsh speech: 'These <s>Kāśyapīya</s> (followers of Kāśyapa) ascetics, like beings reborn as <s>pretas</s>, constantly extend their hands!'

body.translated_text: In a former time, O monks, in this very auspicious <s>kalpa</s>, when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, a teacher named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world—as before up to: he dwelt near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> at <s>Ṛṣivadana</s> in the Deer Park. From his disciples they begged food by solicitation, and performed services for the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>. When the dispensation of the <s>Bhagavān Kāśyapa</s>, the perfectly awakened one, was not yet widespread, (

body.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yāni tāni paṃcopāsakaśatāni etāny eva tāni paṃca pretaśatāni / yad ebhiḥ kāśyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya śrāvakāḥ pretavādena samudācaritās tasya karmaṇo vipākena paṃca janmaśatāni preteṣūpapannāḥ / yāvad etarhy api preteṣv evopapannāḥ / yan mamāntike cittaṃ prasāditaṃ tena deveṣūpapannāḥ / yat kāśyape samyaksaṃbuddhe śaraṇāgamanaśikṣāpadāni gṛhītāni tena satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam* / iti hi bhikṣavaḥ ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ pūrvavad yāvad ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam idam avocat* /
body.translated_text: What do you think, O monks? Those five hundred lay followers were none other than these five hundred <s>pretas</s>. Because they addressed the disciples of the perfectly awakened <s>Kāśyapa</s> with the epithet '<s>preta</s>,' as the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, they were reborn as <s>pretas</s> for five hundred lifetimes, and even now they have been reborn as <s>pretas</s>. Because they generated faith in my presence, they were reborn among the gods. Because they had taken the refuges and training rules under the perfectly awakened <s>Kāśyapa</s>, they attained the seeing of the truths. Thus, O monks, for actions that are entirely black, the ripening is entirely black—as before up to: effort should be made. 'Thus, O monks, you should train yourselves.' This he spoke.

body.text: atha bhagavān nadīṃ gaṃgām uttīrya dakṣiṇena nāgāvalokitena nadīṃ gaṃgāṃ nirīkṣate / bhikṣavo buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ / kimarthaṃ bhadanta (

children.translated_text: ) does the <s>Bhagavān</s> turn around and look at the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: '(

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having crossed the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, looked back at the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> with a southward elephant-glance. The monks asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'For what reason, Venerable Sir, (

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavaḥ piṇḍavaṃśo nāma rājā babhūva / dhārmiko dharmarājo dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayati / tasya janapadā ṛddhāś ca sphītāś ca kṣemāś ca subhikṣāś cākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyāś ca sadā puṣpaphalavṛkṣāḥ devaḥ kālavarṣī / śasyavatī vasumatī praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamarataskararogāpagatā / manuṣyā nityaṃ dharmaparāyaṇāḥ / yāvad asau rājā saṃprāpte vasantakālasamaye saṃpuṣpiteṣu pādapeṣu haṃsakrauṃcamayūraśukaśārikākokilajīvaṃjīvakanirghoṣite vanaṣaṇḍe antaḥpuraparivṛta udyānabhūmiṃ saṃprasthitaḥ / yāvad anyatamaḥ puruṣo valīpalitottamāṃgaḥ {MS

children.text: } pūrvavad yāvad daṇḍam avaṣṭabhya gacchatīti / taiḥ samākhyātam* / deva saṃskāraparikṣayād eṣa jīrṇo vṛddha ity ucyata iti / rājā kathayati / aham api bhavanta evaṃdharmo bhaviṣyāmīti / te kathayanti / deva sādhāraṇa eṣa dharma iti / tato rājā durmanāḥ saṃprasthitaḥ / punar api puruṣaṃ paśyaty utpāṇḍotpāṇḍukaṃ sphuṭitaparuṣagātraṃ parvatopamakukṣiṃ vraṇapūyotkīrṇair aṅgapratyaṅgāvadhāribhiḥ paṭṭakopanibaddhaiḥ dīrghadīrghaiḥ praśvasantan daṇḍam avaṣṭabhya khaṃjamānagatiṃ saṃprasthitaṃ dṛṣṭvā (
children.translated_text: } as before up to, going along leaning on a stick?' They informed him: 'Your Majesty, due to the exhaustion of conditioned things, he is called old and aged.' The king said: 'Will I too, good sirs, become subject to such a condition?' They replied: 'Your Majesty, this is a condition common to all.' Then the king proceeded in low spirits. Again he saw a man—extremely pale, with rough and cracked limbs, with a belly like a mountain, with limbs and extremities bearing wounds oozing pus, bound with bandages, breathing in long gasps, going along with a limping gait leaning on a stick. Having seen him, (

children.text:
) ca punar amātyān āmaṃtrayate / ka eṣa bhavantaḥ puruṣa utpāṇḍotpāṇḍukaḥ pūrvavad yāvat khaṃjamāno 'bhisaṃprasthita iti / te kathayanti / deva eṣa vyādhito nāma / rājā kathayati / aham api bhavantaḥ evaṃdharmo bhaviṣyāmīti / amātyāḥ kathayanti / deva sādhāraṇa eṣa eva dharmo duṣkṛtakarmakāriṇāṃ pūrvakarmāparādhād bhavatīti / rājā saṃlakṣayati / sarvathā pāpaṃ na kartavyam iti viditvā saṃprasthitaḥ / punar api paśyati / nīlapītalohitāvadātair vastraiḥ śivikām alaṃkṛtāṃ chatradhvajapatākāśaṃkhapaṭahastrīpuruṣadārakadārikābhir
ākīrṇāṃ caturbhiḥ puruṣair utkṣiptām ulkāṃ ca purastān nīyamānāṃ kāṣṭhavyagrahastaiḥ puruṣaiḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nubaddhāṃ hā tāta hā bhrātaḥ hā pitaḥ hā svāminn iti ca samantād ārodanaśabdaṃ śrutvā ca punar amātyān āmaṃtrayate / kim eṣā bhavantaḥ śivikā nīlapītalohitāvadātair vastraiḥ pūrvavad yāvad ārodanaśabda iti / amātyāḥ kathayanti / eṣa deva mṛto nāma iti / rājā kathayati / aham api bhavantaḥ evaṃdharmo bhaviṣyāmīti (
children.translated_text: ) And he again addressed his ministers: 'Who is this person, good sirs, pale and sallow?' — as before up to — 'limping along?' They replied: 'Your Majesty, this is what is called a sick person.' The king said: 'I too, good sirs, will become subject to this very condition.' The ministers replied: 'Your Majesty, this is a condition common to all; it befalls those who have performed evil deeds, as a consequence of former <s>karma</s>.' The king reflected: 'By all means, evil should not be done.' Having ascertained this, he continued on. Again he saw a bier adorned with cloths of blue, yellow, red, and white, crowded with umbrellas, banners, flags, conch-shells, drums, men, women, boys, and girls, carried aloft by four men, with a torch being borne ahead, and followed behind by people with firebrands in their hands. Having heard the sound of wailing all around — 'Alas, father! Alas, brother! Alas, dear one! Alas, master!' — he again addressed his ministers: 'What is this bier, good sirs, adorned with cloths of blue, yellow, red, and white?' — as before up to — 'sound of wailing?' The ministers replied: 'This, Your Majesty, is what is called a dead person.' The king said: 'I too, good sirs, will become subject to this very condition.' (

children.text: ) / te kathayanti deva eṣo 'pi sādhāraṇo dharma iti / tato jīrṇāturamṛtasaṃdarśanāt saṃvignamanā evaṃrūpābhogāḥ parityaktavyā iti pratinivṛtya śokāgāraṃ praviśyāvasthita iti /
children.translated_text: ) They replied: 'Your Majesty, this too is a condition common to all.' Then, his mind filled with urgency from seeing the aged, the sick, and the dead, thinking 'Pleasures of this sort must be relinquished,' he turned back and, entering the chamber of grief, remained there.

body.translated_text: In a former time, O monks, there was a king named <s>Piṇḍavaṃśa</s>. He was righteous, a king of <s>Dharma</s>, ruling his kingdom by <s>Dharma</s>. His territories were prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, and teeming with many people; the trees always bore flowers and fruits; the rains fell in season; the earth was rich in grain and wealth; strife, quarrels, disputes, tumults, thieves, and diseases had departed; and the people were always devoted to <s>Dharma</s>. When the spring season arrived, the trees were in bloom, and the forest groves resounded with the calls of geese, cranes, peacocks, parrots, mynahs, cuckoos, and <s>jīvaṃjīvaka</s> birds, that king, surrounded by his inner court, set out for the pleasure grounds. Then a certain man, with head covered in wrinkles and grey hair, {MS

body.text: tasya vijite velāmo nāma brāhmaṇa āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vedavedāṃgapāragaḥ / tena śrutaṃ yathā rājā jīrṇāturamṛtasaṃdarśanād udvignaḥ śokāgāraṃ praviśyāvasthita iti / śrutvā ca punar anekair brāhmaṇaśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ sarvaśvetaṃ vaḍavāratham (

children.translated_text: MSV I 65

children.text: ) abhiruhya sauvarṇena daṇḍakamaṇḍalunā dhāryamāṇena yena rājā piṇḍavaṃśas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / amātyaiḥ rājñe niveditam* / deva velāmo brāhmaṇo dvāre tiṣṭhati / tato rājā nirgatya athādhikaraṇe niṣaṇṇaḥ / brāhmaṇo velāmo jayenāyuṣā ca vardhayitvā niṣaṇṇaḥ kathayati / kimarthaṃ devaḥ śokāgāre praviśyāvasthita iti / rājñā yathāvṛttaṃ sarvaṃ velāmāya brāhmaṇāya vistareṇārocitam* / sa kathayati / devaḥ svakarmaphalabhogī / nātra śokaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / santi satvāḥ sukṛtakarmakāriṇaḥ santi duṣkṛtakarmakāriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: ), with a golden staff and water-vessel being carried before him, he approached king <s>Piṇḍavaṃśa</s>. The ministers informed the king: 'Your Majesty, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Velāma</s> stands at the gate.' Then the king went out and sat at the tribunal. The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Velāma</s>, having wished him victory and long life, sat down and said: 'For what reason has Your Majesty entered the chamber of grief and remained there?' The king reported to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Velāma</s> everything that had happened in detail. He replied: 'Your Majesty is one who experiences the fruit of his own <s>karma</s>. There is no cause for grief here. There are beings who perform meritorious deeds and there are beings who perform evil deeds,
and there are those who perform both kinds of deeds.

children.text: / cakravartinas tu nityaṃ sukṛtakarmakāriṇaḥ santo deveṣūpapadyante / devo 'pi cakravartī / manuṣyaprativiṣiṣṭaṃ sukham anubhūya divyaṃ sukham anubhaviṣyatīti / api tu deva yajña iṣṭavyaḥ svargasopānabhūta iti / tato rājñā amātyānām ājñā dattā / bhavantaḥ sarvavijite ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kārayata / rājā nirarga
children.translated_text: <s>Cakravartins</s> (universal monarchs), however, being always performers of meritorious deeds, are reborn among the gods. Your Majesty is also a <s>Cakravartin</s>. Having experienced human happiness surpassing that of ordinary humans, you will experience divine happiness.' 'Moreover, Your Majesty, a sacrifice should be performed — it is the stairway to heaven.' Thereupon the king gave orders to his ministers: 'Good sirs, have a bell proclamation made throughout the entire realm: "The king is performing an unobstructed sacrifice. You should come and partake."' Then a hall of generosity was established: 'Let food be given to those who seek food; drink to those who seek drink.' There, by the overflow of rinsing-water, a pit was formed where what was hot became cool. 'Cool, cool,' thus the name <s>Anavatapta</s> ('unfevered') arose. As the pit continued to fill over twelve years with rinsing-water and rice-water, it grew larger. Then a river flowed from its mouth. The name '<s>Ācāma</s>-river' (rinsing-water river) arose.

children.text: ṃ yajñaṃ yajati / bhavadbhir āgatya paribhoktavyam iti / tato dānaśālā prajñaptā / annam annārthibhyo dīyatāṃ pānaṃ pānārthibhyaḥ / tatrācāmena parisravamāṇena gartaḥ kṛtaḥ / yatrāsau taptaḥ śītībhavati / anavataptaḥ anavatapta iti sajñā saṃvṛttā / tasyācāmena taṇḍulāmbunā ca dvādaśavārṣikeṇa saṃpūryamāṇasya vṛddhiḥ saṃvṛttā / tata iyaṃ mukhena nadī prasṛtā / ācāmanadīti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā iti /

body.translated_text: In his domain, there was a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Velāma</s>, wealthy, of great riches, of great resources, who had mastered the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Vedāṅgas</s>. He heard that the king, being distressed from seeing the aged, the sick, and the dead, had entered the chamber of grief and remained there. Having heard this, attended by many hundreds of thousands of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, mounting an all-white mare-drawn chariot (

<s>Sālabālā</s>, <s>Sālibālā</s>, <s>Suvarṇaprastha</s>, and <s>Sāketā</s>,

body.text: atha bhagavān kumāravardhanam anuprāptaḥ / kumāravardhane āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate / asminn evānanda pradeśe upoṣadho nāma rājā jātaḥ / atraiva cābhivṛddhaḥ / tenāsya nagarasya kumāravardhanaṃ kumāravardhanam iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> arrived at <s>Kumāravardhana</s>. In <s>Kumāravardhana</s>, he addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'In this very place, <s>Ānanda</s>, a king named <s>Upoṣadha</s> was born, and it was here that he grew up. Thus the name of this town, <s>Kumāravardhana</s> ("where the prince grew up"), arose.'

body.translated_text: He arrived at <s>Aṅgadikā</s>. In <s>Aṅgadikā</s>, at a certain place, he smiled. The account of the four-Buddha seat in detail is as before.

body.translated_text: He arrived at <s>Maṇivatī</s>. In <s>Maṇivatī</s>, he addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'In this <s>Maṇivatī</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> performed a sacrifice with many jewels. Thus the name <s>Maṇivatī</s> ("rich in jewels") arose.'

body.translated_text: He arrived at <s>Sālabālā</s>. In <s>Sālabālā</s>, at a certain place, he smiled. The account of the four-Buddha seat in detail is as before.

body.translated_text: He arrived at <s>Sālibālā</s>. In <s>Sālibālā</s>, at a certain place, he smiled. The account of the four-Buddha seat in detail is as before.

body.text: suvarṇaprastham anuprāptaḥ / asminn ānanda suvarṇaprasthe bodhisatvena bahusuvarṇako yajño yaṣṭaḥ / apīdānīṃ brāhmanaiḥ prasthena suvarṇo bhājitaḥ / suvarṇaprasthaḥ suvarnaprastha iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā /
body.translated_text: He arrived at <s>Suvarṇaprastha</s>. 'In this <s>Suvarṇaprastha</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> performed a sacrifice involving much gold. Even now, the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> have been dividing gold by the <s>prastha</s> (measure). Thus the name <s>Suvarṇaprastha</s> ("gold-plateau") arose.'

body.translated_text: He arrived at <s>Sāketā</s>. In <s>Sāketā</s>, he addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'In this <s>Sāketā</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, a king named <s>Upoṣadha</s> was ruling the kingdom — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, and teeming with many people. After some time, a boil appeared on his head, soft and very soft, like cotton-fluff or kapok-fluff, and it caused no pain. When it ripened, it burst open, and a prince was born — handsome, good-looking, pleasing, fair, of golden complexion, as before up to endowed with all major and minor limbs. Since he was born from the head, the name <s>Mūrdhāta</s> ("head-born") arose. King <s>Upoṣadha</s> had sixty thousand women. The newborn prince was brought into the inner quarters. At the very sight of him, the breasts of all the women began to flow with milk. Each one said: "Let him suckle from me! Let him suckle from me!" Thus the name <s>Māndhātā</s> arose. Some know him as <s>Mūrdhāta</s>, others as <s>Māndhātā</s>.

The ministers instructed: 'Your Highness, for a royal consecration, many things are required — a jeweled throne, a lion-seat, an umbrella, a ceremonial turban, and a crown. The royal consecration is performed in the capital. The prince should come here.' He replied: 'If my kingdom has been obtained by right, let everything come here to me.' Prince <s>Māndhātā</s> had a <s>Yakṣa</s> attendant named <s>Divaukasa</s> who ran ahead of him. He brought the jeweled throne and the lion-seat right there. And the officials of the capital came of their own accord, bringing the umbrella, the ceremonial turban, and the crown. The capital came of its own accord — 'came of its own accord, came of its own accord' — thus the name <s>Sāketā</s> arose.

He gave orders to his ministers: 'Good sirs, quickly consecrate the prince with the royal consecration.' 'Yes, Your Majesty,' the ministers sent a messenger: 'King <s>Upoṣadha</s> is ill. That <s>brāhmaṇa</s> saw the <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, his body radiant with eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a halo extending a fathom, his brilliance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, auspicious on every side. At the very sight of him, faith arose in the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Not even in twelve years does tranquility of mind produce such joy as a childless person's obtaining a child, or a poor person's discovering a treasure, or a kingdom-lover's royal consecration — as does the first sight of a <s>Buddha</s> for a being whose roots of merit are well-accumulated. Then that <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, like a merchant who has gained profit, like a farmer whose crops have ripened, like a warrior who has won the battle, like a sick man freed from all disease, having rejoiced and approved of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words, having paid homage at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet with his head, departed from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence and went to his field. He saw in that field golden barley, fully ripened. Having seen it, with eyes wide open in astonishment, he spoke a verse:

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> showed the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> an old well: 'If you have any to spare, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, pour it into this old well.' He poured it into that old well. That old well, steaming, became full of gruel — such is the power of the <s>Buddhas</s>' majesty and the gods' majesty. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to that <s>brāhmaṇa</s>: 'Distribute the gruel, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.' He began to distribute it. The <s>Bhagavān</s> blessed it such that the entire <s>Saṃgha</s> received gruel, yet the old well, steaming, remained just as full of gruel. Then that <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having become even more deeply devoted, bowed at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> feet and sat before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. body.translated_text: Then that <s>brāhmaṇa</s> quickly approached the king's presence. Having approached, having greeted the king with wishes for victory and long life, he said to the king: 'Your Majesty, I sowed barley and it has turned to gold. May the overseer be pleased to accept this.' The king sent an overseer. The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> had it heaped up and divided. The king's share turned into ordinary barley. The overseer reported this to the king. The king ordered: 'Divide it again.' It was divided again. Likewise, the king's share turned into ordinary barley. Thus, up to seven times it was divided, and each time it was the same. The king, filled with curiosity, went himself and saw. Thereupon he addressed that <s>brāhmaṇa</s>: '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, this has arisen from your merit. Enough of the king's share.

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> set out and in a certain area, five hundred farmers, pale and wan, with cracked hands and feet, clad in hemp garments, were driving ploughs. Those oxen too, with bodies wounded and lacerated by goading sticks smeared with pus from sores, were pulling while resting again and again. Those farmers saw the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, as before up to: for a being with accumulated roots of merit, this was the first sight of the <s>Buddha</s>. Then they approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> saw those farmers. Having seen them from afar, out of consideration for their spiritual training, he stepped aside from the path and sat upon a seat prepared before the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks. Then those farmers, having paid homage at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet with their heads, sat down to one side. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing the disposition, latent tendencies, temperament, and nature of those farmers, delivered such a teaching on the <s>Dharma</s> leading to the penetration of the Four Noble Truths, as before up to: having shattered with the vajra of knowledge the mountain of the view of the personal self, accumulated since beginningless time, they directly realized the fruit of stream-entry. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'sminn eva bhadrake kalpe viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kaśyapo nāma śāstā loke udapādi / pūrvavad yāvat sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśṛtya viharati ṛṣivadane mṛgadāve / tasya śāsane etāni paṃca kārṣikaśatāni pravrajitāny abhūvan* / tatra ebhir na paṭhitaṃ na svādhyāyitaṃ na manasikāro vāhitaḥ kin tu śraddhādeyaṃ bhuktvā bhuktvā saṃgaṇikābhirataiḥ kausīdyenātināmitam* /
body.translated_text:
The monks, having doubts, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, who resolves all doubts: 'Venerable sir, what <s>karma</s> was performed by these monks, formerly farmers, that they became farmers, and having gone forth in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s dispensation, directly realized <s>arhatva</s> (the state of an arhat) through the abandonment of all afflictions? And what <s>karma</s> was performed by those divine sons, formerly oxen, that they were born as oxen and yet attained the vision of truth?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'By these very ones, monks, <s>karmas</s> were performed and accumulated, their requisites gathered, as before up to: indeed they bear fruit for embodied beings.'
In a former time, monks, in this very auspicious <s>kalpa</s> (aeon), when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, a teacher named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world. As before, up to: he dwelt near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, in the Deer Park at <s>Ṛṣivadana</s>. In his dispensation, these five hundred had gone forth. There they did not study, did not recite, did not apply their minds; instead, having consumed the offerings given in faith, they spent their time in socializing, succumbing to laziness.

body.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yāni tāni paṃca bhikṣuśatāni etāni paṃca kārṣikaśatāni / yo 'sau vihārasvāmī sa evāsau (

children.translated_text: MSV I 73

children.text: ) gṛhapatiḥ / yad ete kārṣikā yad ebhir vihārasvāmisantakaṃ śraddhādeyaṃ paribhujya na paṭhitaṃ na svādhyāyitaṃ nāpi manasikāro vāhitaḥ kin tu saṃgaṇikābhirataiḥ kausīdyenātināmitaṃ tena karmaṇā paṃca janmaśatāni tasya vihārasvāminaḥ kārṣikāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ / yāvad etarhy api tasyaiva kārṣikā jātāḥ / yad ebhiḥ kāśyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya śāsane pravrajya brahmacaryaṃ caritaṃ tenaitarhi mama śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* /
children.translated_text: ) householder. Because these farmers, having consumed the faith-offerings belonging to the monastery patron, did not study, did not recite, and did not apply their minds, but instead spent their time in socializing, succumbing to laziness—through that <s>karma</s>, for five hundred births they became the farmers of that monastery patron. Even now they have been born as his farmers. Because they went forth in the dispensation of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the perfectly awakened one, and practiced the holy life, therefore now, having gone forth in my dispensation, they have directly realized <s>arhatva</s> through the abandonment of all afflictions.

body.translated_text: What do you think, monks? Those five hundred monks were these five hundred farmers. The one who was the monastery's patron is this (

body.translated_text: Those divine sons, formerly oxen, had also gone forth in the dispensation of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the perfectly awakened one. There they violated the minor and subsidiary training rules. Through the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, they were born as oxen. Because they generated faith in my presence, they were born among the gods. Because they practiced and maintained the holy life under <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the perfectly awakened one, now, as divine sons (

body.text: tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmaṃtrayate / āgamayānanda yena toyikā / evaṃ bhadantety āyuṣmān ānando bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt* / atha bhagavāṃs toyikām anuprāptaḥ / tasmiṃś ca pradeśe brāhmaṇo lāṅgalaṃ vāhayati / athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā puruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyaṃjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ (

children.text: ) sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṃgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* / sa saṃlakṣayati / yadi bhagavantaṃ gautamam upetyābhivādayiṣyāmi karmaparihānir me bhaviṣyati / atha nopetyābhivādayiṣyāmi puṇyaparihānir me bhaviṣyati / ko 'sāv upāyaḥ syād yena me na karmaparihāniḥ syān nāpi puṇyaparihānir iti / tasya buddhir utpannā / atrastha evābhivādanaṃ karomi / evaṃ na karmaparihānir bhaviṣyati nāpi puṇyaparihānir iti / tena yathāgṛhītayaiva pratodayaṣṭyā tatrasthenaivābhivādanaṃ kṛtam* / abhivādaye buddhaṃ bhagavantam iti /
children.translated_text: ), his radiance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, auspicious on all sides. He reflected: 'If I approach and salute the <s>Bhagavān Gautama</s>, there will be a loss in my work. But if I do not approach and salute him, there will be a loss in my merit. What means could there be by which I would neither lose my work nor my merit?' This idea occurred to him: 'I shall salute him right from where I stand. Thus there will be no loss of work and no loss of merit.' So, standing right there with his goad in hand just as he had grasped it, he made his salutation: 'I salute the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>!'

body.translated_text: There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Come, <s>Ānanda</s>, let us go to <s>Toyikā</s>.' 'Yes, venerable sir,' the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> replied to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> arrived at <s>Toyikā</s>. In that area, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> was driving a plough. That one then beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, adorned with a fathom-wide halo of light (

body.text: tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate / kṣūṇa ānanda eṣa brāhmaṇaḥ /

children.translated_text: Having been approached by him, when the salutation was made at this spot,

If he had approached and venerated me, he would have thereby performed veneration to two perfectly awakened ones. And for what reason? At this spot, <s>Ānanda</s>, stands the undisturbed bone-relic assembly of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the perfectly awakened one.' Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, quickly and swiftly, having spread out the <s>uttarāsaṅga</s> (upper robe) folded in four, addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> be seated upon the prepared seat. Thus this spot of earth will have been used by two perfectly awakened ones—by <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the perfectly awakened one, and now by the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' Having heard this, and being filled with curiosity, he set forth together with the inner-palace princes, ministers, the elite of the army, and townspeople and country-folk. Likewise <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, <s>Uṣidatta</s>, the chief architect, <s>Viśākhā Mṛgāramātā</s>, and many hundreds of thousands of beings, filled with curiosity, set forth, impelled by former roots of merit. But by then he had vanished. They heard that the bodily relics of the perfectly awakened <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s> had vanished. Having heard, sorrow and dejection arose in them: 'Our coming was in vain!'

body.translated_text: A certain lay follower circumambulated that spot. And he generated this thought: 'How much merit will there be from this walking-meditation of mine?'

body.text:
śataṃ sahasrāṇi suvarṇaniṣkā jāmbūnadā nāsya samā bhavanti /
yo buddhacaityeṣu prasannacittaḥ padāvihāraṃ prakaroti vidvān // iti /
body.translated_text:
Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, in order to generate freedom from regret in that great assembly, and having known that lay follower's thought with his own mind, spoke this verse:
'A hundred thousand gold coins of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold cannot equal this—
he who, with a serene mind, performs walking-meditation at the shrines of the <s>Buddha</s>.'

body.text:
anyatamenāpy upāsakena tasmin pradeśe mṛttikāpiṇḍo dattaḥ / evaṃ cittam abhisaṃskṛtam* / padāvihārasya tāvad iyat puṇyam ākhyātaṃ bhagavatā / asya tu mṛttikāpiṇḍasya kiyat puṇyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti / atha bhagavāṃs tasya cetasā cittam ājñāya gāthāṃ bhāṣate /
śataṃ sahasrāṇi suvarṇapiṇḍā jāmbūnadā nāsya samā bhavanti /
yo buddhacaityeṣu prasannacittaḥ āropayen mṛttikāpiṇḍam ekam* // iti /
body.translated_text:
Another lay follower placed a lump of earth on that spot. And he generated this thought: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> has declared such great merit for walking-meditation. But how much merit will there be from this lump of earth?' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having known his thought with his own mind, spoke this verse:
'A hundred thousand lumps of gold of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold cannot equal this—
he who, with a serene mind, places a single lump of earth at the shrines of the <s>Buddha</s>.'

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave such a teaching on the <s>Dharma</s> to that great assembly that, having heard it, many hundreds of thousands of beings attained great distinction. Some generated the aspiration for <s>Śrāvakabodhi</s> (the awakening of disciples), some for <s>Pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening), some for the unsurpassed perfect awakening. Some attained the stage of <s>uṣmagata</s> (warmth), some the stage of <s>mūrdhāna</s> (summit), some the stage of <s>satyānuloma</s> (conformity to truth), some the stage of <s>kṣānti</s> (patience). Some realized the fruit of stream-entry, some the fruit of once-returning, some the fruit of non-returning. Some, having gone forth, through the abandonment of all afflictions realized <s>arhatva</s> (arhatship). For the most part, that assembly was established as inclined toward the <s>Buddha</s>, tending toward the <s>Dharma</s>, and leaning toward the <s>Saṃgha</s>.

body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, from a certain forest dwelling-place, with long hair and beard and worn robes, went to <s>Jetavana</s>. He saw that <s>Jetavana</s> was empty. He asked the attendant: 'Where is the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>?' The attendant told him: 'They have been invited by the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.' He reflected: 'I shall eat my alms-food there and attend upon the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>.' He went to the residence of the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. The doorkeeper said: 'Venerable one, you may not enter.' 'For what reason?' 'The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> has given this order: "Do not admit followers of other sects until the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> has eaten. Afterward I will give to the followers of other sects."' The venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> reflected: 'How fortunate for me that these <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders do not recognize me as a follower of the ascetic <s>Śākyaputra</s>. I shall go and show compassion to the destitute.' Knowing this, he went to the garden. He reflected: 'To whom should I show kindness today?' Then a certain beggar woman, afflicted with leprosy, sick and suffering, with decomposing limbs, was begging for alms. He approached her. She had obtained some rinse-water in her begging. The venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> was seen by her—one whose physical appearance and mental bearing inspire confidence, with a serene deportment. She reflected: 'Surely it is because I have never made offerings to such a worthy recipient that I am in this condition. If the noble <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> were to show compassion toward me

body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, thought: 'These humans, who cannot directly see the fruits of merit, give gifts and perform meritorious deeds. I, who directly see the fruits of merit, remain established in my own merit — therefore I too should give gifts and perform meritorious deeds. This noble <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> has compassion for the poor, destitute, wretched, and lowly. Let me offer him alms-food.' Having resolved thus, he created a house in a poor street, and having created himself as a weaver — wearing ragged, patched garments, with matted hair, dark like a crow, of unremarkable appearance — head disheveled, wearing a hempen cloth, with cracked hands and feet, he began to weave cloth. <s>Śacī</s> the goddess also assumed the guise of a weaver-woman and began to work the loom-shuttle. Beside him, divine ambrosia stood prepared. Then the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, compassionate toward the poor, destitute, and lowly, approached that house in due order. body.translated_text: The news spread throughout the vicinity: 'The noble <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> has been offered leftovers by a certain street-woman, and she has been reborn in the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven.' King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> heard this. Having heard, he approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> feet and sat down to one side. To King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> seated to one side, the <s>Bhagavān</s> instructed him with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, as before up to: having inspired him, fell silent.

body.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, and with joined palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said to him: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> consent to a meal in honor of the noble <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> for seven days.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> consented to King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> through silence. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>, having understood the <s>Bhagavān's</s> consent through silence, bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> feet and departed from the <s>Bhagavān's</s> presence. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>, that very night, having gathered pure, choice hard and soft foods, rising early in the morning, having arranged seats and placed water vessels, sent a messenger to inform the <s>Bhagavān</s> of the time. As before, up to: he served them with his own hands. And a certain wrestler, standing at the end of the line, was generating faith: 'This king, who directly sees the fruits of merit, established in his own merit, still unsatisfied with merit, gives gifts and performs meritorious deeds.'

children.translated_text: In yours, or in the name of the one from whom more abundant merit has arisen?' The king reflected: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> partakes of my alms-food. Who else could generate more abundant merit from my offering?' Having reflected, he said: '<s>Bhagavān</s>, let the <s>Bhagavān</s> dedicate the merit of the offering in the name of the one from whom more abundant merit has arisen.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> dedicated the merit in the name of the wrestler. This continued for six days. On the sixth day, the king, resting his cheek on his hand, sat absorbed in thought: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> partakes of my alms-food, yet dedicates the merit in the wrestler's name.' His ministers saw him and said: 'Why, Your Majesty, do you sit with your cheek on your hand, absorbed in thought?' The king replied: 'Good sirs, how can I not be lost in thought, when the <s>Bhagavān</s> partakes of my alms-food yet dedicates the merit in the wrestler's name?' Then one elderly minister said: 'Do not worry, Your Majesty. We shall arrange things so that tomorrow the <s>Bhagavān</s> will dedicate the merit in Your Majesty's own name.' He gave orders to his men: 'Tomorrow you must prepare food more choice and more abundant. And serve it thus: let half fall into the monks' bowls and half upon the ground.' The next day the ministers prepared abundant and choice food. Then, when the <s>Bhikṣusaṃgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s> was comfortably seated, they began to serve.

In the absence of the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) arise in the world—compassionate toward the lowly and wretched, content with humble lodgings and food, worthy of offerings individually. Then a certain <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> arrived at that place. The boy saw him—pleasing in body, pleasing in mind, of serene deportment. He reflected: 'Surely it is because I have never made offerings to such a true field of merit that I am in such a condition. If this one would accept my unsalted lump of barley-gruel, I would give it to him.' Then the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, having known with his mind the thoughts in the poor man's mind, extended his bowl: 'If you have renounced it, let it be placed in this bowl.' Then, with intense faith, he offered the unsalted lump of barley-gruel to the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>.

body.translated_text: In a former time, monks, in a certain small town, a householder lived. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He amused himself, enjoyed himself, and delighted with her. While he was amusing, enjoying, and delighting himself, a son was born. As before, up to: he was raised, nurtured, and grew up. Then that householder addressed his wife: 'My dear, a son has been born to us who will repay debts and carry forward our wealth. I shall take merchandise and go to another region.' She replied: 'My lord, do so.' He took his merchandise and went to another region. There, however, he met with misfortune and was left with little. The wealth in his household was exhausted. His son grew up in hardship. The householder had a friend. He said to the son: 'You are like a son to me as well. Look after my fields, and I will provide you with food as your livelihood.' He began doing the fieldwork for that householder. And the friend in turn provided him with food as his livelihood. Then, at another time, a festival day arrived. The boy's mother reflected: 'Today the householder's wife will be occupied with feeding relatives, kinsmen, friends, and ascetics. Let me go in good time and bring food for the boy.' She went in good time and informed the householder's wife. She, irritated, replied: 'I have not yet given to the ascetics and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>! Or even to the relatives and servants! Let it wait for today; tomorrow I will give double.' Then the boy's mother reflected: 'Lest the boy go hungry, let me take this unsalted lump of barley-gruel that is my own.' Taking it, she went to the field. Having recounted to her son in detail all that the householder's wife had said, she said: 'Here is this unsalted lump of barley-gruel that I brought—it is my own. (

Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, and said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> accept from me for the three months' rains-retreat robes, almsfood, bedding and seats, and medicines and provisions for the sick, together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> accepted King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala's</s> invitation through silence. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> provided the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> with meals of a hundred flavors for the three months. Each monk was covered with a cloth worth a hundred thousand. And having gathered a <s>koṭi</s> (ten million) of jars of oil, he undertook to offer a garland of lamps. A great commotion arose concerning the food and offerings. Then a certain destitute woman of the city was exceedingly distressed. While begging for alms with a broken pot, she heard that loud, great noise. Having heard it, she asked: 'Good people, what is this loud, great noise?' Others informed her: 'King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> has fed the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> for the three months. Each monk has been covered with a cloth worth a hundred thousand in value. And having gathered a <s>koṭi</s> of jars of oil, he undertakes to offer a garland of lamps.'

body.translated_text: Likewise, the <s>Nāga</s>-king <s>Nandopananda</s>, seeing <s>Māndhātā</s>'s army, thinking 'These are <s>asuras</s> (demons),' came out with a fourfold army. At the very sight of the army, he was defeated. 'Your Majesty, the <s>yakṣas</s> carry skulls in their hands, possess magic, and are eternally intoxicated.' And all including <s>Nandopananda</s>, being defeated, approached the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> (Four Great Kings') gods. Having approached the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods, he said: 'Know this, sirs—a great army has arrived! Let the fourfold army be arrayed. We have all been defeated.' They understood. They said: 'Sirs, this is King <s>Māndhātā</s>, a <s>Cakravartin</s>; he goes to see <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods. And he is known as the Great Lord of Merit. What power do we have to fight against him? Rather, taking offerings of water for washing the feet, let us go out to receive him.' Then the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods, having taken offerings of water for washing the feet, with umbrellas, banners, flags, and various musical instruments, went out to receive him. Then King <s>Māndhātā</s>, having exchanged greetings with the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods, surrounded by the gods, went to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-three) gods. And he was invited by <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, to share half his throne. Then the <s>asuras</s>, having arrayed their fourfold army, attacked <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods. The <s>yakṣas</s> informed <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: 'Know this, <s>Kauśika</s>—the <s>asuras</s>, having broken through five divisions, have arrived. Do what needs to be done.' body.translated_text: In a former time, O great king, there was a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) king named <s>Śakuna</s>, sovereign of the four continents, endowed with the seven treasures and with the four supernatural powers belonging to humans. He was the friend and companion of <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods. His queen bore him neither son nor daughter. He placed his chin on his hand and stood absorbed in worry: 'In such great royal prosperity as mine, there is neither son nor daughter. Upon my passing, my lineage will be without heirs.' He was seen by <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, who said: 'Friend, why do you stand with chin on hand, absorbed in worry?' He replied: 'O <s>Kauśika</s>, in such great royal prosperity as mine, there is neither son nor daughter. Upon my passing, my lineage will be without heirs.' He said: 'Friend, I will send you a medicinal herb. Your queens shall drink it, and then sons and daughters will be born to you.' <s>Śakra</s> obtained the herb from Mount <s>Gandhamādana</s> and sent it to that king. The king gave it to the inner quarters: 'You shall drink this herb.' The king's chief queen was asleep. The others (

body.translated_text: He took up residence on the bank of a river. Weary in body, he descended into the river to bathe. There he saw the reflection of his own face. He reflected: 'I am endowed with eighteen inauspicious marks, and my face has the appearance of a lion's maw. It is for this very reason that this princess shows displeasure toward me. What use is such a life to me? I shall go and kill myself.' He entered a certain thicket and began to hang himself. <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, reflected: 'This <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the Auspicious Age is killing himself because of his lack of physical beauty. His wish must be fulfilled.' <s>Śakra</s> said: 'Prince, do not fall into despair. Do not kill yourself. Wear this crest-jewel on your head and your wish will be fulfilled.' Having said this, he departed. Prince <s>Kuśa</s> began to enter the inner palace. The doorkeeper stopped him: 'This is Prince <s>Kuśa</s>'s inner palace. Do not enter.' He said: 'I am that very <s>Kuśa</s>.' They did not believe him. He removed the crest-jewel. He became as he was before. They believed. Prince <s>Kuśa</s> reflected: 'I shall remain right here.' He sent a message to his father: 'Father, give me leave. I shall remain right here.' <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, showed him four mineral deposits. He had that city built of four kinds of gems and established it. Because Prince <s>Kuśa</s> dwelt there, the designation <s>Kuśāvatī</s> arose. He became king. King <s>Kuśa</s>, a universal sovereign of strength, having established sacrificial grounds in those sixty thousand cities, gave gifts to <s>brāhmaṇas</s> for many years, many hundreds of years, many thousands of years,

The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'By <s>Kuśa</s> himself, O monks, were those <s>karmas</s> performed and accumulated, their requisites gathered, their conditions matured, standing ready like a flood, inevitably coming to fruition. By <s>Kuśa</s> himself, O monks, were those <s>karmas</s> performed and accumulated—who else would experience their results? O monks, <s>karmas</s> performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element. Rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that <s>karmas</s> performed ripen, both wholesome and unwholesome.'

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'nyatamasmin karvaṭake gṛhapatiḥ prativasati / sa prabhūtaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ gṛhītvodyānaṃ gataḥ / asati buddhānāṃ bhagavatām utpāde pratyekabuddhā loke utpadyante hīnadīnānukaṃpakāḥ prāntaśayanāsanabhaktā ekadakṣiṇīyā lokasya /
body.translated_text: 'Once upon a time, O monks, in a certain market-town there lived a householder. Having taken abundant hard and soft food, he went to a garden. When <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bhagavāns</s>, have not arisen in the world, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> arise in the world—compassionate toward the lowly and destitute, fond of secluded dwelling-places and food, worthy of individual offerings from the world.'

body.text: athānyatamaḥ pratyekabuddho janapadacārikāṃ caraṃs tad udyānam anuprāptaḥ / tena gṛhapatinā dṛṣṭaḥ / tena pauruṣeyāṇām ājñā dattā / bhavanto niṣkāsayatainaṃ pravrajitam* / te notsahante niṣkāsayitum* / tena gṛhapatinā svayam evotthāya gṛhītvā niṣkāsitaḥ uktaś ca / siṃhamukhāṣṭādaśabhir avalakṣaṇaiḥ samanvāgataḥ kutra tvaṃ praviśasi / pratyekabuddhaḥ saṃlakṣayati / mā haivāyaṃ tapyeta atyantakṣataś copahataś ceti viditvopari vihāyasam iti vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: Then a certain <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, wandering through the countryside, arrived at that garden. He was seen by that householder. The householder gave orders to his servants: 'Good sirs, throw out this wandering ascetic.' They did not dare to throw him out. The householder himself rose, seized him, and threw him out, saying: 'You with a lion's maw, endowed with eighteen inauspicious marks—where do you think you are entering?' The <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> reflected: 'Let this one not be tormented; he would be utterly destroyed and ruined.' Knowing this, he rose into the sky, and so forth in detail.

body.text: yāvat tena satkṛto yāvat pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ / yan mayā evaṃvidhe sadbhūtadakṣiṇīye kharaṃ vākkarma niścāritaṃ nāham asya (

children.translated_text: (MSV I 109)

children.text: ) karmaṇo bhāgī syām* / yat tu kārāḥ kṛtā anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlenāḍhye mahādhane mahābhoge kule jāyeya / kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau gṛhapatir eṣa evāsau kuśaḥ / yad anena pratyekabuddhasyāntike kharaṃ vākkarma niścāritaṃ tasya karmaṇo vipākenāṣṭādaśabhir avalakṣaṇaiḥ samanvāgataḥ siṃhavaktrākṛtimukhaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ / yat tu kārāḥ kṛtās tasya karmaṇo vipākena rājā saṃvṛtto balacakravartī / iti hi bhikṣavaḥ ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ / vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ / ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ / tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam* / ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogāḥ karaṇīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: What do you think, O monks? That householder is none other than this <s>Kuśa</s>. Because he uttered harsh speech toward a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, as the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, he was endowed with eighteen inauspicious marks and had a face with the appearance of a lion's maw. But because he showed reverence, as the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, he became a king, a universal sovereign of strength. Thus, O monks, for <s>karmas</s> that are entirely black, the ripening is entirely black. For mixed <s>karmas</s>, it is mixed. For <s>karmas</s> that are entirely white, the ripening is entirely white. Therefore, O monks, you should train thus: having cast aside entirely black <s>karmas</s> and mixed <s>karmas</s>, effort should be made only in <s>karmas</s> that are entirely white.'

body.translated_text: Eventually he venerated the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, and falling at his feet, began to make an aspiration: 'Since I uttered harsh speech toward such a truly worthy recipient, may I not partake of the fruit of that <s>karma</s>. But through whatever reverence I have shown, may I, through this root of merit, be born in a wealthy, affluent, and prosperous family.'

He had a retinue of many hundreds, thousands, and hundreds of thousands of <s>Mātaṅgas</s>. He was benevolent by nature, compassionate, and concerned for the welfare of all beings. Whenever there was famine in his domain, by his act of truth the rain would fall. There was never a famine. He went forth among the sages. He directly realized the five supernatural powers. At that time, in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> was ruling — his kingdom was prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, and teeming with people. children.translated_text:
'Hear, O citizens dwelling in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>! The soothsayers have predicted a drought lasting twelve years. Whoever among you has enough food for that long, let him stay. Whoever does not, let him go.' Then that populace, terrified by the fear of famine, death, and scarcity, began to deliberate: 'Good people, the king has had this bell-proclamation made in the kingdom. What should we do? Where shall we go?' They heard: 'In the <s>Mātaṅga</s> territory there is a sage of the <s>Mātaṅga</s> caste. By his act of truth the rain falls.' Then those who did not have food for twelve years went to the <s>Mātaṅga</s> territory. The son of the <s>Mātaṅga</s> sage was the <s>Mātaṅga</s> king. He provided that populace with food and drink for twelve years. Meanwhile the famine persisted. King <s>Brahmadatta</s> asked his ministers: 'Where has that populace gone?' The ministers replied: 'Your Majesty, in the <s>Kaliṅga</s> territory there is a <s>Mātaṅga</s> king named <s>Triśaṅku</s>, benevolent by nature, compassionate, a great soul, devoted to the welfare of all beings. By his act of truth the rain falls. The great populace has gone there.' The king said: 'Good sirs, this is a great famine, comparable to a famine-interval between aeons. What is to be done?' They replied: 'Your Majesty, it is said
that the king in the <s>Mātaṅga</s> territory who has gone forth among the sages should be requested.' Then King <s>Brahmadatta</s>, having gone to the <s>Mātaṅga</s> territory, began to request that sage: 'Great sage, in my kingdom there is a great famine comparable to a famine-interval between aeons. Please perform an act of truth.' He began the act of truth:
