body.translated_text: Then by the act of truth, rain fell upon <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. The famine ended and abundance appeared. Then the people dwelling in <s>Vārāṇasī</s> returned from the <s>Mātaṅga</s> territory to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. You should not think, O great king, that that <s>Mātaṅga</s> king named <s>Triśaṅku</s> at that time and on that occasion — benevolent by nature, compassionate, concerned for the welfare of all beings, by whose act of truth the rain fell, the famine ended, and abundance appeared — was someone else. Rather, it was I myself who at that time and on that occasion was the <s>Mātaṅga</s> king named <s>Triśaṅku</s>, benevolent by nature, compassionate, concerned for the welfare of all beings, by whose act of truth the rain fell. You should not think, O great king, that by that gift or that sharing of gifts I attained supreme, perfect awakening. Rather, that gift was merely a cause, merely a requisite for supreme, perfect awakening.

body.translated_text: You should not think, O great king, that that <s>Cakravartin</s> king named <s>Mahādeva</s> at that time and on that occasion, who set in motion the unfailing, wholesome <s>Dharma</s>, and depending upon whose unfailing, wholesome path eighty-four thousand royal sages practiced the holy life, was someone else. Rather, it was I myself who at that time and on that occasion was the <s>Cakravartin</s> king named <s>Mahādeva</s>. It was I who set in motion the unfailing, wholesome <s>Dharma</s>, and depending upon my unfailing, wholesome path, eighty-four thousand royal sages practiced the holy life. You should not think, O great king, that by that gift or that sharing of gifts I attained supreme, perfect awakening. Rather, that gift was merely a cause, merely a condition, merely a requisite for supreme, perfect awakening.

The inner treasure is the treasure inside the threshold. What is the outer treasure? The outer treasure is the treasure outside the threshold. What is the inner-outer treasure? body.translated_text: After that, there was a glorious king named <s>Ānanda</s>. In detail, up to: one, then two, up to five sons were born to him. The last of his sons had a face like a mirror. The name <s>Ādarśamukha</s> (Mirror-face) arose for him. He was raised, nurtured, and grew up. Prince <s>Ādarśamukha</s> was good-natured and well-disciplined. But the other four were violent, impetuous, and harsh. All of them sat in their father's court for legal proceedings but could not resolve anything with wisdom. Prince <s>Ādarśamukha</s> resolved even the most profound questions by his own wisdom. King <s>Ānanda</s> became ill. He reflected: 'Whom shall I establish as king? If I establish any one of the four elder brothers as king, they are violent, impetuous, and harsh — they will bring the country to ruin and calamity. If I establish Prince <s>Ādarśamukha</s> as king, I will be censured by the relatives: "How is it that this king, passing over his elder sons, establishes the youngest as king?" body.translated_text: In a certain small town, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Daṇḍin</s> ("staff-bearer") lived. He borrowed oxen from a householder, used them for plowing during the day, and then took those oxen to the householder's residence. Meanwhile, the householder was eating. <s>Daṇḍin</s> led the oxen inside. They went out through another door. The householder, having finished eating, got up. He could not find the oxen. He seized <s>Daṇḍin</s>: 'Where are the oxen?' He replied: 'I led them into the house.' 'You have caused my oxen to be lost! Give me back my oxen.' He replied: 'I did not cause them to be lost.' The householder said: 'This King <s>Ādarśamukha</s> is wise. Let us go to his presence. He will decide our case and tell us what is right and wrong.' The two set out.

body.translated_text: The tavern-woman reported the matter in full. The king declared: 'Cut off this tavern-woman's hands, since the child was covered up completely when laid down to sleep. And gouge out <s>Daṇḍin's</s> eyes too, since without looking he would sit on someone else's seat.' She said: 'Once my son was killed, and now my hands would be cut off? Let <s>Daṇḍin</s> win the case!'

body.text: ahinakulasandeśam ārocitam* / rājā kathayati / tau vaktavyau / yuvāṃ manuṣyabhūtau dvau bhrātarau / tatraikaḥ kathayati svāpateyaṃ bhājayāvaḥ / dvitīyena mātsaryābhibhūtena na bhājitam* / tatraiko 'dhyavasānaṃ kṛtvā āśīviṣeṣūpapannaḥ / dvitīyo 'pi svāpateyam avaṣṭabhyādhyavasānaṃ kṛtvā nakulaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ / tena yūyam etat svāpateyaṃ śramaṇabrāhmaṇebhyo datvā tasmāt sthānād apakramata / svasthā bhaviṣyatha /
body.translated_text: The message of the snake and the mongoose was reported to him. The king said: 'They should be told: "You two, when you were humans, were two brothers. One of you said, 'Let us divide our property.' The second, overcome by avarice, did not divide it. The one, having made a firm resolution, was reborn among poisonous serpents. The other, clinging to the property, made a firm resolution and became a mongoose. Therefore you should give this property to ascetics and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and depart from that place. You will be well."'

body.text: sarpasya sandeśam ārocitam* / rājā kathayati / vaktavyas te sa sarpaḥ / tvaṃ jighatsādaurbalyaparīta āśayān nirgacchasi / mukhena prabhūtam āhāraṃ bhuktvā duḥkhenāśayaṃ praviśasi / sa tvam āhāre mātrāṃ jānīyāḥ / yatheṣṭacārī sukhaṃ vihariṣyasi /
body.translated_text: The message of the snake was reported to him. The king said: 'That snake should be told: "You, afflicted by hunger and weakness, come out from your lair. Having eaten much food with your mouth, you enter your lair with difficulty. You should know moderation in food. Then you will live happily, going wherever you wish."'

body.text: vadhūkumāryāḥ sandeśam ārocitam* / rājā kathayati / vaktavyā vadhūkumārī tvayā / tava paitṛke gṛhe sapremakas tiṣṭhati / sā tvaṃ yadā śvaśuragṛhe tiṣṭhasi tadā sapremakasyārthe utkaṇṭhayasi / yadā paitṛkagṛhe tiṣṭhasi tadā svāmino 'rthe utkaṇṭhayasi / sā tvam ekaṃ sthānaṃ parityajya ekaṃ sugṛhītaṃ kuru / mānayena vyasanam āpatsyase /
body.translated_text: The message of the young bride was reported to him. The king said: 'The young bride should be told: "In your father's house, your lover awaits. When you are in your father-in-law's house, you long for your lover. When you are in your father's house, you long for your husband. You should give up one place and hold firmly to one. Otherwise, through vacillation, you will come to ruin."'

body.text: vadhūkumārī āśīviṣaś ca yathānuśiṣṭaḥ pratipannaḥ / ahinakulau daṇḍinaḥ svāpateyam anupradattaḥ / kākenāpi avaśiṣṭā yathānuśiṣṭāḥ pratipannāḥ /
body.translated_text: The young bride and the snake followed the instruction as taught. The snake and the mongoose gave their property to mendicants. The crow and the rest also followed the instruction as taught.

body.text: amātyāḥ kathayanti / aho devasya īdṛśo 'pi pratibhānaḥ / rājā āttamanasā caturṣu nagaradvāreṣu dānaśālā māpitā / dānādhiṣṭhāyikāḥ puruṣāḥ sthāpitāḥ /
body.translated_text: The ministers said: 'Wonderful is such wisdom of the king!' The king, elated, had halls of generosity established at the four city gates. He stationed men to oversee the gifts.

body.translated_text: At that time, a twelve-year famine occurred there. During that twelve-year famine, he sustained many hundreds of thousands of living beings with alms-food. Having seen the success of his own sacrifice, he spoke a verse:

body.translated_text: 'Perhaps, O great king, you may think it was someone else who was at that time and on that occasion the glorious king named <s>Ādarśamukha</s>, who during that twelve-year famine sustained many hundreds of thousands of living beings with alms-food. But it should not be seen thus. It was I myself who was at that time and on that occasion the glorious king named <s>Ādarśamukha</s>. It was I myself who, during the twelve-year famine, sustained many hundreds of thousands of living beings with alms-food. Perhaps, O great king, you may think that by that gift or by that distribution of gifts, the unsurpassed perfect awakening was attained. But it should not be seen thus. Rather, that gift was merely a cause, merely a condition, (

In a former time, O great king, there was a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) king named <s>Sudhana</s>. He had sacrifice-enclosures established in eighty-four thousand cities, and for many years, many hundreds of years, many (

body.text: syāt khalu te mahārājānyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena rājābhūc cakravartī yena tac caturaśītiṣu nagarasahasreṣu yajñavāṭaṃ māpayitvā bahūni varṣāṇi bahūni varṣaśatāni bahūni varṣaśatasahasrāṇi dānāni dattāni puṇyāni kṛtāni / na khalv evaṃ draṣṭavyam* / api tu tad dānaṃ saṃbodher hetumātrakaṃ pratyayamātrakaṃ saṃbhāramātrakam* /
body.translated_text: 'Perhaps, O great king, you may think it was someone else who was at that time and on that occasion the <s>Cakravartin</s> king who had sacrifice-enclosures established in eighty-four thousand cities and for many years, many hundreds of years, many hundreds of thousands of years, gave gifts and performed merits. But it should not be seen thus. Rather, that gift was merely a cause, merely a condition, merely a requisite for awakening.'

body.text: punar api mahārāja yan mayānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ prārthayitā dānāni dattāni puṇyāni kṛtāni vīryapāramitā ca paripūritā na cānuttarā samyaksaṃbodhir adhigateti tac chrūyatām* / bhūtapūrvaṃ mahārāja paṃcālaviṣaye dvau rājānau babhūvatuḥ / uttarapaṃcālo dakṣiṇapaṃcālaś ca /
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, O great king, hear about the gifts I gave, the merits I made, and the perfection of vigor I fulfilled while aspiring to the unsurpassed perfect awakening, yet without attaining the unsurpassed perfect awakening.' In a former time, O great king, in the <s>Pañcāla</s> territory, there were two kings — <s>Uttarapañcāla</s> (Northern <s>Pañcāla</s>) and <s>Dakṣiṇapañcāla</s> (Southern <s>Pañcāla</s>).

body.text: tatrottarapaṃcālo dhano nāmnā hastināpure nagare rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ cākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ (

children.translated_text: ), free from quarrels, conflicts, strife, and tumult, free from robbers and disease, rich in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffaloes. He was righteous, a king of <s>Dharma</s>, ruling the kingdom by <s>Dharma</s>. In that city, there was a great lake, covered with blue lotuses, red lotuses, white water-lilies, and white lotuses, adorned with geese, <s>kāraṇḍava</s> ducks, and <s>cakravāka</s> birds — a delightful place. In that lake dwelt a young <s>Nāga</s> named <s>Janmacitra</s>. He gave timely and proper rain-showers, so that the harvest was exceedingly abundant. The land was rich in grain, prosperous, well-supplied with food and drink. The people were generous and respectful, providing sustenance to ascetics, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the destitute, and merchants.

body.translated_text: The king of <s>Uttarapañcāla</s>, named <s>Dhana</s>, ruled the kingdom in the city of <s>Hastināpura</s> — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, and teeming with many people (

children.translated_text: ), the king of <s>Dakṣiṇapañcāla</s>, under the pretext of a hunting expedition, went out to inspect his dominions. He saw that the villages and towns were empty, and the gardens and temples were broken and ruined. Having seen this, he addressed his ministers: 'Why, good sirs, are these villages and towns empty, and the gardens and temples broken and ruined? Where has the populace gone?' The ministers replied: 'Your Majesty, they have gone to the territory of the king of <s>Uttarapañcāla</s> (

children.translated_text: ), king <s>Dhana</s>.' 'For what reason?' 'Your Majesty, grant us immunity from punishment and we will speak.' 'It is granted.' Then they said: 'Your Majesty, the king of <s>Uttarapañcāla</s> rules the kingdom by <s>Dharma</s>. His territories are prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with many people, free from quarrels, conflicts, strife, and tumult, free from robbers and disease, rich in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffaloes. The people are generous and respectful, providing sustenance to ascetics, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the destitute, and merchants. Your Majesty, on the other hand, is cruel, violent, and harsh, constantly terrorizing the realm with punishments, beatings, killings, chains, bonds, stocks, fetters, and imprisonment. Therefore those people, terrified and filled with urgency, have gone to the territory of the king of <s>Uttarapañcāla</s>.' The king of <s>Dakṣiṇapañcāla</s> said: 'Good sirs, what means could there be by which those people would return and dwell again in these villages and towns?' The ministers replied: 'If Your Majesty, like the king of <s>Uttarapañcāla</s>, rules the kingdom by <s>Dharma</s>, with a mind of friendliness, benevolence, and compassion, protecting his own realm, before long those people will return and dwell again in these villages and towns.' The king of <s>Dakṣiṇapañcāla</s> said: 'Good sirs, if so, then I too, like <s>Uttarapañcāla</s>, will rule the kingdom by <s>Dharma</s>, with a mind of friendliness, benevolence, and compassion, protecting the realm. You should act in such a way that those people return and dwell again in these villages and towns.' 'Your Majesty, there is another advantage as well. In that city there is a great lake, covered with blue lotuses, water-lilies, and white lotuses, adorned with geese, <s>kāraṇḍava</s> ducks, and <s>cakravāka</s> birds. There dwells the young <s>Nāga</s> <s>Janmacitra</s>. He gives timely and proper rain. The harvest is exceedingly abundant. children.translated_text: ) At that moment you must strike that snake-charmer in a vital spot with an arrow. And quickly approach him and say: "Release the mantras! Or else I will cut off your head at the root and cast it upon the ground!" If he dies without releasing the mantras, then even in death I would remain forever bound by the mantra-noose.' The hunter said: 'Even if this benefit were for you alone, I would still do it—how much more so for the sake of the entire realm! I shall go and take my position there.' Then the <s>nāga</s>-cub showed him a hidden spot on one side. On the seventh day, the hunter concealed himself at the hidden spot and waited. The snake-charmer came and began to perform the <s>bali</s> offering. He drove four stakes of <s>khadira</s> wood at the four quarters. Having bound them with threads of various colors, he chanted the mantras. Then the water began to boil. The hunter struck him in a vital spot with an arrow, drew his sword from its scabbard, and said: 'You carry away this <s>nāga</s>-cub dwelling in this realm by means of mantras! Release the mantras! Or else I will cut off your head at the root and cast it upon the ground!' Then the snake-charmer, overcome by pain, reversed the mantras. And thereupon the hunter killed him. Then the <s>nāga</s>-cub, freed from the bond of the mantra-noose, emerged from the lake and embraced that hunter, saying: 'You are my mother, you are my father—for through your coming, the suffering of separation from my parents did not arise for me. Come, let us go to my abode.' He took him to his own abode and satisfied him with various kinds of food and drink, and showed him treasures. And he informed his parents: 'Mother, Father, this is my friend, my refuge (

body.translated_text: The king of <s>Dakṣiṇapañcāla</s>, however, was given to unrighteousness, cruel, violent, and harsh; he ruled the kingdom unrighteously. He constantly terrorized the inhabitants of the realm with punishments, beatings, killings, chains, bonds, stocks, fetters, and imprisonment. Because of his unrighteousness, the gods did not grant him timely and proper rain. Therefore those people, terrified and filled with urgency, out of concern for their own lives, abandoned their realm and went to dwell in the territory of the king of <s>Uttarapañcāla</s>. body.translated_text: Not far from that lake was a hermitage abounding in flowers and fruits, resounding with various birds. There dwelt a <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage), benevolent by nature, compassionate, tender toward beings. The hunter began visiting that <s>ṛṣi</s> three times daily. Whatever had transpired between him and the <s>nāga</s>-cub <s>Janmacitra</s>, all of it he related in detail. Then the <s>ṛṣi</s> said: 'What use are jewels? What use is gold to you? In that <s>nāga</s> abode there is an unfailing noose (<s>amogha pāśa</s>). Ask for that.' Then the hunter, having developed craving for the <s>Amogha-pāśa</s>, having heeded the <s>ṛṣi</s>'s words, went again to the <s>nāga</s> abode. There he saw the <s>Amogha-pāśa</s> at the gate of the <s>nāga</s> abode. He thought: 'That is the noose I must ask for.' Having noted this, he entered the <s>nāga</s> abode. Then the <s>nāga</s>-cub <s>Janmacitra</s> and the other <s>nāga</s>-cubs greeted him warmly with delight and offered him jewels. He said: 'Enough of jewels for me; but give me that <s>Amogha-pāśa</s> (unfailing noose).' <s>Janmacitra</s> said: 'What use is it to you?

body.translated_text: At another time, King <s>Dhana</s> was sporting, enjoying himself, and being attended to with his queen. While sporting, enjoying, and being attended, neither son nor daughter was born to him. He placed his chin on his hand and stood absorbed in worry: 'My house overflows with wealth, yet I have neither son nor daughter. After my passing, with the cutting off of my family lineage, the kingdom will be seized. And all my property, being heirless, will become subject to the crown.' His ascetics, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, friends, relatives, and kinsmen said to him: 'Your Majesty, why are you so absorbed in worry?' He related this matter to them in detail. They said: 'Perform worship of the deities; a son will be born to you.' He, sonless and longing for a son, prayed to <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and other special deities—garden deities, forest deities, crossroad deities, intersection deities, <s>bali</s>-receiving deities, innate deities, co-religious deities, and ever-attendant deities—he prayed to them all. And there is this popular saying that sons and daughters are born as a result of prayer. But it is not so. If it were so, each person would have a thousand sons, just like a <s>Cakravartin</s> king. Rather, it is from the conjunction of three conditions that sons and daughters are born. Which three? The parents must have desire for each other; they must come together; the mother must be healthy and in her fertile period; and a <s>gandharva</s> (being seeking rebirth) must be present. From the conjunction of these three conditions, sons and daughters are born. While he was thus engaged in prayers, a certain <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the auspicious <s>kalpa</s> (

children.translated_text: with foods that are neither too bitter, nor too sour, nor too salty, nor too sweet, nor too pungent, nor too astringent, devoid of bitter, sour, salty, sweet, pungent, and astringent flavors, her body adorned with necklaces and half-necklaces, like an <s>apsaras</s> (celestial nymph) dwelling in the <s>Nandana</s> grove, descending from couch to couch, from seat to seat, to the lowest floor. And she heard no unpleasant sound whatsoever until the maturation of the embryo. After eight or nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born—handsome, good-looking, pleasing, fair, golden-complexioned, with an umbrella-shaped head, long arms, a broad forehead, a deep voice, joined eyebrows, a prominent nose, endowed with all limbs and secondary limbs. At his birth, drums of joy were beaten. Having heard, the king asked: 'What is this?' The ladies of the inner palace informed the king: 'Congratulations, Your Majesty! A son has been born to you.' Then the king had the entire city cleared of stones, gravel, and potsherds, sprinkled with sandalwood water, with banners and flags raised, fragrant incense-pots placed about, strewn with various flowers, made beautiful. And he gave orders: 'Give gifts to ascetics, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the destitute, and travelers. Release all prisoners.' Thus, for three periods of seven—twenty-one days—a birth celebration was performed in detail, and a name was assigned: 'What shall be the boy's name?' The ministers said: 'This boy is the son of King <s>Dhana</s>. Let the boy's name be <s>Sudhana</s>.' The name <s>Sudhana</s> was assigned. The boy <s>Sudhana</s> was entrusted to eight nurses: two shoulder-nurses, two milk-nurses, two bathing-nurses, and two play-nurses. children.translated_text: He began to roam about that hermitage. Then he saw the sage—with long hair, beard, nails, and body-hair, his body withered by wind and sun, wearing bark garments, taking shelter at the foot of a certain tree, making his dwelling in a grass hut. Having seen him, he made obeisance at his feet and, with palms joined, asked: 'Venerable sir, how long have you been dwelling in this place?' 'Forty years.' 'In all this time, have you seen or heard from anyone any wonderful or marvelous thing in this place?' The sage spoke slowly and softly: 'Good sir, have you seen this lake?' 'I have, venerable sir.' body.translated_text: Then at another time, <s>Phalaka</s> the hunter, searching for game and roaming here and there, arrived at a certain mountain. Below that mountain he saw a sage's hermitage, abounding in flowers and fruits, frequented by flocks of various birds. And he saw a great lake covered with blue lotuses, white water-lilies, and white lotuses, adorned with geese, <s>kāraṇḍava</s> ducks, and <s>cakravāka</s> birds.

How then would he install that one as royal priest?'

body.translated_text: Then at another time, two <s>brāhmaṇas</s> came from the countryside. One of them attached himself to the king, the second to Prince <s>Sudhana</s>. The one who attached himself to the king was appointed by the king as chaplain and was given a share of wealth. But the one who attached himself to Prince <s>Sudhana</s> received only a share of material provisions.

body.translated_text: <s>Sūdayā</s>}. With it, ghee should be cooked and drunk; thereby you will have neither thirst nor hunger, and it strengthens the power of memory. A monkey should be obtained, a mantra should be learned, a bow with arrows should be taken, gems that give light, an antidote that destroys poison, three iron stakes, and a <s>vīṇā</s> (lute). North of <s>Himavān</s>, the king of mountains, is Mount <s>Utkīlaka</s>. Then: <s>Kūjaka</s> {
Divy:

body.text: kūlako} jalapathaḥ khadirakaḥ ekadhārako vajrakaḥ kāmarūpī utkīlaka airāvatako 'dhunānaḥ {
body.translated_text: <s>Kūlaka</s>}, <s>Jalapatha</s>, <s>Khadiraka</s>, <s>Ekadhāraka</s>, <s>Vajraka</s>, <s>Kāmarūpī</s>, <s>Utkīlaka</s>, <s>Airāvataka</s>, <s>Adhunāna</s> {
Divy:
<s>Adhovāṇa</s>},
<s>Pramokṣaṇa</s> {
Divy:
-ka} — these are the mountains. All of them must be crossed.'

body.text: tatra khadirake parvate guhāpraveśa ekadhārake ca utkīlake / vajrake tu pakṣirājena praveśaḥ / ebhir upāyais te sarve parvatāḥ samatikramaṇīyāḥ / yantrāṇi ca bhaṃktavyāni / ajavaktro meṇḍhakaḥ puruṣo rākṣasarūpī piṅgalo hantavyaḥ / guhāyāṃ lālāsrotasā mahatājagaro vegena pradhāvati / sa te vikrameṇa hantavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'At Mount <s>Khadiraka</s>, entry is through a cave; at <s>Ekadhāraka</s> and <s>Utkīlaka</s> as well. At <s>Vajraka</s>, however, entry is by the king of birds. By these means, all those mountains are to be crossed. And the mechanical devices are to be broken. The goat-faced one, the ram, the man in <s>Rākṣasa</s>-form — the tawny one — is to be slain. In the cave, a great serpent rushes forth with speed in a stream of saliva. He is to be slain by your valor.'

children.translated_text: MSV I 153
'When you see mid-way a crested <s>Nāga</s>, {
Divy:

children.text:
kiṭibhakaś ca}
cāpamuktena bāṇena hantavyo mama kāraṇāt* //
children.translated_text:
and <s>Kiṭibhaka</s>}
he is to be slain with an arrow released from the bow, for my sake.'

children.text: yatra paśyeta dvau meṣau saṃghaṭṭantau parasparam* /
children.translated_text: 'Where you see two rams butting each other,

children.text: tayoḥ śṛṅgam ekaṃ bhaṃktvā mārgaṃ pratilapsyase //
children.translated_text: breaking one horn of those two, you will find the path.'
'Seeing two iron men, weapons in hand, terrifying,
striking one of them, you will find the path.'
'A <s>Rākṣasī</s> with an iron mouth, contracting and expanding it —

children.text: yadā paśyet tadā kīlaṃ lalāṭe tasyā nikhānayet* //
children.translated_text: when you see her, then drive a stake into her forehead.'

children.text: śilāvartas tathā kūpo vilaṃghyas te ṣaṣṭihastakaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'A whirlpool of rock, and likewise a well sixty arm-lengths deep, to be leapt over;
a tawny-haired, tawny-eyed, terrible <s>Yakṣa-Rākṣasa</s> —'

children.text: kārmukaṃ maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā hantavyaś ca durāsadaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Drawing the bow in a full circle, the difficult-to-approach one is to be slain.'
'And rivers are to be crossed by force, teeming with crocodiles and water-monsters.'

children.text: naṅgā pataṅgā tapanī citrā rudanī hasanī āśīviṣā vetravatī ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Naṅgā</s>, <s>Pataṅgā</s>, <s>Tapanī</s>, <s>Citrā</s>, <s>Rudanī</s>, <s>Hasanī</s>, <s>Āśīviṣā</s>, and <s>Vetravatī</s> —
'In <s>Naṅgā</s>, there is the wrath of a <s>Rākṣasī</s>; in <s>Pataṅgā</s>, non-human beings;
in <s>Tapanī</s>, an abundance of crocodiles; in <s>Citrā</s>, shape-shifters.'
'In <s>Rudanī</s>, <s>Kinnarī</s> maidservants; in <s>Hasanī</s>, <s>Kinnarī</s> daughters-in-law;

children.text: āśīviṣāyāṃ nānāvidhāḥ sarpā vetranadyāṃ tu śālmaliḥ /
children.translated_text: in <s>Āśīviṣā</s>, serpents of various kinds; in the river <s>Vetrā</s>, <s>śālmalī</s> thorns.'
'In <s>Naṅgā</s>, the method is fortitude; in <s>Pataṅgā</s>, valor;
in <s>Tapanī</s>, binding the mouths of the crocodiles; in <s>Citrā</s>, various songs.'
MSV I 154

body.text: rudanyāṃ saumanasyena samuttāraḥ / hasanyāṃ tūṣṇīṃbhāvena / āśīviṣāyāṃ sarpaviṣamantraprayogena samuttāro vetranadyāṃ
body.translated_text: 'In <s>Rudanī</s>, crossing is by means of cheerfulness; in <s>Hasanī</s>, by silence; in <s>Āśīviṣā</s>, by the application of anti-venom mantras; in the river <s>Vetrā</s>,

body.text: tīkṣṇaśastrasaṃpātayogena samuttāraḥ / nadīm atikramya pañcayakṣaśatānāṃ gulmakasthānam* / tad dhairyam āsthāya vidrāvyam* / tato drumasya kinnararājasya bhavanam iti /
body.translated_text: crossing is by means of wielding sharp weapons. Having crossed the rivers, there is the guard-post of five hundred <s>Yakṣas</s>. They are to be routed by mustering courage. Beyond that is the dwelling of <s>Druma</s>, the king of the <s>Kinnaras</s>.'

children.text: tataḥ sudhanaḥ kumāro yathopadiṣṭān oṣadhamantrāgadaprayogān samudānīya tasya ṛṣeḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā prakrāntaḥ / tatas tena yathopadiṣṭāḥ sarve samudānītāḥ sthāpayitvā vānaram* / tatas tān ādāya punar api tasya ṛṣeḥ sakāśam upasaṃkrāntaḥ / uktaś ca / alaṃ kumāra kim anena vyavasāyena kiṃ manoharayā / tvam ekākī asahāyaḥ śārīrasaṃśayam avāpsyasīti / kumāraḥ prāha / maharṣe 'vaśyam evāhaṃ prayāsyāmīti / kutaḥ
children.translated_text: Then prince <s>Sudhana</s>, having gathered the medicines, mantras, antidotes, and other provisions as instructed, bowed at that seer's feet and departed. He gathered everything as instructed, except for the monkey. Taking all of these, he again approached that seer. He was told: 'Enough, prince! What is the purpose of this endeavor? What use is <s>Manoharā</s>? You are alone, without companion — you will risk your very life.' The prince replied: 'Great seer, I shall certainly go forth.' And why?

children.text: candrasya khe vicarataḥ kva sahāyabhāvaḥ daṃṣṭrābalena balinaś ca mṛgādhipasya /
children.translated_text: 'Where is there a companion for the moon traversing the sky? Or for the mighty lord of beasts with the power of his fangs?

children.text: agneś ca dāvadahena kva sahāyabhāvaḥ asmadvidhasya ca sahāyabalena kiṃ syāt* //
children.translated_text: Where is there a companion for fire as it burns the forest? What need has one such as I for the strength of companions?'

children.text:
kiṃ bho mahārṇavajalaṃ na vigāhitavyaṃ kiṃ sarpaduṣṭa iti naiva cikitsanīyaḥ /
vīryaṃ bhajeta sumahadūrjitasatvadṛṣṭaṃ yatne kṛto yadi na sidhyati ko 'tra doṣaḥ // iti /
children.translated_text: 'Should one not plunge into the waters of the great ocean? Should the snake-bitten not be treated? One should embrace vigor, great, robust, seen by the resolute — if, after effort is made, success does not come, what fault is there?'

children.text: tataḥ sudhanaḥ kumāro manoharopadiṣṭena vidhinā saṃprasthito 'nupūrveṇa parvatanadīguhāprapātādīni bhaiṣajyamantrāgadaprayogena vinirjitya
children.translated_text: Then prince <s>Sudhana</s>, following the method instructed by <s>Manoharā</s>, set out and in due course, having conquered the mountains, rivers, caves, and precipices by means of medicines, mantras, and antidotes,
MSV I 155
he reached the vicinity of the dwelling of <s>Druma</s>, the king of the <s>Kinnaras</s>. The prince beheld
that city not far away, adorned with glorious gardens,
endowed with various flowers and fruits, frequented by various birds,
surrounded by ponds, reservoirs, and wells, and attended by <s>Kinnaras</s>.
There he saw <s>Kinnarī</s> maidens who had come for water.

body.text: tatas tāḥ sudhanakumāreṇābhihitāḥ / kim anena bahunā pānīyena kriyata iti / tāḥ kathayati / asti drumasya kinnararājasya duhitā manoharā nāma / sā manuṣyahastagatā babhūva / tasyāḥ sa manuṣyagandho naśyati / sudhanaḥ kumāraḥ pṛcchati / kim ete ghaṭāḥ samastāḥ sarve tasyā upari nipātyante āhosvid ānupūrveṇeti / tāḥ kathayanti / ānupūrvyā / sa saṃlakṣayati / śobhano 'yam
body.translated_text: Then prince <s>Sudhana</s> addressed them: 'What do you need so much water for?' They replied: 'There is a daughter of <s>Druma</s>, the king of the <s>Kinnaras</s>, named <s>Manoharā</s>. She fell into the hands of a human. Her human scent must be washed away.' Prince <s>Sudhana</s> asked: 'Are all these water-pots poured over her at once, or one after another?' They replied: 'One after another.' He reflected: 'This is an excellent

body.text: upāya imām aṃgulimudrām ekasmin ghaṭe prakṣipāmīti / tenaikasyāḥ kinnaryā ghaṭe 'nālakṣitaṃ prakṣiptā / sā ca kinnarī abhihitā / anena tvayā ghaṭena manoharā tatprathamataraṃ snāpayitavyā / sā saṃlakṣayati / nūnam atra kāryeṇa bhavitavyam* / tatas tayāsau ghaṭaḥ prathamataraṃ manoharāyā mūrdhni nipātito yāvad aṃgulimudrā utsaṅge nipatitā / sā manoharayā pratyabhijñātā / tataḥ kinnarīṃ pṛcchati / mā tatra kaścin manuṣyo 'bhyāgataḥ / sāha / abhyāgataḥ / gacchainaṃ pracchannaṃ praveśaya / tayā praveśitaḥ sugupte pradeśe sthāpitaḥ /
body.translated_text: stratagem — I shall drop this signet ring into one of the pots.' He dropped it unnoticed into the pot of one of the <s>Kinnarī</s> maidens. And he told that <s>Kinnarī</s>: 'With this pot of yours, you must bathe <s>Manoharā</s> first.' She reflected: 'Surely there must be some purpose here.' Then she poured that pot first over <s>Manoharā's</s> head, and the signet ring fell into her lap. <s>Manoharā</s> recognized it. She then asked the <s>Kinnarī</s>: 'Has a human man perhaps arrived there?' She replied: 'He has arrived.' 'Go and bring him in secretly.' She brought him in and placed him in a hidden spot.

children.text: tato manoharā pituḥ pādayor nipatya kathayati / tāta yady asau sudhanaḥ kumāra āgacched yenāhaṃ hṛtā tasya tvaṃ kiṃ kuryāḥ / sa kathayati / tam ahaṃ khaṇḍaśataṃ kṛtvā catasṛṣu dikṣu kṣipeyaṃ manuṣyaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Manoharā</s>, falling at her father's feet, said: 'Father, if that prince <s>Sudhana</s>, by whom I was taken, were to come, what would you do to him?' He replied: 'I would cut him into a hundred pieces and hurl them in the four directions. A human
MSV I 156

children.text: asau kiṃ teneti / manoharā kathayati / tāta manuṣyabhūtasya kuta ihāgamanam* / aham eva bravīmīti / tato drumasya kinnararājasya paryavasthāno vigataḥ / tato vigataparyavasthānaḥ kathayati / yady asau kumāra āgacchet tasya hi tvāṃ sarvālaṅkāravibhūṣitāṃ prabhūtacittopakaraṇaiḥ kinnarīsahasraparivṛtāṃ bhāryāratnaṃ dadyām iti / tato manoharayā hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramuditayā sudhanaḥ kumāro divyālaṅkāravibhūṣito drumasya kinnararājasyopadarśitaḥ / tato drumaḥ kinnararājaḥ sudhanaṃ kumāraṃ dadarśābhirūpaṃ darśanīyaṃ prāsādikaṃ paramayā śubhavarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgatam* / dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ paraṃ vismayam upagataḥ / tatas tasya vijñāsāṃ kartukāmena sauvarṇāstambhā ucchritāḥ sapta tālāḥ sapta bheryaḥ sapta śūkarāḥ / āha ca /
children.translated_text: — what is he to me?' <s>Manoharā</s> replied: 'Father, for a human being, how could there be a way to come here? I was merely speaking hypothetically.' Then <s>Druma</s>, the king of the <s>Kinnaras</s>, was freed from his agitation. Once his agitation had subsided, he said: 'If that prince were to come, I would give you to him as his wife-jewel, adorned with all ornaments, with abundant provisions for your pleasure, and attended by a thousand <s>Kinnarī</s> maidens.' Then <s>Manoharā</s>, joyful, delighted, and elated, adorned prince <s>Sudhana</s> with divine ornaments and presented him to <s>Druma</s>, the king of the <s>Kinnaras</s>. <s>Druma</s>, the king of the <s>Kinnaras</s>, beheld prince <s>Sudhana</s> — handsome, good-looking, pleasing, endowed with supreme beauty of complexion. Having seen him, he was filled with the greatest wonder. Then, wishing to test him, he had golden pillars erected, seven palm-trees, seven drums, and seven boars. And he said:

children.text: tvayā kāntyā jitās tāvad ete kinnaradārakāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'By your beauty, you have already surpassed these <s>Kinnara</s> youths;
but having displayed your prowess, you would be worthy of a divine alliance.'
'From an exceedingly tall reed-bed, pull out a reed in an instant,

children.text: vyuptam anyūnam uccitya punar dehi tilāḍhakam* /
children.translated_text: and having scattered and then gathered up every single sesame seed, return the <s>āḍhaka</s> (measure) of sesame.'
'Demonstrate in archery your skill in hitting firm targets and the like —
then this banner of glory, <s>Manoharā</s>, shall depend on you.'

children.text: sudhanaḥ kumāro bodhisatvaḥ / kuśalāś ca bhavanti bodhisatvās teṣu teṣu śilpasthānakarmasthāneṣu devatāś caiṣām autsukyam āpatsyante avighnabhāvāya / tato bodhisatvo nṛtyagītavīṇāpaṇavasughoṣakavallarīmṛdaṅgādinānāvidhena
children.translated_text: Prince <s>Sudhana</s> was a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. And <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are skilled in every art and craft, and the gods would feel eager to ensure his success without obstacles. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, surrounded by many thousands of <s>Kinnaras</s>, was filled on all sides with various divine musical instruments — dancing, singing, <s>vīṇā</s>, <s>paṇava</s> drum, <s>sughoṣaka</s>, <s>vallarī</s> lute, <s>mṛdaṅga</s> drum, and others —
MSV I 157

children.text: daivatyopasaṃhatena vāditraviśeṣeṇa samantād āpūryamāṇo 'nekaiḥ kinnarasahasraiḥ parivṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: accompanied by divine music of various kinds.
By <s>Yakṣas</s> in boar-form, dispatched by <s>Śatakratu</s> (<s>Indra</s>),
the reed-bed was uprooted, and on the leveled ground, the <s>āḍhaka</s> of sesame was scattered.
The seeds were gathered together by ants sent by <s>Śakra</s>,
and the prince presented the result to the astonished king of the <s>Kinnaras</s>.

children.text: nīlotpaladalābhenāsinā gṛhītena paśyato drumasya kinnararājasya sauvarṇastambhasamīpaṃ gatvā tān stambhān kadalīcchedena khaṇḍakhaṇḍaṃ chettum ārabdhaḥ / tatas tān tilaśo 'vakīrya sapta tālān sapta bherīḥ sapta ca śūkarān bāṇena vidhya sumeruvad akampyo 'vasthitaḥ / tato gaganatalasthābhir devatābhiś ca kinnaraśatasahasrair hāhākārakilikilāprakṣveḍoccair nādo mukto yaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca kinnararājaḥ paraṃ vismayam upagataḥ / tataḥ kinnarīsahasrasya manoharāsamānarūpasya madhye manoharāṃ sthāpayitvā sudhanaḥ kumāro 'bhihitaḥ / ehi kumāra pratyabhijānāsi manoharām iti / tataḥ sudhanaḥ kumāras tāṃ pratyabhijñāya gāthābhigītenoktavān* /
children.translated_text: Then, taking a sword gleaming like a blue lotus petal, before the very eyes of <s>Druma</s>, the king of the <s>Kinnaras</s>, he went near the golden pillars and began to cut those pillars to pieces as easily as slicing a plantain trunk. Then, having scattered them like sesame seeds, he pierced the seven palm-trees, the seven drums, and the seven boars with his arrows, and stood unshakable as Mount <s>Sumeru</s>. Then a great cry of "Hāhā!" and shrieks and cheers was raised by the deities stationed in the sky and by hundreds of thousands of <s>Kinnaras</s>. Seeing this, the king of the <s>Kinnaras</s> was filled with the utmost wonder. Then, having placed <s>Manoharā</s> in the midst of a thousand <s>Kinnarī</s> maidens, all of equal beauty to her, prince <s>Sudhana</s> was addressed: 'Come, prince, do you recognize <s>Manoharā</s>?' Then prince <s>Sudhana</s>, having recognized her, spoke in verse:

children.text: yathā drumasya duhitā mameha tvaṃ manoharā /
children.translated_text: 'Just as she is your daughter, <s>Manoharā</s> is mine here, O <s>Druma</s>;

children.text: śīghram etena satyena padaṃ vraja manohare //
children.translated_text: quickly, by the power of this truth, take a step forward, O <s>Manoharā</s>!'

body.text: tataḥ sā drutapadam abhikrāntā / kinnarāḥ kathayanti / devāyaṃ sudhanaḥ kumāro balavīryaparākramasamanvito manoharāyāḥ pratirūpaḥ / kimarthaṃ vipralabhya / dīyatām asya manohareti / tato drumaḥ kinnararājaḥ kinnaragaṇena saṃvarṇitaḥ sudhanaṃ kinnarābhimatena mahatā
body.translated_text: Then she stepped forward with quick steps. The <s>Kinnaras</s> said: 'Your Majesty, this prince <s>Sudhana</s> is endowed with strength, valor, and prowess, and is a fitting match for <s>Manoharā</s>. Why deceive him? Let <s>Manoharā</s> be given to him.' Then <s>Druma</s>, the king of the <s>Kinnaras</s>, praised by the assembly of <s>Kinnaras</s>, with great
MSV I 158

body.text: satkāreṇa puraskṛtya manoharāṃ divyālaṅkāravibhūṣitāṃ vāmena pāṇinā gṛhītvā dakṣiṇena sauvarṇabhṛṅgāraṃ
body.translated_text: with honor and reverence, holding <s>Manoharā</s>, adorned with divine ornaments, captivating, by the left hand, and with his right hand a golden ewer,

body.text: sudhanaḥ kumāro 'bhihitaḥ / kumāra eṣā te manoharā kinnarīparivṛtā bhāryārthāya dattā / aparicitā mānuṣāḥ / yathaināṃ na parityakṣyasīti / paraṃ tāteti sudhanaḥ kumāro drumasya kinnararājasya pratiśrutya kinnarabhavanastho manoharayā sārdhaṃ niṣpuruṣeṇa tūryeṇa kṛīḍate ramate paricārayati /
body.translated_text: Prince <s>Sudhana</s> was addressed: 'Prince, this <s>Manoharā</s>, attended by <s>Kinnarīs</s>, is given to you as a wife. Humans are unreliable. See that you do not abandon her.' 'Yes, father,' Prince <s>Sudhana</s> replied to <s>Druma</s>, the <s>Kinnara</s> king, and while dwelling in the <s>Kinnara</s> abode, he sported, enjoyed himself, and was attended to with <s>Manoharā</s>, accompanied by music played without human performers.

children.text: so 'pareṇa samayena svadeśam anusmṛtya mātāpitṛviyogajena duḥkhenātyāhato manoharāyā nivedayati / mātāpitṛviyogajaṃ me duḥkhaṃ bādhata iti / tato manoharayā eṣa vṛttānto vistareṇa pitur niveditaḥ / sa kathayati / gaccha kumāreṇa sārdham apakrāntayā te bhavitavyaṃ vipralambhakā manuṣyāḥ / tato drumeṇa kinnararājena prabhūtaṃ maṇimuktāsuvarṇādīn datvānupreṣitaḥ / sa manoharayā sārdham uparivihāyasā kinnarakhagapathena saṃprasthito 'nupūrveṇa hastināpuranagaram anuprāptaḥ / tato hastināpuraṃ nagaraṃ nānāmanohareṇa surabhiṇā gandhaviśeṣeṇa sarvadig āmoditam* / śrutvā dhanena rājñānandabheryaś ca tāḍitāḥ / sarvaṃ ca tan nagaram apagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakaṭhallaṃ kāritaṃ candanavārisiktam āmuktapaṭṭadāmakalāpasamucchritadhvajapatākaṃ surabhidhūpaghaṭikopanibaddhaṃ nānāpuṣpāvakīrṇaramaṇīyam* / tataḥ kumāro 'nekanaravarasahasraparivṛto manoharayā sārdhaṃ hastināpuraṃ
children.translated_text: At another time, remembering his own country and afflicted by the suffering of separation from his parents, he informed <s>Manoharā</s>: 'The suffering of separation from my parents presses upon me.' Then <s>Manoharā</s> reported this matter in detail to her father. He said: 'Go with the prince, but you must depart—humans are deceitful.' Then <s>Druma</s>, the <s>Kinnara</s> king, having given abundant gems, pearls, gold, and other treasures, sent him off. He set out with <s>Manoharā</s> through the sky by the aerial path of the <s>Kinnaras</s> and gradually arrived at the city of <s>Hastināpura</s>. Then the city of <s>Hastināpura</s> was pervaded in all directions by various delightful and fragrant scents. Having heard this, King <s>Dhana</s> had drums of joy beaten. The entire city was cleared of stones, gravel, and rubble, sprinkled with sandalwood water, adorned with unfurled banners of silk and festoons, with raised flags and pennants, furnished with fragrant incense-pots, and strewn with various flowers, making it delightful. Then the prince, accompanied by many thousands of excellent men, entered the city of <s>Hastināpura</s>
MSV I 159

children.text: nagaraṃ praviṣṭaḥ / tato mārgaśramaṃ prativinodya vividhāni ratnāny ādāya pituḥ sakāśam upasaṃkrāntaḥ / pitrā kaṇṭhe pariṣvaktaḥ pārśve rājāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ / kinnaranagaragamanāgamanaṃ ca vistareṇa samākhyātam* /
children.translated_text: together with <s>Manoharā</s>. Then, having dispelled the fatigue of the journey, he took various jewels and approached his father's presence. He attracted a certain householder as a follower. That householder had a <s>vihāra</s> built for him, equipped with all requisites. Then he sent word to his brother <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>: 'Come, let us dwell together in one place.' He heard and came. Then that householder saw him — of peaceful deportment, pleasing in body, and pleasing in mind. Seeing him, he was filled with faith. Then, with faith arisen, he satisfied him with choice food and covered him with a pair of precious garments. Then jealousy arose in <s>Bharadvāja</s>: 'I am his senior in all respects. Never has he covered me with a garment. Yet this one, who has only recently arrived, has been covered with a garment.' He began seeking faults in his brother <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>. <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> observed him and thought: 'This one is of a jealous nature. If I do not give him this pair of garments,

body.translated_text: Which is the unshared one? In a former time, O monks, in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> was ruling — his kingdom was prosperous, and so on in detail. At that time, there dwelt a courtesan named <s>Bhadrā</s>. And there was a rogue named <s>Mṛṇāla</s>. He had sent her garments and ornaments as a gift for her company. She put on those garments and ornaments. Then a certain man came with five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> and said: '<s>Bhadrā</s>, come, let us enjoy ourselves together.' She reflected: 'If I go, I will not receive the five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>. And it would be uncivil to refuse someone who has come to one's house and go elsewhere.' She told her maidservant: 'Go, tell <s>Mṛṇāla</s>: "The mistress says she is not yet ready; she will come later."'

body.translated_text: Then the angry crowd addressed the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>: 'You, O renunciant, bear the insignia of a sage! Is this what you do?' He said: 'What have I done?' They said: 'You had relations with <s>Bhadrā</s>. She has been killed.' He said: 'Peace! I am not the doer of this deed.' Though he spoke words of peace, the great crowd, having bound him tightly with his arms behind his back, brought him before the king: 'Your Majesty, this renunciant had relations with <s>Bhadrā</s> and she has been killed.' For kings are not given to investigation. He said: 'If so, go, have him executed. I abandon this renunciant.' Then, with a garland of <s>karavīra</s> flowers around his neck, surrounded by men in dark garments with drawn swords, he was proclaimed through the streets, alleys, crossroads, and intersections, and led out of the city toward the execution ground. Then <s>Mṛṇāla</s> the rogue had this thought: 'This wretched renunciant — innocent, without fault — has been falsely accused. He is now about to be executed. It would not be proper for me to remain indifferent.' Knowing this, he turned back, approached the king, fell at his feet, and said: 'Your Majesty, this renunciant is not the doer of this deed. This evil deed was done by me. Let this renunciant be released.' What do you think, monks? That rogue <s>Mṛṇāla</s> was none other than I at that time and on that occasion. Because I falsely accused a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, as the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, for many years, as before up to, I was cooked in the hells. And by the
MSV I 216
residue of that <s>karma</s>, I was falsely accused by <s>Caṃcā</s> the female wanderer. This is the unshared <s>karma</s>.

At that time, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Vairaṭṭasiṃha</s> was seated in that very assembly. Then the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Vairaṭṭasiṃha</s> addressed the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Nāgarabindavā</s> thus: 'I will demonstrate for you directly whether the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> is of few desires or of great desires, and whether his disciples are of few desires or great desires.' Then the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Vairaṭṭasiṃha</s> approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. body.translated_text: The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Vairaṭṭasiṃha</s> had five hundred pots of jaggery. Taking one pot of jaggery from each jaggery-store, he brought five hundred pots of jaggery and approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Let the <s>Bhagavān Gautama</s>, together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples, sit down. The jaggery is ready. Please consume it.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having washed his hands and bowl, sat upon a seat prepared before the assembly of monks. Then the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Vairaṭṭasiṃha</s> took one pot of jaggery and began to distribute it. The <s>Bhagavān</s> exercised such a supernatural determination that, when it was distributed to the entire <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks, the rest remained just as full. Then the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Vairaṭṭasiṃha</s> was filled with deep faith. Having been moved to faith, he proclaimed far and wide: 'The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> is of few desires, good people! And his disciples are of few desires!' Then he invited the sectarians. They consumed jaggery. But those sectarians took jaggery without moderation. Some filled their pouches, took more, and set off. Then the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Vairaṭṭasiṃha</s> said: 'You fools are the ones of great desires! But the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> is of few desires, and his disciples are of few desires.' Having said this, with even greater faith in the <s>Bhagavān</s>, he approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he exchanged various greetings and pleasantries with the <s>Bhagavān</s> and sat down to one side. Then the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Vairaṭṭasiṃha</s>, joining his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May I, Venerable Sir, obtain the going forth, full ordination, and the state of a monk in the well-taught <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, (

body.text: ) pravrajyām upasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvaṃ careyam ahaṃ bhagavato 'ntike brahmacaryam iti / tato bhagavatā ehibhikṣukayā ābhāṣitaḥ / ehi bhikṣo cara brahmacaryam iti / pūrvavad yāvan nopasthito buddhamanorathena / {MS:

body.text: tatra bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma / tasmād anujānāmi kālena vākalena vā glānena vāglānena vā guḍaḥ paribhoktavyaḥ / nātra kaukṛtyaṃ karaṇīyam iti /
body.translated_text: There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'Therefore I permit that jaggery may be consumed at the proper time or at an improper time, by one who is ill or not ill. No scruple need be felt about this.'

body.text: āyuṣmān vairaṭṭasiṃhaḥ kuṇapadaurgandhyena cittaikāgratāṃ nārāgayati / bhagavān saṃlakṣayati / vairaṭṭasiṃho bhikṣuś caramabhavikaḥ kimarthaṃ satyāni na paśyatīti / saṃlakṣayati / kuṇapadaurgandhyavihāram* / pūrvavad yāvat* / tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate sma / gacchānanda vairaṭṭasiṃhasya bhikṣor vihāraṃ gandhair mālyair dhūpaiś cūrṇaiḥ saṃskuru / śayanāsanaṃ ca dhūpaya / surabhikusumopacitaṃ ca puṣpavitānaṃ vitanv iti / evaṃ bhadantety āyuṣmān ānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya yāvad asau piṇḍapātaṃ gatas tāvat tasya vihāraṃ gatvā bhagavatopadiṣṭena vidhinā sarvam anuṣṭhitavān* /
body.translated_text: The venerable <s>Vairaṭṭasiṃha</s> could not attain one-pointed concentration of mind because of the stench of putrefaction. The <s>Bhagavān</s> reflected: 'This monk <s>Vairaṭṭasiṃha</s> is in his last existence. Why does he not see the truths?' He reflected: 'It is the dwelling with its stench of putrefaction.' As before, up to: There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, prepare the dwelling of the monk <s>Vairaṭṭasiṃha</s> with perfumes, garlands, incense, and powders. Fumigate his bed and seat. And spread a canopy of fragrant flowers.' 'Yes, Venerable Sir,' the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. While <s>Vairaṭṭasiṃha</s> was away on his alms-round, <s>Ānanda</s> went to his dwelling and arranged everything as instructed by the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: athāyuṣmān vairaṭṭasiṃhaḥ piṇḍapātam aṭitvā vihāram āgataḥ / paśyati divyāṃ vibhūtim* / tataḥ prītamanāḥ piṇḍapātaṃ paribhujya kṛtabhaktakṛtyo bahir vihārasya pādau prakṣālya vihāraṃ prāviśat* / praviśya niṣaṇṇaḥ paryaṅkam ābhujya ṛjuṃ kāyaṃ praṇidhāya pratimukhāṃ smṛtim upasthāpya (
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Vairaṭṭasiṃha</s>, having gone on his alms-round, returned to the dwelling. He saw a divine splendor. Then, with a delighted mind, having consumed his alms-food, having completed his meal, having washed his feet outside the dwelling, he entered the dwelling. Having entered and sat down, he crossed his legs, straightened his body, established mindfulness before him, (

body.text: ) tasya sugandhaṃ ghrātvā cittasamādhānam utpannam* / tatas tena sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* / pūrvavad yāvad abhivādyaś ca (
body.translated_text: ) Having smelled that fragrance, concentration of mind arose in him. Thereupon, through the abandonment of all afflictions, he directly realized <s>arhatva</s> (the state of an arhat). As before, up to: he became worthy of veneration (

body.text: bhikṣavo bhikṣūṇāṃ mama śrāvakāṇāṃ śubhādhimuktānāṃ yaduta vairaṭṭasiṃho bhikṣuḥ / bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ / paśya bhadanta anye bhikṣavaḥ śubhayādhimuktāḥ / āyuṣmāṃs tu vairaṭṭasiṃhaḥ śubhayādhimukta iti / bhagavān āha /
body.translated_text: among my monk disciples who are inclined to the beautiful (<s>śubhādhimukta</s>), namely the monk <s>Vairaṭṭasiṃha</s>.' The monks, having doubts, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, who resolves all doubts: 'See, venerable sir, other monks are inclined to the beautiful through beauty. But the venerable <s>Vairaṭṭasiṃha</s> is inclined to the beautiful through beauty.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: eṣa bhikṣavaḥ paṃca janmaśatāni nirantaraṃ trayastriṃśebhyo devebhyaś cyutvā teṣv evopapannaḥ / idānīṃ carame bhave manuṣyeṣūpapannaḥ / kuṇapagandhaṃ ghrātvā cittaikāgratāṃ nāsāditavān* / sugandhaṃ tu ghrātvā cittasamādhānaṃ pratilabhya śubhayādhimuktaḥ / yady asyāyam upacāro na kṛto 'bhaviṣyad ūṣmagatam apy anena notpāditam abhaviṣyad iti / tasmād anujānāmi yo 'py anya evaṃ śubhādhimuktas tasyāpy evaṃrūpānupūrvī kartavyā / nātra kaukṛtyaṃ karaṇīyam* /
body.translated_text: 'This monk, for five hundred births without interruption, having passed away from the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-three) gods, was reborn among them again. Now, in his final existence, he was born among humans. Having smelled the odor of a corpse, he could not attain one-pointedness of mind. But having smelled a fragrance, he obtained concentration of mind and became inclined to the beautiful. If this special approach had not been applied for him, he would not have produced even the warmth stage. Therefore I permit: for anyone else who is likewise inclined to the beautiful, the same procedure should be followed. No scruple need be felt about this.'

body.text: atha bhagavān vṛjiṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ caran vaiśālīm anuprāpto vaiśālyāṃ viharati markaṭahradatīre kūṭāgāraśālāyām* / aśrauṣur vaiśālakā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo bhagavān vṛjiṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ caran vaiśālīm anuprāpto vaiśālyāṃ viharati markaṭahradatīre kūṭāgāraśālāyām iti / śrutvā ca punar ekadhye sannipatya kathayati / bhavantaḥ śrūyate bhagavān vṛjiṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ caran vaiśālīm anuprāpto vaiśālyāṃ viharati markaṭahradatīre kūṭāgāraśālāyām iti / yady asmākam ekaiko bhagavantam upanimantrya bhojayiṣyati bhagavān viprakramiṣyati / anye 'vakāśaṃ na lapsyante / (

children.translated_text: MSV I 225

children.text: ) tat kriyākāraṃ vyavasthāpayāmo yathā gaṇa eva sambhūya bhagavantaṃ bhojayati na tv ekapuruṣa iti / te kriyākāraṃ kṛtvā vyavasthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: ) Therefore let us establish a rule that the assembly, having gathered together, feeds the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and not a single individual.' They established the rule and abided by it.

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, wandering on a journey through the <s>Vṛji</s> territories, arrived at <s>Vaiśālī</s> and dwelt in <s>Vaiśālī</s> at the Monkey Pond, in the Gabled Hall. The <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Vaiśālī</s> heard that the <s>Bhagavān</s>, wandering on a journey through the <s>Vṛji</s> territories, had arrived at <s>Vaiśālī</s> and was dwelling in <s>Vaiśālī</s> at the Monkey Pond, in the Gabled Hall. Having heard this, they gathered together and said: 'Sirs, it is heard that the <s>Bhagavān</s>, wandering on a journey through the <s>Vṛji</s> territories, has arrived at <s>Vaiśālī</s> and is dwelling in <s>Vaiśālī</s> at the Monkey Pond, in the Gabled Hall. If each of us individually invites the <s>Bhagavān</s> and feeds him, the <s>Bhagavān</s> will depart and others will not get the opportunity. (

body.text: tena khalu samayena vaiśālyāṃ catvāro mahāpuṇyāḥ prativasanti / dhaniko dhanikapatnī dhanikaputro dhanikasnuṣā ca / teṣāṃ divyamānuṣyaśrīr gṛhe prādurbhūtā / tair asau kriyākāro na śrutaḥ / aśrauṣīd dhaniko gṛhapatir bhagavān vṛjiṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ caran vaiśālīm anuprāpto vaiśālyāṃ viharati markaṭahradatīre kūṭāgāraśālāyām iti / śrutvā ca punar vaiśālyā niṣkramya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / pūrvavad yāvat saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm* / atha dhaniko gṛhapatir utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṃgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃs tenāṃjaliṃ praṇamayya bhagavantam idam avocat* / adhivāsayatu bhagavān me śvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktena sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃgheneti / adhivāsayati bhagavān dhanikasya gṛhe tūṣṇīṃbhāvena / atha dhaniko gṛhapatir bhagavatas tūṣṇīṃbhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ /
body.translated_text: At that time, in <s>Vaiśālī</s>, there dwelt four persons of great merit: <s>Dhanika</s>, <s>Dhanika</s>'s wife, <s>Dhanika</s>'s son, and <s>Dhanika</s>'s daughter-in-law. In their house, divine and human prosperity had appeared. They had not heard that rule. The householder <s>Dhanika</s> heard that the <s>Bhagavān</s>, wandering on a journey through the <s>Vṛji</s> territories, had arrived at <s>Vaiśālī</s> and was dwelling in <s>Vaiśālī</s> at the Monkey Pond, in the Gabled Hall. Having heard, he departed from <s>Vaiśālī</s> and approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. As before, up to: having gladdened him, he fell silent. Then the householder <s>Dhanika</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, extending his joined palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> consent to accept a meal tomorrow in my house together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> accepted the householder <s>Dhanika</s>'s invitation through silence. Then the householder <s>Dhanika</s>, having understood the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s acceptance through silence, paid homage at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet with his head and departed from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence.

body.text: puruṣaḥ śvo bhojayatu / vayaṃ paraśvo bhojayiṣyāma iti /
body.translated_text: 'Let the man feed him tomorrow. We shall feed him the day after tomorrow.'

body.text: athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kālyam evotthāya pātracīvaram ādāya yena dhanikasya gṛhapater niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / upasaṃkramya pūrveṇa nagaradvāreṇa praviṣṭaḥ / yāvat paśyati nāsanaprajñaptiṃ na bhaktaṃ sajjīkṛtam* / tato dhanikaṃ gṛhapatim idam avocat* / gṛhapate tvaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃgham upanimantryālpotsukaḥ sthita iti / sa kathayati / kim āryānandaiva kathayasi gṛhapate nāsanaprajñaptiṃ paśyāmi nāpy āhāraṃ sajjīkṛtam* / ārya katareṇa tvaṃ dvāreṇa praviṣṭaḥ / gṛhapate pūrveṇa nagaradvāreṇa / ārya dakṣiṇena praviśa / sa dakṣiṇena praviṣṭo yāvat paśyati divyām āsanaprajñaptiṃ kṛtāṃ divyaṃ cāhāram upanvāhṛtam* / dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ paraṃ vismayam āpannaḥ / atha dhaniko gṛhapatir bhagavato dūtena kālam ārocayati / samayo bhadanta sajjaṃ bhaktam* / apīdānīṃ pūrvavad bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastam apanītapātraṃ nīcataram āsanaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya /
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having risen early in the morning, taken his bowl and robes, approached the dwelling of the householder <s>Dhanika</s>. Having approached, he entered through the eastern gate of the city. He saw that no seats had been arranged and no food had been prepared. Then he addressed the householder <s>Dhanika</s> thus: 'Householder, you invited the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>, yet you stand about with little enthusiasm.' He replied: 'Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, why do you say that, householder? I see no arrangement of seats and no food prepared.' 'Venerable one, through which gate did you enter?' 'Householder, through the eastern city gate.' 'Venerable one, enter through the southern gate.' He entered through the southern gate. There he saw divine arrangements of seats prepared and divine food brought out. Having seen this, he was struck with great amazement. Then the householder <s>Dhanika</s> informed the <s>Bhagavān</s> of the time through a messenger: 'The time has come, venerable sir; the meal is ready.' As before, up to: knowing the <s>Bhagavān</s> had finished eating, with hands washed and bowl put away, having taken a lower seat, he sat before the <s>Bhagavān</s> to hear the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.translated_text: addressed <s>Dhanika</s>'s son thus: 'Householder's son, you invited the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>; why do you stand about with so little enthusiasm?' He replied: 'Venerable one, why do you say that? I see no arrangement of seats and no food prepared.' 'Venerable one, through which gate did you enter?' 'Through the southern gate.' 'Venerable one, enter through the western gate.' He entered. There he saw a splendid arrangement of seats and excellent food brought out. Having seen this, he was struck with great amazement. Then <s>Dhanika</s>'s son informed the <s>Bhagavān</s> of the time through a messenger: 'The time has come, venerable sir; the meal is ready. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> come when he deems it the right time.' As before, up to: with hands washed and bowl put away, having taken a lower seat, he sat before the <s>Bhagavān</s> to hear the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.translated_text: Then the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Vaiśālī</s> approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, they paid homage at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet with their heads and sat down to one side. To the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Vaiśālī</s> seated to one side, the <s>Bhagavān</s> instructed, inspired, encouraged, and gladdened them with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, then fell silent. Then the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, rising from their seats, arranging their upper robes over one shoulder, extending their joined palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> consent to accept a meal tomorrow in our house together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'I have already been invited, <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>, first by <s>Dhanika</s>'s daughter-in-law.' Then the people of <s>Vaiśālī</s> (

body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, rising early in the morning, having taken his bowl and robes, approached the residence of the householder. Having approached, he entered through the western gate. He saw that no seats had been prepared, nor had food been brought out. Having seen this, he spoke thus to <s>Dhanika</s>'s daughter-in-law: '<s>Dhanika</s>'s daughter-in-law, having invited the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>, why do you stand so unconcerned?' She replied: 'Do not say so. I do not see any seats prepared, nor any food made ready. Noble sir, through which gate did you enter?' 'Through the western one.' 'Noble sir, enter through the northern one.' He entered through the northern gate. There he saw divine seats arranged and divine food brought out. Having seen this, he was filled with the utmost wonder. Then <s>Dhanika</s>'s daughter-in-law sent a messenger to announce the meal-time to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. (

body.translated_text: ) He went out and began to apologize. They said: 'Householder, is it only you who has wealth, that you feed the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> every day while we do not even get an opportunity?' He replied: 'Good people, I had not heard about the assembly's established practice. May the assembly be pleased to forgive.' Others said: 'Good people, this is a leading man; let him be forgiven.' They forgave him. He said: 'If so, please enter.' They entered the house. They saw splendid seats arranged and excellent food brought out. Having seen this, they were filled with the utmost wonder and said: 'Householder, you alone are worthy of feeding the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>, not us.' He gave them jewels. They did not accept. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said to them: 'Accept them; such jewels are rare.' They accepted. And whatever kind each person took, his own complexion took on that very luster. Then <s>Dhanika</s>'s daughter-in-law, having ascertained that the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> was comfortably seated, served them with pure, choice hard and soft foods — as before up to: with hands washed and bowls put away, having taken a lower seat, he sat before the <s>Bhagavān</s> to hear the <s>Dharma</s>.

May you consider us lay followers (<s>upāsakas</s>), from this day forth, for as long as life lasts, who have taken refuge and are of clear faith.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having instructed, inspired, encouraged, and gladdened <s>Dhanika</s>, <s>Dhanika</s>'s wife, <s>Dhanika</s>'s son, and <s>Dhanika</s>'s daughter-in-law with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, rose from his seat and departed.

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having known the disposition, latent tendencies, temperament, and nature of <s>Dhanika</s>, <s>Dhanika</s>'s wife, <s>Dhanika</s>'s son, and <s>Dhanika</s>'s daughter-in-law, delivered a teaching on the <s>Dharma</s> leading to the penetration of the Four Noble Truths. Having heard it, <s>Dhanika</s>, <s>Dhanika</s>'s wife, <s>Dhanika</s>'s son, and <s>Dhanika</s>'s daughter-in-law, having shattered with the vajra of knowledge the mountain of the view of the personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) rising with twenty peaks, directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>). body.translated_text: The monks, having doubts, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, who resolves all doubts: 'Venerable sir, what <s>karma</s> was performed by <s>Dhanika</s>, <s>Dhanika</s>'s wife, <s>Dhanika</s>'s son, and <s>Dhanika</s>'s daughter-in-law, that by the ripening of that <s>karma</s> they were born in a wealthy family of great riches and great resources, and experience both divine and human splendor? And they attained the vision of truth in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'By these very ones, O monks, <s>karmas</s> were performed and accumulated, their requisites gathered, their conditions matured, standing ready like a flood, inevitable — as before up to: indeed they bear fruit for embodied beings.'

children.translated_text: <s>ṃkara</s>. The countryside became prosperous and flourishing. The followers of other sects, together with the townspeople, sent spies: 'Go, see what the countryside looks like.' They went and saw that the countryside was exceedingly prosperous and flourishing. They came back and reported: 'Good sirs, never before have we seen the countryside so prosperous and flourishing.' The followers of other sects said: 'Good people, you have seen how he commands even inanimate things—will he not command you? So whence this? In any case, look well, good people. This is your last sight of us; we are leaving.' They said: 'Noble sirs, stay. What will the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> do to you? He too is a renunciant, and you too are renunciants. He lives on alms—will he prevent you from receiving alms?' The followers of other sects said: 'We will stay on one condition. If you make a formal agreement that no one shall go to see the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>—whoever goes shall be fined sixty <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>.' They agreed and made the formal agreement.

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, in due course, arrived at the city of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s> and dwelt at <s>Bhadraṃkara</s> in the Southern Quarter. At that time, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> girl from <s>Kapilavastu</s> had been married in the city of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s>. Standing on the city wall, she saw the <s>Bhagavān</s> standing in the darkness. She reflected: 'This <s>Bhagavān</s>, the joy of the <s>Śākya</s> clan, renounced the kingdom from the <s>Śākya</s> family and went forth. If there were a stairway here, I would take a lamp and go down to him.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing her mind with his own, created a stairway. Then she, delighted and overjoyed, taking a lamp, descended by the stairway and approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, she placed the lamp before the <s>Bhagavān</s>, paid homage at his feet with her head, and sat down to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing her disposition, latent tendencies, constitution, and nature, gave such a teaching leading to the penetration of the Four Noble Truths, as before up to: she took refuge and became deeply faithful. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed that girl: 'Come, girl, go to the householder <s>Miṇḍha</s>-

body.translated_text: The townspeople said: 'Householder, is it good to see the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>?' He replied: 'It is good.' They said: 'If so, the assembly itself established the rule — let the assembly itself revoke it. What objection is there?' They revoked the rule and began to go out. Then, because of the crowding against each other, they were unable to get out. The <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, out of compassion for the people to be disciplined, hurled his thunderbolt. A section of the wall fell down. Many hundreds of thousands of beings went out — some out of curiosity, some impelled by former roots of merit. From the gathering of the great multitude, an assembly congregated for a <s>yojana</s> (league) around the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having entered that assembly, sat upon a seat prepared before the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks and delivered a teaching on the <s>Dharma</s> that implanted roots of merit in the mind-streams of many hundreds of beings. Having heard it, some directly realized the fruit of stream-entry. As before, some took the refuges and training rules. Because the <s>Bhagavān</s> had been teaching the <s>Dharma</s> for a very long time, the mealtime had passed.

children.translated_text: ) a drought is proclaimed; there will be a famine requiring subsistence by ration-tickets, and it will bring white bones. Those who have provisions for twelve years should remain. Those who do not may go wherever they wish. When the famine has passed and abundance returns, come back.' At that time in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a certain householder was wealthy, of great riches, great fortune, with an extensive and ample retinue. He summoned the storekeeper and said: 'Good man, will there be provisions for me and my household for twelve years?' He replied: 'Sir, there will be.' So he remained there. The famine came immediately. His stores were exhausted. All his household died. Only he and five others remained. Then that householder, having swept out his storehouses, gathered together one <s>prastha</s> (measure) of grain. His wife put it in a pot and prepared it. In the absence of the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) arise in the world—compassionate toward the lowly and wretched, content with humble lodgings and food, worthy of individual offerings to the world. A certain <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, wandering on a journey through the countryside, arrived at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. In the forenoon, having put on his robes and taken his bowl, he entered <s>Vārāṇasī</s> for alms. The householder stood ready to eat. That <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, going on his alms-round in order, reached his house. The householder saw him—pleasing in body and mind. Having seen him, he reflected: 'Even if I eat this, I will surely die. Let me give my share to this renunciant.' He told his wife: 'My dear, give my share to this renunciant.' (

Then all of them together offered the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> the entire alms-food. The teaching of those great souls is through the body, not through words. Spreading his wings like a royal swan, he rose into the sky and began to perform miracles of blazing, burning, raining, and lightning. Swiftly does the supernatural power of a common person sway minds. They, like trees cut at the root, fell at his feet and began to make aspirations as they wished. The householder began his aspiration: 'By the merit of this offering to such a true field worthy of gifts, may I, by this root of merit—if I see my storehouses empty—at the very sight of them may they be full. And may I obtain such qualities. And may I please a teacher more excellent than this one, and never displease him.' The wife began her aspiration: 'By the merit of this offering to such a true field worthy of gifts, by this root of merit, if I cook a single pot for one person's sake, may it not be exhausted even when a hundred consume it, even a thousand, so long as my effort is not relaxed. May I obtain such qualities. And may I please a teacher more excellent than this one, and never displease him.' The son began his aspiration: 'By the merit of this offering to such a true field worthy of gifts, by this root of merit, may five hundred purses be fastened at my waist. children.translated_text: Then the householder had a bell proclamation made in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>: 'Whoever, good people, is in need of food, let him come.' A loud, great noise arose in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. The king heard it. He said: 'What is this loud, great noise, good people?' The ministers informed him: 'Your Majesty, such-and-such a householder has opened his storehouses.' The king said: 'When practically everyone has died, this householder opens his storehouses? Summon that householder, good people.' He was summoned. Then the king said: 'Householder, when everyone has died, you open your storehouses?' 'Your Majesty, whose storehouses have been opened? Rather, my seed was sown today and has borne fruit today.' The king said: 'How so?' He reported the entire matter in detail. The king said: 'Householder, you offered that great soul alms-food?' 'Your Majesty, I did.' He spoke a verse:

body.translated_text: In a former time, O monks, in this very auspicious <s>kalpa</s> (aeon), when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, a teacher named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world. As before up to: teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.translated_text: Having heard that teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, the seer <s>Kaineya</s> was filled with the utmost wonder and was filled with faith toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.translated_text: Then the sage <s>Kaineya</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, and with joined palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said to him: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> consent to a meal tomorrow together with the <s>Bhikṣusaṃgha</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> consented to the sage <s>Kaineya</s> through silence. Then the sage <s>Kaineya</s>, having understood the <s>Bhagavān's</s> consent through silence, rose from his seat and departed. The <s>Bhagavān</s> too disappeared from the bank of the <s>Mandākinī</s> lotus-pond and appeared at <s>Ādumā</s> together with the <s>Bhikṣusaṃgha</s>. Then the sage <s>Kaineya</s>, rising early that night, addressed his community:

Then the sage <s>Śaila</s>, with mindfulness focused on the <s>Buddha</s>, rising early in the morning with his retinue of five hundred, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May I, Venerable Sir, receive ordination, full ordination, and the status of a monk in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>? May I practice the holy life in the <s>Bhagavān's</s> presence.' The sage <s>Śaila</s> with his retinue of five hundred received ordination, full ordination, and the status of a monk in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>.

body.translated_text: At that time, a sage named <s>Śaila</s>, the nephew of the sage <s>Kaineya</s>, had come to spend the night at that lodging. The sage <s>Śaila</s> heard the sage <s>Kaineya</s> rising early that night and addressing his community. Having heard, he said to the sage <s>Kaineya</s>: 'Have your fellow practitioners been invited, sage? Or King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s>? Or the people of the realm? Or has the accomplishment of some desired sage-practice been fulfilled?' He replied: 'No, <s>Śaila</s>, my fellow practitioners have not been invited, nor King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s>, nor the people of the realm, nor has any desired sage-practice been fulfilled. But I have invited the <s>Bhikṣusaṃgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s> for a meal.' Upon hearing the word '<s>Buddha</s>' — a word he had never heard before — all his hair stood on end. With reverence, he asked: 'Who is this one called <s>Buddha</s>, sage?' 'There is, <s>Śaila</s>, an ascetic <s>Gautama</s>, a son of the <s>Śākyas</s>, who, having shaved his hair and beard from the <s>Śākya</s> clan, donned saffron robes, and with right faith went forth from the household life to homelessness. He has awakened to unsurpassed, perfect awakening. He is the one called <s>Buddha</s>.' <s>Śaila</s> asked: 'Who is this one called <s>Saṃgha</s>, sage?' The sage <s>Kaineya</s> replied: 'There are, <s>Śaila</s>, sons of good family from the <s>Kṣatriya</s> class who, having shaved their hair and beard, donned saffron robes, and with right faith went forth from the household life to homelessness. There are also sons of good family from the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> class, from the <s>Vaiśya</s> class — as before — who have gone forth following that very <s>Bhagavān</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly awakened one. That, sage, is what is called the <s>Saṃgha</s>.' 'And this <s>Saṃgha</s>, <s>Śaila</s>, and the

children.translated_text: passed away. Then his students, tormented by the grief and sorrow of separation from their teacher, wandered here and there and approached that second sage. He saw them with tear-filled eyes and asked: 'Students, your teacher has passed away.' He reflected: 'After my passing, these students will be in a similar condition. Let me take them under my care.' He consoled and adopted them. Then at another time, that sage too fell ill. He had three chief disciples. To the first he gave five hundred, to the second two hundred and fifty, and to the third two hundred and fifty. He passed away in the natural course of time. There, the one who received five hundred instructed them so that they became established in the formless realm. The one who received two hundred and fifty instructed them so that they became established in the form realm. The one who also received two hundred and fifty instructed them so that they became established in the five supernatural knowledges. What do you think, monks? The sage who established the five hundred students in the formless realm is none other than the monk <s>Kapphiṇa</s> at that time and on that occasion. The one who established two hundred and fifty in the form realm is none other than the monk <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>. The one who established the two hundred and fifty in the five supernatural knowledges is none other than the monk <s>Śāriputra</s>. However, monks, those instructed by <s>Kapphiṇa</s> were of sharp faculties; those instructed by <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> were of medium faculties; those instructed by <s>Śāriputra</s> were of dull faculties. If they had not been instructed by <s>Śāriputra</s>, even those at the stage of warmth would have fallen into ruin.

by fame and infamy — he is untouched, as a lotus by water.'

body.translated_text: 'By gain and loss, by happiness and suffering, by blame and praise,

children.translated_text: 'He abstains from the taking of life, he does not delight in what is not given,
truthful, celibate, he has refrained from slander.'
'He does not utter harsh speech; he speaks pleasantly and at the right time;

children.translated_text: '"Welcome to you too, O <s>Śaila</s>; sit down on this seat;
