children.text: niṣadya brāhmaṇaḥ śailo lakṣaṇān īkṣate muneḥ //
children.translated_text: having sat down, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Śaila</s> examined the marks of the sage.'
'He saw thirty marks on the body of the Lord of the World;
but <s>Śaila</s> had doubt about two — the sheathed tongue and the concealed organ.'

about the marks of the great sage,
he questioned the one of the <s>Āṅgirasa</s> lineage, the truly named, the fully awakened one.'

body.translated_text: 'Uncertain and perplexed,

children.translated_text: '"I have heard of thirty-two marks of a great sage;

children.text: dvayaṃ tatra na paśyāmi tava gātreṣu gautama //
children.translated_text: but two among them I do not see on your body, O <s>Gautama</s>."'
'"Is the sheath-concealed male organ indeed present in you here?

children.text: rasanānuttamā vāpi kaccij jihvā na hrasvikā //
children.translated_text: And is your tongue unsurpassed — is it not short?"'
'"Are you one of ample tongue? Let me know, O great sage;
extend it outward, this slender one — dispel my doubt."'
'"Rarely, at some time in the world, do Guides appear;

children.text: udumbare vā kusumaṃ durlabho hi mahāmuniḥ //
children.translated_text: like a flower on a fig tree — rare indeed is a great sage."'

children.text: vāri grīṣmābhitapto vā bhojanaṃ vā bubhukṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: '"As one scorched by summer heat seeks water, or one hungry seeks food,
or as a sick man seeks medicine, so we attend upon the Teacher."'
'With a full, unwavering voice, with the sound of a <s>kalaviṅka</s> bird,

children.text: buddhaḥ pratyavadac chailaṃ kāṃkṣāṃ brāhmaṇa nirṇuda //
children.translated_text: the <s>Buddha</s> replied to <s>Śaila</s>: "Dispel your doubt, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>."'

children.text: ubhe ca cakṣuṣī śrotre pracchādayati jihvayā /
children.translated_text: 'He covered both eyes and both ears with his tongue,
and with that ample tongue he covered the surface of his face.'
'Through his supernatural power he also displayed — skilled in the bases of psychic power.'

children.text: adrākṣīd brāhmaṇa śailo guhyaṃ koṣāvṛtaṃ muniḥ //
children.translated_text: The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Śaila</s> saw the sage's private parts sheathed. //
With the thorn of doubt removed, free from hesitation, regarding the marks of the great sage,
with a delighted mind and resolve, <s>Śaila</s> raised his voice: //

children.text: mantreṣv āptāni me yāni dvātriṃśal lakṣaṇāny aham* /
children.translated_text: 'The thirty-two marks that I have learned in the mantras —

children.text: sarvaṃ tat tava gātreṣu paripūrṇam anūnakam* //
children.translated_text: all of them are fulfilled on your body, complete and lacking nothing. //
Of auspicious speech, of good conduct, well-born, pleasant to behold,
in the midst of the assembly of ascetics, you shine like the sun. //
What need is there of the ascetic's state for you, of supreme complexion?

children.text: rājā tvam arho bhavituṃ cakravartī nararṣabhaḥ //
children.translated_text: You are worthy of being a king, a <s>Cakravartin</s>, a bull among men. //
Endowed with a fourfold army and with the seven jewels,

children.text: vartayati kṣitau cakraṃ rājā bhava mahīpatiḥ //
children.translated_text: you would turn the wheel upon the earth — be a king, a lord of the earth!' //

children.text: rājāham asmi śaileti dharmarājo hy anuttaraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I am a king, O <s>Śaila</s> — the unsurpassed king of <s>Dharma</s>;
by <s>Dharma</s> I turn the wheel here upon the circle of the earth. //

children.text: kalyo 'smy ahaṃ kule jātaḥ kṣatriyo 'smy abhijātitaḥ /
children.translated_text: I am fit, born of a noble family, a <s>Kṣatriya</s> by birth;

children.text: vitrāsya sabalaṃ māraṃ prāptaḥ saṃbodhim uttamām* //
children.translated_text: having terrified <s>Māra</s> together with his army, I have attained the supreme awakening. //

children.text: smṛtir brāhmaṇa cakraṃ me prajñā me parināyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Mindfulness, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, is my wheel; wisdom is my guide;

children.text: vīryaṃ hayaḥ śīghrajavo dhuraṃ vahati coditaḥ /
children.translated_text: vigor is the swift-running horse that draws the yoke when urged on;

children.text: samādhir me maṇiśreṣṭho hy andhakāro prabhākaraḥ //
children.translated_text: concentration is my foremost gem, the light-giver in the darkness. //

body.text: upekṣā hastināgaś ca dhuraṃ vahati coditaḥ //
body.translated_text: Equanimity is the bull-elephant that draws the yoke when urged on. //

children.text: strī vai ratiḥ sarāgāṇāṃ prītir brāhmaṇa me ratiḥ /
children.translated_text: A wife is the delight of those with desire; joy, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, is my delight;

children.text: prasṛṣṭaṃ brāhmaṇa śreṣṭhaṃ dhanaṃ gṛhagataṃ mayā //
children.translated_text: relinquished by me, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, is the best wealth that was in the house. //
The seven jewels of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>) transcend all worlds;

children.text: prabodhayāmi yaiḥ suptām andhabhūtām imāṃ prajām* //
children.translated_text: with them I awaken this sleeping, blinded humanity. //

children.text: jitā mayā diśaḥ sarvāḥ pratiśatrur na vidyate /
children.translated_text: All directions have been conquered by me; no adversary exists;

children.text: catasro me parṣadaś ca caturaṃgaṃ balaṃ mama //
children.translated_text: my four assemblies are my fourfold army. //
I dwell in a city frequented by former <s>Buddhas</s>,
furnished with parks of supernatural power, with crossroads built by the path. //
Filled with <s>sūtras</s> and <s>jātakas</s>, frequented by great beings,
the three gates of liberation, guarded by the protection of mindfulness. //
Endowed with modesty and conscience, I am a king, a <s>Tathāgata</s>;
a <s>Dharma</s>-battle has been given by me; the drum of <s>Dharma</s> has been struck. //
Having conquered <s>Māra</s> the variegated one together with his army, I am anointed for awakening;
well-cultivated and immeasurable are my ornaments. //
The four <s>Brahmā-vihāras</s> (divine abodes) ward off the afflictions;
rival doctrines have been defeated, demolished, and uprooted. //

children.text: mama samyaktvaṃ loke 'sminn ālokaṃ prāṇināṃ dadat* /
children.translated_text: My right conduct in this world gives light to living beings;

children.text: chinna dṛg jñānaśastreṇa vivekaś cāyudhaṃ mama //
children.translated_text: the false view is cut by the weapon of knowledge; discernment is my armament. //

body.text:
riddhipādaḥ avasthānaṃ śamatho muṣṭisaṃgrahaḥ /
śīlaratho nandighoṣaḥ (

children.translated_text: ) and my charioteer is insight (<s>vipaśyanā</s>). //

body.translated_text:
The bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>) are my foothold; tranquility is the grip;
the chariot of moral conduct — <s>Nandighoṣa</s> is its name — (

children.translated_text: My armor is patience and forbearance; the battle is the cultivation of the path;
the quiver is the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>), by which the hindrances are slain. //
The four right exertions (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), by which the afflictions are destroyed;

children.text: śūrayuddhaṃ mayā dattaṃ dharmabherī mayā hatā /
children.translated_text: a hero's battle has been given by me; the drum of <s>Dharma</s> has been struck by me;
having terrified <s>Māra</s> together with his army, I am anointed for awakening. //
Having slain ignorance with knowledge, and the rise and fall of the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>),
having crossed the head of the battle, I, the <s>Buddha</s>, awaken humanity. //

children.text: trayo loke mahācaurā yair iyaṃ bādhyate prajā /
children.translated_text: Three great thieves exist in the world, by whom humanity is afflicted:

children.text: rāgo dveṣaś ca mohaś ca sarve te nāśitā mayā //
children.translated_text: passion, hatred, and delusion — all of them have been destroyed by me. //
I am an <s>arhat</s>, worthy of offerings, possessing the six superknowledges, risen in power;
a recipient of oblations offered in a good field. //

children.text: ārabhya paramaṃ vīryam āsravā nihatā mayā /
children.translated_text: Having exerted supreme vigor, the outflows have been destroyed by me;
having crossed the great flood, I stand firm among those who are confused. //

children.text: daṃṣṭrābalī yathā siṃha āsādya prāṇino vane /
children.translated_text: As a lion with the strength of his fangs, encountering creatures in the forest,

children.text: samaṃ teṣu praharati bālye madhye mahallake //
children.translated_text: strikes equally among them — young, middle-aged, and old — //
just so the perfectly awakened one in the world, the lion among men, the guide,
proclaims the <s>Dharma</s> equally among the foolish, the middling, and the great-souled. //

children.text: āturasya ca me ha tvaṃ kāṃkṣāṃ vinaya gautama /
children.translated_text: 'I am afflicted — remove my doubt, O <s>Gautama</s>;
for you are the best among those who remove thorns, and among those who perceive the light.' //

children.text: vinaya śāmya te kāṃkṣām adhimucyasva brāhmaṇa /
children.translated_text: 'I shall remove it — be calm; your doubt will be dispelled; have faith, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>!
Rare is the sight of the perfectly awakened ones, the glorious ones. //
He whose appearance in the world is rare and difficult at any time —
I am that one, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — the perfectly awakened one, the unsurpassed king of <s>Dharma</s>.' //
'"I am perfectly awakened" — so you say.' <s>Śaila</s> said to the <s>Tathāgata</s>:

children.text: pravartayasi kevalaṃ cakraṃ yathā gautama bhāṣase //
children.translated_text: 'Do you indeed turn the complete wheel, as you declare, O <s>Gautama</s>? //

children.text: senāpatiḥ ko bhavataḥ śrāvakaḥ śāstur ātmajaḥ /
children.translated_text: Who is your general, the disciple, the Teacher's own son,

children.text: yat tvayā vartitaṃ cakram anuvartayati paṇḍitaḥ //
children.translated_text: the wise one who keeps turning the wheel that was turned by you?' //

children.text: asti me śrāvako brahman sadṛśaḥ prajñayātmajaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I have a disciple, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, equal to me in wisdom, my own son —
known as <s>Upatiṣya</s>, the learned <s>Śāriputra</s>. //
Free from all bonds, tranquil, without outflows,

children.text: yan mayā vartitaṃ cakram anuvartayati paṇḍitaḥ //
children.translated_text: the wise one keeps turning the wheel that was turned by me.' //
the marvel of the perfectly

children.text:
buddha āścaryam aho śrāvakasaṃpadaḥ /
lokeṣv āścaryam utpannam aho ratnatrayaṃ param* //
children.translated_text:
awakened one! Oh, the excellence of the disciples!
A marvel has arisen in the worlds! Oh, the supreme Three Jewels! //

body.translated_text: 'Oh,

children.text: ahaṃ vadāmi bhadraṃ te śrāvakatvam upāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: I tell you — blessings upon you — having become a disciple,
oh, having drunk the nectar of the <s>Dharma</s>, I shall become utterly at peace!' //
With a delighted mind and resolve, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, then deeply moved,
with a mind inclined to detachment, addressed this assembly: //

children.text: idaṃ bhavantaḥ śṛṇuta cakṣuṣmān bhāṣate yathā /
children.translated_text: 'Hear this, good people, as the one with sight declares:
the remover of thorns, the great reciter, roars in the forest like a lion. //

children.text: ya icchanty anugacchantu ye necchanti vrajantu te /
children.translated_text: Those who wish, let them follow; those who do not, let them go;
this very day I shall go forth in the dispensation of the supreme sage. //
When the holy life has been well-practiced, and the path well-cultivated,
the going forth becomes fruitful for one who dwells in heedfulness.' //

children.text: rocate ced iyaṃ tava pravraja jinaśāsane /
children.translated_text: 'If this is pleasing to you, then go forth in the Conqueror's dispensation;
having cut your matted locks here, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, we shall go forth.' //
With a delighted mind and resolve, with palms joined in tenfold homage,
the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Śaila</s> spoke, having arranged his robe over one shoulder: //
'These five hundred young men stand with palms joined;
may we, O sage, obtain the going forth and full ordination!' //
Then the compassionate Teacher, the great sage, the merciful one,

children.text: ehi bhikṣave ity āha sa teṣām upasaṃpadā //
children.translated_text: said 'Come, monks!' — that was their ordination. //

body.text:
śāriputro mahāprajño maudgalyāyana ṛddhimān* /
brāhmaṇa kapphiṇasthaviraḥ

children.translated_text: who had
attained the state of eloquence —

body.translated_text:
<s>Śāriputra</s> the greatly wise, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> the supernaturally powerful,
the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the elder <s>Kapphiṇa</s>,

children.translated_text: those elders, skilled in eloquence, addressed them there. //

body.translated_text: on the bank of the river <s>Sundarikā</s>, in a delightful forest grove,

children.text: tebhyas taṃ dharmam ājñāya kathāṃ tatrānulomikīm* /
children.translated_text: Having understood from them that <s>Dharma</s>, the discourse in accordance with it,
before long, freed from bonds, they were established in the supreme goal. //
They, having attained the gain, happy, at peace in this very life,
they behold with delight the perfectly awakened one, the leader of the world. //

children.text: saddharmaṃ ca dhanaśreṣṭhaṃ śikṣāṃ ca jinavarṇitām* /
children.translated_text: The true <s>Dharma</s>, the supreme wealth, and the training praised by the Conqueror —
they venerate heedfulness, concentration, and the bedding. //
Therefore, one who desires his own welfare, who aspires to greatness,

children.text: buddhaṃ dharmaṃ ca saṃghaṃ ca satkṛtiṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajet* //
children.translated_text: should go with reverence to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s> for refuge. //

body.text: etad dhi śaraṇaṃ loke varṇitaṃ ta

children.translated_text: sees

the truth —
the giver of all happiness to the distressed and the frightened. //

body.translated_text: For this is the refuge in the world, praised by the one who

children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the sun of <s>Ādityas</s>, the supreme glory of the <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>Dharma</s> —
one who seeks liberation should always follow the dispensation of the king of <s>Dharma</s>.' //

body.translated_text: The <s>Kaineya</s> verses are completed. //

body.text: atha bhagavān kāśīṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ caran kāśīpaṭṭam anuprāptaḥ / tasmiṃś ca kāśīpaṭṭe śobhitapūrviṇau dvau pitāputrau pravrajitau / putraḥ kathayati / bhagavān śrāvakasaṃghaḥ kāśīṣu janapade cārikāṃ carann ihānuprāptaḥ śrāntakāyo bhagavān bhikṣusaṃghaś ca / yan nu vayaṃ bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ yavāgūpānenopanimantrayāmaḥ / tat kiṃ tvaṃ peyāṃ samudānayasi āhosvid bhikṣusaṃgham upanimaṃtrayasīti / gaccha tvaṃ bhikṣusaṃgham upanimaṃtraya / ahaṃ peyāṃ samudānayāmīti / tena bhikṣusaṃgha upanimaṃtritaḥ / so 'py ādarśaṃ gṛhītvā vīthīṃ gataḥ / tena tasyāṃ śreṣṭhī dṛṣṭo dīrghakeśaśmaśruḥ / tasya tenādarśa upadarśitaḥ / sa kathayati / ārya etad apy asti te kauśalyam* / sa kathayati / asti / avatāraya / so 'vatārayitum (

children.text: ) ārabdho gṛhapatir middham avakrāntaḥ / avatārite pratibuddhaḥ / sa kathayati / āryāvatāritam* / gṛhapate avatāritam* / saṃtuṣṭaḥ kathayati / ārya atīva parituṣṭo 'smi / vada kaṃ te varam anuprayacchāmīti / sa kathayati / mayā buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃgho yavāgūpānenopanimantritaḥ / yavāgūm anuprayaccheti / sa kathayati / ārya kiṃ te yavāgūpānena / praṇītaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyam anuprayacchāmi / gacchopanimaṃtrayasveti / ārogyam ity uktvāsau prakrāntaḥ / tato 'sau gṛhapatiḥ śuci praṇītaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ pūrvavad yāvat purastād bhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇas tatra praṇītaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ cāryate / bhikṣavaḥ saṃlakṣayanti / vayaṃ lūhenopanimaṃtritāḥ / ayaṃ ca praṇīta āhāraḥ / kathaṃ vayaṃ pratigṛhṇīma iti / te na pratigṛhṇanti / etat prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣavo bhagavata ārocayanti / bhagavān āha / yadi lūhenopanimantritaḥ praṇītaṃ labhate paribhoktavyam* / nātra kaukṛtyaṃ karaṇīyam* /
children.translated_text: ) He began [to trim it]; the householder fell asleep. When the trimming was finished, he woke up. He said: 'Noble one, it has been trimmed.' 'Householder, it has been trimmed.' Pleased, he said: 'Noble one, I am exceedingly pleased. Tell me — what boon shall I grant you?' He replied: 'I have invited the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> for gruel and drink. Please provide the gruel.' He said: 'Noble one, what use is gruel to you? I will provide excellent hard and soft foods. Go and invite them.' Having said 'Good health!' he departed. Then that householder prepared pure and excellent hard and soft foods, as before up to: having sat upon a seat prepared before the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks, excellent hard and soft foods were brought out there. The monks reflected: 'We were invited with something modest, yet this is excellent food. How can we accept it?' They did not accept. The monks reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'If one has been invited with something modest and receives something excellent, it should be consumed. No scruple need be felt about this.'

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, wandering on a journey through the <s>Kāśī</s> territories, arrived at <s>Kāśīpaṭṭa</s>. In that <s>Kāśīpaṭṭa</s>, there were two monks, father and son, formerly of the <s>Śobhita</s> family, who had gone forth. The son said: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks, wandering through the <s>Kāśī</s> territories, has arrived here. The <s>Bhagavān</s> and the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks are weary in body. Let us invite the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> for gruel and drink. Now, will you prepare the gruel, or will you invite the <s>Saṃgha</s>?' 'Go, you invite the <s>Saṃgha</s>. I will prepare the gruel.' He invited the <s>Saṃgha</s>. And the other, having taken a mirror, went out into the street. There he saw a guild-master with long hair and beard. He showed him the mirror. The guild-master said: 'Noble one, you have this skill too?' He replied: 'I do.' 'Trim my hair.' He began to trim it. The householder fell asleep. When the trimming was finished, he woke up. He said: 'Noble one, it has been trimmed.' 'Householder, it has been trimmed.' Pleased, he said: 'Noble one, I am exceedingly pleased. Tell me — what boon shall I grant you?' He replied: 'I have invited the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> for gruel and drink. Please provide the gruel.' He said: 'Noble one, what use is gruel to you? I will provide excellent hard and soft foods. Go and invite them.' Having said 'Good health!' he departed. Then that householder prepared pure and excellent hard and soft foods, as before up to: having sat upon a seat prepared before the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks, excellent hard and soft foods were brought out. The monks reflected: 'We were invited with something modest, yet this is excellent food. How can we accept it?' They did not accept. The monks reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'If one has been invited with something modest and receives something excellent, it should be consumed. No scruple need be felt about this.'

body.text: bhagavān saṃlakṣayati / yaḥ kaścid ādīnavo bhikṣavo jātīyaṃ bhāṇḍaṃ dhārayanti / tasmān na bhikṣuṇā śilpam upadarśayitavyam* / na tāvajjātīyena tāvajjātīyaṃ bhāṇḍam upasthāpayitavyam* / upasthāpayati sātisāro bhavati sthāpayitvā vaidyapūrviṇāṃ śastrakoṣaṃ kāyasthapūrviṇām api bhājanaṃ sūcikapravrajitānāṃ sūcīgṛham iti /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> reflected: 'Whatever disadvantage there is in monks keeping professional implements.' Therefore a monk should not display professional skills. A craftsman-monk should not set up implements of his craft. If he does, he commits a transgression — except for a physician's surgical case, a scribe's container, and a needle-case for those who have gone forth as tailors.

children.translated_text: ) The <s>Bhagavān</s>, wandering on a journey through the <s>Malla</s> territories, arrived at <s>Pāpā</s>. At <s>Pāpā</s>, he dwelt in the <s>Jalūkā</s> grove. In <s>Pāpā</s> there lived a <s>Malla</s> chief named <s>Roca</s>. He was the maternal uncle of the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>. He was exceedingly faithless. The <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Pāpā</s> heard that the <s>Bhagavān</s>, wandering on a journey through the <s>Malla</s> territories, had arrived at <s>Pāpā</s> and was dwelling at <s>Pāpā</s> in the <s>Jalūkā</s> grove. Having heard this, they consulted together: 'Good people, it is heard that the <s>Bhagavān</s>, wandering on a journey through the <s>Malla</s> territories, has arrived at <s>Pāpā</s> and is dwelling at <s>Pāpā</s> in the <s>Jalūkā</s> grove. If each of us individually feeds the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>, others will not get the opportunity. Let us establish a rule in every way: no single individual among us shall feed the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>. We shall all feed him together. Whoever among you feeds him alone shall be fined sixty <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> by the assembly.' Then the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Pāpā</s>, all together, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, they bowed at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> feet with their heads and sat down to one side. To the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Pāpā</s> seated to one side, the <s>Bhagavān</s> instructed—as before up to—gladdened them, then fell silent. Then the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Pāpā</s>, rising from their seats, arranging their upper robes over one shoulder, joined their palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> consent to accept a meal tomorrow in our assembly hall, together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> accepted the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Pāpā's</s> invitation through silence. Then the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Pāpā</s>, having understood the <s>Bhagavān's</s> acceptance through silence, rejoiced and approved of the <s>Bhagavān's</s> words, bowed at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> feet with their heads, rose from their seats, and departed. <s>Roca</s> the <s>Malla</s> chief remained there. children.translated_text: ) He was addressed by the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: '<s>Roca</s>, have you become faithful?' He replied: 'I have not become faithful. But the assembly has established a rule.' As before, up to: 'Whoever feeds him alone shall be fined sixty <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>.' 'So you have come to see the <s>Bhagavān</s> only out of fear of punishment?' 'Yes, Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>.' Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, bringing <s>Roca</s> the <s>Malla</s> chief with him, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Venerable Sir, this <s>Roca</s> the <s>Malla</s> chief has no faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, no faith in the <s>Dharma</s>, no faith in the <s>Saṃgha</s>. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> teach him the <s>Dharma</s> in such a way that he would develop faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s>.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave <s>Roca</s> the chief such a teaching on the <s>Dharma</s> that, upon hearing it, <s>Roca</s> the <s>Malla</s> chief developed faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s>. Then <s>Roca</s> the <s>Malla</s> chief, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, joined his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> consent to accept a meal tomorrow in my residence, together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks.' children.translated_text: ) it will not be difficult to feed the <s>Bhagavān</s> and the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks.' They replied: 'We invited the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> first. We do not consent.' He said: 'If you do not consent, then let me at least distribute a food-preparation and a drink.' Among them, those who were faithful said: 'Good people, this man is faithless. Let us consent. If the merit is established as going to the <s>Saṃgha</s>, it will be well-established.' They gave their consent. Then he summoned the confectioners and said: 'Good people, prepare such a food-preparation that a single one satisfies a person. I will provide all the ingredients.' He provided ingredients combined with various fragrant substances. They prepared a food-preparation filled with various fragrances, such that a single one satisfied one person. Then the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Pāpā</s>, that very night, prepared pure and choice hard and soft foods—as before up to—sat upon a seat prepared before the assembly of monks. Then <s>Roca</s> the <s>Malla</s> chief began to distribute the food-preparation and the drink. The monks, out of scruple, would not consume it. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'One should look to the donor.' The monks looked toward the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Pāpā</s>. They said: 'Noble ones, we have been noticed by <s>Roca</s> the <s>Malla</s> chief. Accept it.' Then <s>Roca</s> the <s>Malla</s> chief distributed the food-preparation. That single preparation satisfied the monks. The <s>Bhagavān</s> made the dedication of merit and departed. The food of the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Pāpā</s> went unconsumed.

children.translated_text: ) The monks, out of scruple, would accept it. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'One should ask: "Do you give to me, or to the one who is the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the supreme among bipeds?" If they reply: "To the one who is the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the supreme among bipeds," it should not be accepted. But if they say: "You are our <s>Buddha</s>," one should accept it. No scruple need be felt about this. Likewise regarding the <s>Dharma</s>, one should say: "The one that is the supreme among things free from passion." Regarding the <s>Saṃgha</s>, one should say: "The one that is the supreme among assemblies." The formula should be applied in detail.'

children.translated_text: ) all of them become sharers of the merit. Let me therefore do the preparation work.' He began to split firewood. From a certain hollow in a piece of rotten wood, a poisonous snake emerged and bit him on the big toe of his right foot. Overcome by the poison, he fell to the ground, drooling, his face contorted, his eyes rolling. He was seen in that distressed state by the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders. They said: 'Good people, whose son is this householder's?' Others informed them: 'Such-and-such a person's.' They said: 'He has gone forth among the helpless followers of the <s>Śramaṇa Śākyaputra</s>. If he had not gone forth, his relatives would have had treatment arranged for him.' The monks reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s> (

children.text: ) ārocayanti / bhagavān āha / vaidyaṃ pṛṣṭvā cikitsā kartavyeti / bhikṣubhir vaidyaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ / sa kathayati / āryā vikṛtabhojanam anuprayacchateti / etat prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣavo bhagavata ārocayanti / bhagavān āha / dātavyaṃ vaidyopadeśeneti / bhikṣavo na jānate kīdṛśaṃ vikṛtabhojanam iti / tair vaidyaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ / sa kathayati / āryā yuṣmākam eva śāstā sarvajño bhagavān sarvadarśī sa eva jñāsyatīti / bhikṣavo bhagavata ārocayanti / bhagavān āha / vikṛtabhojanaṃ bhikṣava uccāraḥ prasrāvaś chāyikā mṛttikā ca / tatra uccāraḥ acirajātakānāṃ vatsakānāṃ teṣām eva ca prasrāvaḥ / chāyikā paṃcānāṃ vṛkṣāṇām* / kāṃcanaya kamībalasyāśvatthasyodumbarasya nyagrodhasya / mṛttikā pṛthivyāṃ caturaṃgulam apanīyoddhartavyā iti vikṛtabhojanam iti /
children.translated_text: ). The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Having consulted a physician, treatment should be administered.' The monks consulted a physician. He said: 'Noble ones, give him repulsive food (<s>vikṛtabhojana</s>) as medicine.' The monks reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'It should be given as the physician prescribes.' The monks did not know what constitutes repulsive food. They asked the physician. He replied: 'Noble ones, your own Teacher is omniscient, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the All-Seeing One. He himself will know.' The monks reported to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Repulsive food, monks, consists of feces, urine, ashes, and earth. The feces are from newly born calves; the urine also from those very calves. The ashes are from five kinds of trees: <s>kāṃcanaya</s>, <s>kamībala</s>, <s>aśvattha</s> (sacred fig), <s>udumbara</s> (cluster fig), and <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan). The earth is to be obtained by removing four finger-breadths from the surface of the ground. This constitutes repulsive food.'

children.text: brahmasvare pūrṇe pūrṇamanorathe mukte jīvati rakṣā svātiṃ sarvopadravabhayarogebhyaḥ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmasvare Pūrṇe Pūrṇamanorathe Mukte Jīvati</s>—protection for <s>Svāti</s> from all calamities, dangers, and diseases. <s>Svāhā</s>.

body.translated_text: <s>Tadyathā: Amale Vimale Nirmale</s>,

body.text: evaṃ bhadantety āyuṣmān ānando bhagavato 'ntikān mahāmāyūrīṃ vidyām udgṛhya paryavāpya svāter bhikṣoḥ svastyayanaṃ kṛtam* / nirviṣaś ca saṃvṛtto yathā paurāṇaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Yes, Venerable Sir,' the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having learned and mastered the <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyā</s> from the <s>Bhagavān</s>, performed the blessing for the monk <s>Svāti</s>. He became free from poison and was restored to his former state.

body.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ / āscaryaṃ bhagavan yāvac ca bhagavatā mahāmāyūrī vidyā upakarā bahukarā ca / na bhikṣava etarhi yathā mamātīte 'py adhvany akṣaṇapratipannasya (

children.text: ) vinipatitaśarīrasyāpi mahāmāyūrī vidyārājā upakarā bahukarā ca / tac chrūyatām* /
children.translated_text: ) with a body destined for ruin, the <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājā</s> (Great Peacock Spell-King) was beneficial and very helpful. Listen to this:'

body.translated_text: The monks, having doubts, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, who resolves all doubts: 'It is wonderful, <s>Bhagavān</s>, how beneficial and very helpful is the <s>Mahāmāyūrī Vidyā</s> spoken by the <s>Bhagavān</s>!' 'Monks, not only now—in the past too, even for one born at an inauspicious time, (

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo himavati parvatarāje dakṣiṇe pārśve suvarṇāvabhāso nāma mayūrarājaḥ prativasati sma / so 'nayā mahāmāyūryā vidyayā kālyaṃ svastyayanaṃ kṛtvā divā svastyayanena viharati / so 'yaṃ svastyayanaṃ kṛtvā rātrau svastyayanena viharati / so 'pareṇa samayena saṃbahulābhir vanamayūrībhiḥ sārdham ārāmeṇārāmam udyānenodyānaṃ parvatapārśveṇa parvatapārśvam atyarthaṃ kāmarāgaraktaḥ kāme 'nugṛddho grathito mūrchito madamattaḥ pramūḍhaḥ pramūrchitaḥ (

children.translated_text: MSV I 288

children.text: ) pravicaran prasādād anyataraṃ parvatavivaram anupraviṣṭaḥ / sa tatra dīrgharātraṃ pratyarthikaiḥ pratyamitrair hiṃsakair avatāraprekṣibhir mayūrapāśair baddhaḥ / so 'py atra madhyagataḥ pramūḍhaḥ smṛtiṃ ca labdhvā imām eva mahāmāyūrīṃ vidyāṃ manasyakārṣīt* / tadyathā amale vimale nirmale maṅgalye hiraṇye hiraṇyagarbhe bhadre subhadre samantabhadre śrībhadre sarvārthasādhani paramārthasādhani sarvānarthapraśamani sarvamaṅgalyasādhani manasi mānasi mahāmānasi acyute adbhute atyadbhute mukte mocani mokṣaṇi araje viraje amare amṛte
children.translated_text: he carelessly entered a certain mountain cave. There, for a long time, he was caught in peacock-snares set by hostile enemies seeking an opportunity to harm him. But even in this predicament, though bewildered, he recovered his mindfulness and recollected this very great <s>Mahāmāyūrī</s> <s>vidyā</s>: <s>tadyathā amale vimale nirmale maṅgalye hiraṇye hiraṇyagarbhe bhadre subhadre samantabhadre śrībhadre sarvārthasādhani paramārthasādhani sarvānarthapraśamani sarvamaṅgalyasādhani manasi mānasi mahāmānasi acyute adbhute atyadbhute mukte mocani mokṣaṇi araje viraje amare amṛte</s>
<s>amaraṇi</s>

children.text: brahme brahmasvare pūrṇe pūrṇamanorathe vimukte jīvati rakṣa māṃ sarvopadravebhyaḥ svāhā /
children.translated_text: <s>brahme brahmasvare pūrṇe pūrṇamanorathe vimukte jīvati rakṣa māṃ sarvopadravebhyaḥ svāhā</s>.

body.translated_text: In a former time, monks, on the southern slope of the <s>Himavat</s>, king of mountains, there dwelt a peacock-king named <s>Suvarṇāvabhāsa</s> (Golden Radiance). He, by means of this great <s>Mahāmāyūrī</s> <s>vidyā</s> (incantation), would perform a blessing in the morning and dwell during the day under that blessing. He would perform a blessing in the evening and dwell during the night under that blessing. At a later time, roaming with many wild peahens from pleasure grove to pleasure grove, from garden to garden, from mountainside to mountainside, exceedingly impassioned with desire, craving sensual pleasures, entangled, infatuated, intoxicated with pride, deluded, and stupefied,

body.text: sa mayūrapāśāṃś chitvā niṣpalānaḥ / kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau suvarṇāvabhāso nāma mayūrarājas tena kālena tena samayena / tadāpi mama mahāmāyūrī vidyā upakarā ca bahukarā ca etarhy api mama mahāmāyūrī vidyā upakarā ca bahukarā ceti / paśya bhadanta yāvac ca bhagavataḥ svāter bhikṣor vidyayā svastyayanaṃ kṛtam* / na bhikṣava etarhi yathātīte 'py adhvani / tac chrūyatām* /
body.translated_text: He cut through the peacock-snares and escaped. What do you think, monks? That peacock-king named <s>Suvarṇāvabhāsa</s> at that time and on that occasion — that was I. Even then, the great <s>Mahāmāyūrī</s> <s>vidyā</s> was of benefit and of great benefit to me; even now, the great <s>Mahāmāyūrī</s> <s>vidyā</s> is of benefit and of great benefit to me.' 'Observe, Venerable Sir, how the <s>Bhagavān</s> has performed a blessing for the monk <s>Svāti</s> by means of the <s>vidyā</s>.' 'It is not only now, monks, that I have done so, but also in the past. Listen to this:'

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ nāgamaṇḍaliko 'nyatamaḥ kṣatriyadārakaḥ sarpeṇa dṛṣṭaḥ / sa kālagataḥ / nāgamaṇḍalikena vidyayā tasya svāsthyaṃ kṛtam* / kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau nāgamaṇḍalikaḥ ahaṃ sa tena kālena tena samayena / yo 'sau dārakaḥ svātir bhikṣus tena kālena tena samayena /
body.translated_text: In a former time, monks, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a certain <s>Kṣatriya</s> boy, who was a snake-charmer, was bitten by a snake. He died. The snake-charmer restored him to health by means of a <s>vidyā</s>. What do you think, monks? That snake-charmer was I at that time and on that occasion. That boy was the monk <s>Svāti</s> at that time and on that occasion.
End of the <s>Bhaiṣajyavastu</s> (Chapter on Medicine). //
